6. it appears in the gallery (`gallery/variants.js`) and renders there without console messages.

A component that does not meet them yet is listed as **not yet verified** in the release record. The mechanism (commands, what is stored where, the integrity loop) is in `TESTING.md` at the library root; these are the rules for a component.

- **Codes.** Every Business analysis line ends with a hidden, permanent code: ` <!-- BA-07 -->`. A new line takes the next free number; codes are never reused, renumbered or removed while published (`tests/published.json`).
- **Test plan.** `xTESTS.md` has one table `ID | Covers | Kind | Steps | Expected result`. Covers names codes, callbacks and error labels; every one of them is covered by at least one case, except the labels the shared contract test proves for every component. Kind is `auto` (code in `tests/components/x.test.mjs`, same ID) or `manual` (only what a script cannot judge: the look in the gallery, other applications, screen readers).
- **Test code.** It acts as a user (real clicks and keys through Playwright) and reads only the page, the clipboard and the instance members, never the component's internal files.
- **Gallery.** The component's key variants are listed in `gallery/variants.js`: its main variants, each enum option that changes the look, and a disabled or error state when there is one. The gallery is where people look at the library's real look (`npm run gallery`, with light, dark and right-to-left switches).
- **Same change.** A change of behaviour updates the README line, the test plan, the test code and, when the look changes, the gallery variants together.
- **Bugs.** First a case that fails because of the bug, then the fix; the case stays.
- **Shared contract.** A new component adds its smallest valid configuration to `tests/contract/cases.js`.
- **Before finishing:** `npm run check`, `npm test` and the component's tests pass. A release is recorded only with `npm run release -- <version>`, on explicit request.

## 15. README

`xREADME.md` is the usage contract. It serves four audiences in this fixed order, and each audience finds what it needs in its own layer.

| Layer | Heading | Subsections (in order) | Content |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Business | `## For business` | `### Overview`, `### When to use`, `### Key features`, `### Dependencies`, `### Not included` | Plain language, with no parameter names, code or classes. Overview: one or two sentences — what it is and typical uses (its first sentence is the component's summary in catalogs). When to use: when to choose it and which component to choose instead in similar cases. Key features: three to seven capabilities specific to the component, most important first, one short sentence each, no shared behaviour (§11.1). Dependencies table: dependency, needed when, purpose. Not included: what the application provides. |
| Designers | `## For designers` | `### Structure`, `### Visual options`, `### States`, `### Styling contract` | Generated HTML hierarchy as a class tree (`text` block), conditional parts and state attributes. Visual options: what the Consumer chooses. States: what the component shows at run time. Styling contract: the tokens of each stylesheet part (see below). |
| AI-assisted development | `## For AI-assisted development` | `### Instructions`, `### Safety`, `### Example prompts` | Direct instructions, general then component-specific (see below). Safety: prohibited actions. Two or three realistic prompts. |
| Developers | `## For developers` | `### Business analysis`, `### Contracts`, `### Public API`, `### Configuration`, `### Callbacks`, `### Errors`, `### Accessibility`, `### Examples`, `### Files` | Business analysis: the complete behaviour as statements (§15.1). Contracts: the shared contracts line (see below). Then the complete technical contract. Examples show only non-trivial usage (at least one). Accessibility lists only what the component adds to §11.1. |

Omit subsections that have no content, except States ("No states of its own.") and Contracts, which every README has.

**General AI instructions** (each README states them, adapted to the component):
- read the README first and import only from `xIndex.js`;
- check the configuration before adding code, and configure instead of reproducing markup, styles, validation, errors or events;
- keep business logic in the consumer, and don't modify the component for application needs (propose reusable framework changes instead);
- respect conditional options, user/programmatic differences and callback semantics;
- use unique ids (rules in §5, "Ids"), and call `destroy()` before rendering into the same container again.

**Safety** covers inserting untrusted HTML, removing accessibility attributes, bypassing native semantics and breaking invariants.

**Configuration table** columns: `Parameter`, `Type`, `Default`, `Allowed values / format`, `Applies when`, `Usage / description`. Nested paths are written in full (`validation.maxLength`). Ignored options, precedence, conflicts and fallbacks are stated once, below the table.

**Applies when** uses a fixed form, so tools (and the showcase's Variants panel) can evaluate it: `Always`, or terms joined by ` + `, which must all hold. A term is one or more code tokens separated by commas, of which at least one must hold, optionally preceded by `not`; `, not` also starts a new term (`` `CUSTOM`, not `WEEK` ``). A token is an option path (`` `label` ``: true for a boolean, set for any other option), a path with a value (`` `stateText:NONE` ``), or an allowed value in capitals that belongs to one option only (`` `PASSWORD` ``). Nothing else goes in the cell: a requirement ("required with …"), a screen size or a condition on the data goes in `Usage / description`, and the cell says `Always` when no option decides it. `npm run check` reports any other text.

**Callbacks table** columns: `Callback`, `Arguments`, `Fires when`, `Does not fire when`.

**Errors:** a user error table (`Label`, default message, trigger, visibility, clearing) and a developer table (`Label`, `Severity`, `Cause`). Developer console messages are not repeated.

**Visual options and States tables** have the same columns: `Option` (or `State`), `Values`, `CSS class or attribute`. An option is chosen by the Consumer in the configuration (look, size, label position, what is shown). A state is what the component shows at run time because of the user, the data or the App (open, current, selected, checked, unavailable, invalid, busy, loading, empty); disabled is a state even when it is configured.

**Styling contract** (there is no separate token table) starts with the standard paragraph (the component's file name and class prefix replace `x.css` and `ui-x-`):

```md
`x.css` has three parts, marked in the stylesheet. Restyle by writing the same selector with a new value in your own stylesheet, inside `@layer overrides` (preferred: library updates keep your changes), or by changing a value in your copy of the stylesheet. After each token come the parts it styles, named by their class without `ui-x-` (as in Structure), with the option or state in brackets (joined by “+” when they apply together). Text uses the typography roles of `design-system.css`; border sides are physical (top, right, bottom, left).
```

The border sentence is left out when the Appearance part uses logical border sides. Component-specific notes follow in one paragraph (e.g. which rules also apply inside a disabled `fieldset`). Then, in this order and only when not empty:

- `**1. Appearance — change freely**`, `**2. Dimensions — change with care**`, `**3. Structure — don't change**`, each followed by its tokens grouped under `- Colours`, `- Typography`, `- Borders and corners`, `- Shadows`, `- States and motion`, `- Spacing`, `- Sizes`, `- Layers` (a part without tokens: `- No tokens.`). One line per token: `` - `--token`: part, part (option or state) ``; a part styled always and also in some options or states is written `part (also option, state)`. A token used in two parts is listed in both, each time with what it styles there. Local variables declared in the stylesheet are listed like tokens, marked "(defined in this stylesheet)".
- `**Set by the component — don't change**`: the `--ui-x-…` variables the JavaScript writes, with what they carry and where it comes from (an option, or "measured").
- `**Used by the code**`: design tokens named in the component's JavaScript (defaults passed to child components, values read or written), with their purpose.

Every token referenced in the stylesheet appears in the Styling contract, and nothing else; tokens written only in error messages are not listed.

**Contracts** (first subsection after Business analysis) is one line, always in this form and order:

```md
**Contracts:** Styling: three parts (Styling contract) · Form field: yes · Actions: no · Shared behaviour: yes, additions under Accessibility
```

- **Styling** (§12): always "three parts (Styling contract)".
- **Form field** (§10.1): "yes", "yes, when …" (only in some modes), "coordinates the fields" (Form), "no (container: `getChildren()`)" for containers, or "no".
- **Actions** (§10.2): "yes (`actions`, `onAction`)" with any extra members (`canAct`) or prefixed names (`selectionActions`), "through each panel" when items carry them, or "no".
- **Shared behaviour** (§11.1): "yes, additions under Accessibility"; a documented deviation is named here ("yes, except …").

**Writing rules:**
- **No repetition:** state each fact once, in the layer that needs it most, and use tables for enumerable facts.
- **No filler:** no marketing language, no prose restating tables, no trivial examples.
- **Headings:** `#` for the component name, `##` for layers, `###` for subsections, `####` only if unavoidable; no numbering.
- **Code blocks:** fences always name their language.

**Markdown format:**
- **Table syntax:** GitHub-Flavored Markdown pipe tables only. Every header, separator and row is on one physical line, starts and ends with `|`, and uses `| --- |` separators (`| ---: |` for numbers). Escape a literal pipe in a cell as `\|`. Never use Pandoc simple, grid or multiline tables.
- **Line wrapping:** use one physical line per paragraph and per list item, with no fixed-width wrapping. Multiline content appears only in fenced code blocks.
- **Verification:** inspect the Markdown source, not only the rendering: check literal pipe syntax and consistent column counts.

### 15.1 Business analysis

The behaviour of the component as short statements, for analysts, testers, developers and AI assistants. It describes **what happens**; the Configuration and Callbacks tables describe **how to set it up**, so statements name no options, parameters or classes.

- **Roles.** Each statement starts with one role: **User** (the person using the screen), **Component** (the component itself), **Consumer** (the developer who configures the component in the application's code) or **App** (the running application that uses the component; it provides the data, performs the actions and stores the changes). "App" is used everywhere, never "System".
- **Role definitions.** Directly under the heading, a block quote defines the roles other than User, with this text (the component's name replaces `{Name}`): `> **Component**: the {Name} itself. **Consumer**: the developer who configures the {Name} in the application's code. **App**: the running application that uses the {Name}; it provides the data, performs the actions and stores the changes.`
- **Verbs.** After the role comes one verb in the present tense, from this list only (one verb per meaning, no synonyms, never "can", "should" or "shall"):

| Role | Verbs |
| --- | --- |
| User | clicks (also taps), presses (a key), types, pastes, selects (an option, a date, a value), changes (a value), drags (and drops), hovers, leaves (a field) |
| Component | displays, hides, opens, closes, selects, clears, ticks (and unticks), marks, adds, removes, moves, sorts, changes, adapts, wraps, shortens, scrolls, keeps, checks, prevents, disables, asks, requests, reports, sends, submits, resets, applies, announces (spoken at once), exposes (available to screen readers without being announced) |
| App | provides, performs, stores, sends, opens, adds, changes, marks, disables, forbids, decides |
| Consumer | chooses, provides, enables, disables, adds |

- **One fact per statement**, a complete sentence ending with a full stop. User-visible texts appear in quotes ("No matching items").
- **Dependent statements** are indented under the statement they follow from (`  - ` per level), e.g. what the Component does after a User action.
- **Codes.** Each statement ends with its hidden test code (` <!-- BA-07 -->`, §14); renderers do not show it.
- **Groups.** Statements are grouped by function under a bold line (`**Search**`); a group or statement enabled by the Consumer ends with "(optional)", and "(optional, on by default)" when it starts enabled.
- **No shared behaviour.** Keyboard, screen-reader, translation, right-to-left and validation-timing behaviour from §11.1 is not repeated; component-specific additions are stated in their group.

## 16. Designing a new component

Settle these points before writing code, and ask when a point has several reasonable answers.

1. **Boundary:** the reusable problem, and what is excluded (the consumer's part).
2. **Existing components:** which existing framework components already cover part of the behavior. Compose them.
3. **User view:** what the user sees and does, including accepted, rejected and automatically corrected actions.
4. **Configuration:** options, defaults, enums, conditions, conflicts, precedence and texts.
5. **Native capabilities:** which are reused, and why any are replaced.
6. **Programmatic behavior:** initial values and runtime methods, including how invariants apply.
7. **State:** the minimum runtime state and where the truth lives (native element or state).
8. **Validation:** generic rules and when each one runs.
9. **Errors:** user errors (trigger, visibility, clearing) and developer errors and warnings, with labels.
10. **Callbacks:** outcome, arguments, firing and non-firing cases.
11. **Accessibility:** semantics, names, relationships and state attributes.
12. **Presentation:** structure, classes, verified tokens and spacing ownership.
13. **Dependencies:** framework components, design system and external libraries, and who owns each child's lifecycle.
14. **Shared behaviour:** how the component meets §11.1 (keyboard, screen readers, texts, right-to-left, reduced motion, container widths; for inputs, the form-field behaviour), and which additions it brings.
15. **Buttons:** which buttons are owned (named options, `texts`) and which are application actions (`actions` + `onAction`, §10.2).

Build order: implementation files, then the gallery variants and manual verification of configurations and interactions in the gallery, then the README (written last, from the stabilized behavior), then the test plan with its test code (§14).

## 17. Changing an existing component

1. Read the current files, the README and the public contracts of the component's dependencies.
2. Find inconsistencies among configuration, markup, events, state, validation, errors, CSS, README, test plan and test code.
3. Define the target behavior before coding, keeping user interaction, programmatic interaction, validation, temporary feedback and callbacks separate.
4. Decide where the capability belongs: this component, a child component, a new component or the consumer.
5. Update every affected surface coherently: implementation, `xIndex.js` header, README, test plan, test code and gallery variants.
6. Avoid unrelated refactoring.

## 18. Delivery

- **Isolated change** (one or two exact spots): give precise location guidance (file, section or line, the text to find, the replacement).
- **Larger change:** deliver the complete file.
- **Changelog:** list breaking changes separately from fixes and improvements, with the consumer action required.
- **Scope:** don't change unrelated files or agreed behavior silently. Changes to other components (e.g. references in comments) are reported, not made silently.
- **Before delivery, verify** (`npm run check` covers the items marked ✓; `npm test` and `npm run test:components` cover the behaviour):
  - ✓ every referenced token exists in `design-system.css`;
  - ✓ every reported label exists in its catalog, no catalog entry is unused, and the README Errors section lists the same labels with the same severity;
  - ✓ every Business analysis line has its code, and every code, callback and label is covered by the test plan (when the component has one);
  - ✓ no `console.warn` or `console.error` calls exist outside `xErrors.js`;
  - there are no class names or selectors without the `ui-` prefix, and no stale names from renames;
  - no internal helper is exported from `xIndex.js`;
  - application buttons follow §10.2 (`actions`, `onAction`, `setActionDisabled`, the action errors, `--gap-inline-items`), with no pass-through Button configurations;
  - the component renders in the gallery without page errors or console messages;
  - the completion rule of §14 holds, or the component is reported as not yet verified;
  - ✓ README tables pass the Markdown format rules;
  - the README has Overview, When to use and Key features (§15), Business analysis (§15.1) with the role definitions and only listed verbs, and repeats nothing from the shared behaviour (§11.1);
  - the stylesheet has the three parts (§12), and the README's Styling contract lists every token of each part, the variables set by the component and the tokens used by the code, and nothing else (§15);
  - Visual options hold only what the Consumer chooses, and States what the component shows at run time (§15);
  - the Contracts line matches the code: form-field members (§10.1), actions (§10.2), the three CSS parts (§12) and the shared behaviour (§11.1);
  - the component provides the shared behaviour of §11.1.


<!-- ===== source/components-js/accordion/accordionREADME.md ===== -->

# Accordion

## For business

### Overview

Accordion stacks several sections of which only the titles are visible; the user opens a section to read or edit its content, such as frequently asked questions, the parts of a settings page or the steps of a long form.

### When to use

- Use it for several sections of which the user reads or edits one or a few at a time: frequently asked questions, parts of a settings page, steps of a long form.
- Use a single CollapsiblePanel for one section that opens and closes on its own.
- Use ContentGroup when all sections stay visible.

### Key features

- One section open at a time (default), or sections that open and close independently.
- Two looks: one frame with lines between the sections, or one card per section.
- Each section with the possibilities of a CollapsiblePanel: icon, description, labels, buttons, status colour, summary while closed.
- Section titles as headings that screen-reader users jump between.
- Fields inside the sections take part in the surrounding form, also while their section is closed.

### Dependencies

| Dependency | Needed when | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Design system (`design-system.css`) | Always | Colours, lines, corners and spacing. |
| Accordion styles (`accordion.css`) | Always | Frame, dividers and space between sections. |
| CollapsiblePanel component and `collapsiblePanel.css` | Always | Each section is a CollapsiblePanel. |
| Chip and Button components and their styles | A section has labels or buttons in its header | Through CollapsiblePanel. |
| Font Awesome icon library | Sections have icons | Icon glyphs. Loaded by the application page. |
| Tooltip component and `tooltip.css` | `tooltipMode` `TOOLTIP` | Tooltips (the Tooltip module is loaded only then). |

### Not included

The application provides the sections and their content, loads content from a server if needed, and decides which section opens first. Saving which sections were open between visits, drag-and-drop reordering and nested accordions with their own behaviour belong to the application.

## For designers

### Structure

```text
div#{id}.ui-accordion.ui-accordion-{joined|separate}[.ui-accordion-bordered][.ui-accordion-square]  data-expand-mode="SINGLE|MULTIPLE"
└── div.ui-accordion-item  data-index="{n}"   (one per item)
    └── CollapsiblePanel: section.ui-collapsible-panel[.ui-collapsible-panel-plain]   (JOINED: variant PLAIN)
        ├── div.ui-collapsible-panel-header > h{2–6}.ui-collapsible-panel-heading-level > button.ui-collapsible-panel-toggle
        ├── div.ui-collapsible-panel-summary
        └── div.ui-collapsible-panel-content  (role="region")
```

JOINED: the Accordion draws the frame (surface, corners, shadow, optional border) and a line between items; every panel is variant `PLAIN` (no frame of its own). SEPARATE: every panel is a card (its own `variant`, default `DEFAULT`) with `bordered` and `cornerRadius` from the Accordion; the Accordion only sets the gap. The panels keep their own look in both: the Accordion never styles the inside of a panel.

### Visual options

| Option | Values | CSS class or attribute |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Look | Joined, separate | `ui-accordion-joined`, `ui-accordion-separate` |
| Bordered | Yes, no | `ui-accordion-bordered` (JOINED); SEPARATE: the panel's `ui-collapsible-panel-bordered` |
| Corners | Rounded, none | — , `ui-accordion-square` (JOINED); SEPARATE: the panel's `ui-collapsible-panel-square` |

### States

No states of its own.

### Styling contract

`accordion.css` has three parts, marked in the stylesheet. Restyle by writing the same selector with a new value in your own stylesheet, inside `@layer overrides` (preferred: library updates keep your changes), or by changing a value in your copy of the stylesheet. After each token come the parts it styles, named by their class without `ui-accordion-` (as in Structure), with the option or state in brackets (joined by “+” when they apply together). Text uses the typography roles of `design-system.css`; border sides are physical (top, right, bottom, left).

**1. Appearance — change freely** (colours, type, borders, corners, motion: only the look changes)

- Colours
  - `--c-surface`: accordion (joined)
  - `--c-border`: accordion (joined + bordered), item (joined)
- Borders and corners
  - `--radius-panel`: accordion (joined)
  - `--border-thin`: accordion (joined + bordered), item (joined)
- Shadows
  - `--shadow-sm`: accordion (joined)

**2. Dimensions — change with care** (sizes and spacing: the component keeps working, its size changes)

- Spacing
  - `--gap-toolbar`: accordion (separate)

**3. Structure — don't change** (layout, behaviour, states, accessibility)

- No tokens.

## For AI-assisted development

### Instructions

- Read this README and the CollapsiblePanel README before writing code. Import only from `accordionIndex.js`.
- Each item is a CollapsiblePanel configuration (`id`, `title`, `description`, `icon`, `chips`, `actions` + `onAction` (header buttons, guidelines §10.2), `status`, `state`, `disabled`, `lazyContent`, `summaryRenderer`, …) plus `content`, the panel's children. Configure the item instead of writing panel markup.
- Set `headingLevel` to fit the page outline (e.g. `3` under an `h2`); it applies to every item.
- Use `expandMode:'MULTIPLE'` when users compare sections or work in several at once; keep `SINGLE` for FAQs and step-by-step content.
- Use `onChange(openIds)` to react to the user (e.g. load content, remember open sections); `expand()`, `collapse()`, `expandAll()` and `collapseAll()` never call it.
- Put fields inside items through render functions; a surrounding Form finds them through `getChildren()`. With `lazyContent`, fields exist only after their section was first opened.
- Keep business logic (what the sections contain, which one opens) in the consuming code; don't modify the component for application needs.
- Give the Accordion and every item a unique `id`, and call `destroy()` before rendering into the same container again.

### Safety

- String `content` and `summaryRenderer` output are inserted as HTML: escape user-provided or external data first.
- Never remove the headings, `aria-expanded` or `aria-controls`, and never replace the header buttons with clickable non-buttons.
- Don't style the inside of the panels from the Accordion's container; restyle CollapsiblePanel or use `@layer overrides`.

### Example prompts

```text
Add an FAQ Accordion under the "Help" heading (h2) with four questions; only one answer open at a time, the first one open.
```

```text
Split the long settings page into an Accordion in MULTIPLE mode with the sections Account, Notifications and Privacy, each holding its fields, inside the existing Form, so Save validates all fields, also in closed sections.
```

## For developers

### Business analysis

> **Component**: the Accordion itself. **Consumer**: the developer who configures the Accordion in the application's code. **App**: the running application that uses the Accordion; it provides the data, performs the actions and stores the changes.

**Sections**

- App provides the sections and their content. <!-- BA-01 -->
- User clicks the title of a section. <!-- BA-02 -->
  - Component opens or closes the section. <!-- BA-03 -->
  - Component closes the open section first (one-at-a-time mode, on by default). <!-- BA-04 -->
  - Component reports the open sections to the App. <!-- BA-05 -->
- Consumer chooses sections that open and close independently (optional). <!-- BA-06 -->
- Consumer chooses which sections start open. <!-- BA-07 -->

**Look**

- Consumer chooses one frame with a line between the sections, or one card per section with space between them. <!-- BA-08 -->
- Consumer chooses a border and rounded or square corners. <!-- BA-09 -->
- Consumer provides for each section an icon, a short description, labels, buttons, a status colour and a summary while closed (optional). <!-- BA-10 -->

**Keyboard additions**

- User presses the up or down arrow, Home or End on a title to move between the titles. <!-- BA-11 -->

**Screen readers**

- Component exposes each title as a heading, at a level chosen by the Consumer, with the open or closed state. <!-- BA-12 -->

**Forms**

- Component adds the fields of all sections to a surrounding form, also while their section is closed. <!-- BA-13 -->
  - Component adds fields that load on first opening once their section is opened. <!-- BA-14 -->

**Tooltips**

- Consumer chooses how the panels' icon-only actions show their names on hover and keyboard focus: the browser's tooltip, a Tooltip or none (optional). <!-- BA-15 -->

### Contracts

**Contracts:** Styling: three parts (Styling contract) · Form field: no (container: `getChildren()`) · Actions: through each panel (an item's `actions`) · Shared behaviour: yes, additions under Accessibility

### Public API

```js
import { renderAccordion, DEFAULT_ACCORDION_CONFIG, ACCORDION_TOOLTIP_MODES, ACCORDION_EXPAND_MODES, ACCORDION_LOOKS, ACCORDION_CORNER_RADII } from './accordionIndex.js';

const accordion = renderAccordion(container, config); // null after a developer error
```

`container` is a dedicated, consumer-owned element. Rendering replaces its content; `destroy()` clears it. Accordion renders each item with `renderCollapsiblePanel()` into its own item host.

| Member | Returns | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | The configured id. |
| `getOpenIds()` | array | Ids of the open items, in display order (a non-collapsible item is always open). |
| `expand(id)` | boolean | Opens an item; SINGLE closes the open one. `false` when the id is unknown (`UNKNOWN_ITEM`), the item is not collapsible or already open. Works on disabled items. |
| `collapse(id)` | boolean | Closes an item; `false` when unknown, not collapsible or already closed. |
| `expandAll()` | boolean | MULTIPLE: opens every item; returns whether any changed. SINGLE: `false` and `OPTION_IGNORED`. |
| `collapseAll()` | boolean | Closes every collapsible item; returns whether any changed. |
| `getPanel(id)` | object \| null | The item's CollapsiblePanel instance (e.g. for `setStatus()` or `refreshSummary()`). |
| `getChildren()` | array | The CollapsiblePanel instances in display order; a Form finds fields through their own `getChildren()`. |
| `focus()` | boolean | Moves focus to the first header that can take it. |
| `destroy()` | — | Removes the keyboard listener and the panels (and their content), clears the container. |

### Configuration

| Parameter | Type | Default | Allowed values / format | Applies when | Usage / description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | — | Starts with a letter; letters, digits, `_ : . -`; unique in the document | Always | Required. Root element id. |
| `items` | array | `[]` | CollapsiblePanel configurations plus `content` | Always | Required, at least one. Display order. Each item needs its own unique `id` and a `title` (CollapsiblePanel rules). |
| `items[].content` | array \| string | `[]` | Static HTML strings or functions `(host, panel) => instance \| null` | Always | The panel's children, passed to `renderCollapsiblePanel()` unchanged. |
| `expandMode` | string | `'SINGLE'` | `SINGLE`, `MULTIPLE` | Always | `SINGLE`: opening an item closes the open one. `MULTIPLE`: items open and close independently. |
| `look` | string | `'JOINED'` | `JOINED`, `SEPARATE` | Always | `JOINED`: one frame with a line between items (items use CollapsiblePanel `PLAIN`). `SEPARATE`: one card per item, with a gap. |
| `bordered` | boolean | `true` | — | Always | JOINED: the thin line around the frame. SEPARATE: passed to every card unless the item sets its own. |
| `cornerRadius` | string | `'ROUNDED'` | `NONE`, `ROUNDED` | Always | JOINED: corners of the frame. SEPARATE: passed to every card unless the item sets its own. |
| `headingLevel` | number | `3` | Integer 2–6 | Always | Heading level of every item header (CollapsiblePanel `headingLevel`). |
| `keyboardNavigation` | boolean | `true` | — | Always | Up / Down (wrapping), Home / End move focus between headers; disabled and non-collapsible items are skipped. |
| `tooltipMode` | string | `'NONE'` | `NONE`, `TITLE`, `TOOLTIP` | Always | How the panels' icon-only actions (passed to each CollapsiblePanel) show their names on hover and keyboard focus: not at all, the browser's tooltip (`title`, mouse only) or a Tooltip (also on keyboard focus; needs `tooltip.css`, the Tooltip module is loaded only then). |
| `onChange` | function | `null` | `(openIds, instance) => {}` | Always | See Callbacks. |

Accordion sets on every item: `headingLevel` and `onToggle` (wrapped: the item's own `onToggle` still runs first). With `look:'JOINED'` it also sets `variant:'PLAIN'` and drops the item's `bordered` and `cornerRadius`. Item options it sets are ignored with `OPTION_IGNORED`: `items[n].headingLevel` always, `items[n].variant/bordered/cornerRadius` with JOINED. In SINGLE mode, when several items start with `state:'EXPANDED'`, only the first keeps it (`SINGLE_EXPANDED`).

### Callbacks

| Callback | Arguments | Fires when | Does not fire when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `onChange` | `(openIds, instance)` | The user opens or closes an item (after SINGLE has closed the other one); `openIds` as `getOpenIds()`. | `expand()`, `collapse()`, `expandAll()`, `collapseAll()`; disabled or non-collapsible items. |
| `items[].onToggle` | `(state, panel)` | As in CollapsiblePanel: the user toggles that item; runs before `onChange`. | As in CollapsiblePanel; an item closed by SINGLE coordination. |

### Errors

Accordion has no user-facing errors. Developer errors prevent rendering; warnings are logged and rendering continues. Console format: `Accordion "id" [LABEL]: message`. Errors in an item's configuration are reported by CollapsiblePanel.

| Label | Severity | Cause |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CONTAINER_REQUIRED` | error | No container passed. |
| `ID_REQUIRED` | error | `id` is empty. |
| `UNSAFE_ID` | error | `id` is not DOM-safe. |
| `DUPLICATE_ID` | error | An element with the same id already exists in the document. |
| `ITEMS_REQUIRED` | error | `items` is missing, empty, or has no valid item. |
| `INVALID_OPTION` | warning | Invalid `expandMode`, `look`, `cornerRadius` or `headingLevel`; the default is used. |
| `OPTION_IGNORED` | warning | An item option the Accordion sets itself (see Configuration), or `expandAll()` in SINGLE mode. |
| `INVALID_ITEM` | warning | An item that is not an object; dropped. |
| `ITEM_NOT_RENDERED` | warning | CollapsiblePanel refused an item (e.g. missing id or title, duplicate id); the item is left out. |
| `SINGLE_EXPANDED` | warning | SINGLE mode with several items starting open; only the first stays open. |
| `UNKNOWN_ITEM` | warning | `expand()` or `collapse()` with an id that is not an item. |

### Accessibility

- Follows the WAI-ARIA accordion pattern: each header is a native `<button>` with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`, inside a heading of level `headingLevel`, so screen-reader users can list the headers and jump between them.
- Each open section is a region labelled by its title (CollapsiblePanel); closed content is hidden and never reached with Tab.
- Tab and Shift+Tab move through headers and the open content; Enter and Space toggle (native button); Up / Down / Home / End move between headers when `keyboardNavigation` is on (it acts only while a header has focus).
- Opening or closing is announced through `aria-expanded`; no live region is needed.
- Status colours are visual only (CollapsiblePanel); add a Chip or text when a status must be announced.

### Examples

FAQ in SINGLE mode, with an open item and its answer loaded when first opened:

```js
const faq = renderAccordion(faqHost,
{
    id:'faq', headingLevel:3,
    items:
    [
        { id:'faq-shipping', title:'How fast do you ship?', state:'EXPANDED', content:[ '<p>Within 2 working days.</p>' ] },
        { id:'faq-returns', title:'Can I return an order?', lazyContent:true, content:[ host => { host.textContent = 'Loading…'; api.answer('returns').then(text => { host.textContent = text; }); return null; } ] }
    ],
    onChange:( openIds ) => analytics.track('faq-open',openIds)
});
```

Settings sections with fields, MULTIPLE mode, separate cards, inside a Form:

```js
renderForm(formHost,{ id:'settings', onSubmit:values => api.saveSettings(values) },
[
    host => renderAccordion(host,
    {
        id:'settings-sections', expandMode:'MULTIPLE', look:'SEPARATE',
        items:
        [
            { id:'section-account', title:'Account', icon:'fa-solid fa-user', state:'EXPANDED', content:[ h => renderTextInput(h,{ id:'name', name:'name', label:'Name' }) ] },
            { id:'section-privacy', title:'Privacy', icon:'fa-solid fa-lock', content:[ h => renderToggle(h,{ id:'public', name:'publicProfile', label:'Public profile' }) ] }
        ]
    })
]);
```

### Files

| File | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `accordionIndex.js` | Public entry point; the only import surface. |
| `accordionConfig.js` | Defaults, allowed values, normalization of the configuration and the items, developer validation. |
| `accordionComponent.js` | Lifecycle, CollapsiblePanel composition, SINGLE coordination, keyboard movement, runtime API. |
| `accordionHTML.js` | Frame and item hosts. |
| `accordionEvents.js` | Keyboard listener (Up / Down / Home / End on headers). |
| `accordionErrors.js` | Developer error and warning catalog. |
| `accordion.css` | Presentation of the frame, dividers and gap. |
| `accordionTESTS.md` | Test plan: the cases that prove this README (automatic ones in `tests/components/accordion.test.mjs`). |


<!-- ===== source/components-js/actionMenu/actionMenuREADME.md ===== -->

# ActionMenu

## For business

### Overview

ActionMenu is the small "more" button (three dots) that opens a short list of actions, such as Edit, Duplicate, Download or Delete. It keeps screens tidy when a row, card or page header has more actions than there is room for buttons.

### When to use

- Use it when a row, card or page header has more actions than there is room for buttons.
- Use Button when two or three actions fit on the screen; frequent actions stay visible as buttons.
- Use TopNavigation or SideNavigation for moving between pages.

### Key features

- A compact "more" button (three dots, or another icon) that opens a short list of actions.
- Actions with an optional icon, separators between groups, and dangerous actions marked in red.
- Unavailable actions stay visible but cannot be chosen.
- Entries that are links to other pages.
- The list opens where there is room: below or above the button, aligned to its end or start edge.

### Dependencies

| Dependency | Needed when | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Design system (`design-system.css`) | Always | Colours, spacing and typography. |
| ActionMenu styles (`actionMenu.css`) | Always | Menu appearance. |
| Button component and `button.css` | Always | The trigger button. |
| Font Awesome icon library | Always | Trigger and item icons. Loaded by the application page. |
| Tooltip component and `tooltip.css` | `tooltipMode` `TOOLTIP` | Tooltips (the Tooltip module is loaded only then). |

### Not included

The application performs the chosen action (and asks for confirmation for dangerous ones). Nested submenus, checkable items and menus opened by right-click are not part of this version.

## For designers

### Structure

```text
span.ui-action-menu
├── span.ui-action-menu-trigger-host → Button (icon; tertiary, or secondary when bordered) aria-haspopup="menu", aria-expanded
└── ul.ui-action-menu-list  role="menu", popover (top layer)
    ├── li[role="none"] > button.ui-action-menu-item[.ui-action-menu-danger]  role="menuitem" [aria-disabled]
    │   └── span.ui-action-menu-icon + span.ui-action-menu-label
    ├── li[role="none"] > a.ui-action-menu-item  role="menuitem"       (link items)
    └── li.ui-action-menu-separator  role="separator"
```

Items have the control height, a hover/focus background and the focus outline for keyboard users; danger items use the danger text colour; unavailable items keep their place with reduced opacity. Items without an icon keep the icon column, so labels align. The menu position is set by the component (`--ui-action-menu-top`, `--ui-action-menu-left`).

### Visual options

| Option | Values | CSS class or attribute |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Trigger size | Small, medium, large | Button sizes |
| Trigger border | Without (tertiary Button), with (secondary Button) | `bordered` |
| Item | Normal, danger | `.ui-action-menu-item`, `.ui-action-menu-danger` |
| Separator | — | `.ui-action-menu-separator` |

### States

| State | Values | CSS class or attribute |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Trigger under the pointer | Darker background | `.ui-action-menu .ui-button:hover` |
| Item | Unavailable | `[aria-disabled="true"]` |

### Styling contract

`actionMenu.css` has three parts, marked in the stylesheet. Restyle by writing the same selector with a new value in your own stylesheet, inside `@layer overrides` (preferred: library updates keep your changes), or by changing a value in your copy of the stylesheet. After each token come the parts it styles, named by their class without `ui-action-menu-` (as in Structure), with the option or state in brackets (joined by “+” when they apply together). Text uses the typography roles of `design-system.css`; border sides are physical (top, right, bottom, left).

**1. Appearance — change freely** (colours, type, borders, corners, motion: only the look changes)

- Colours
  - `--c-surface-muted`: button
  - `--c-border`: button (hover, pressed), list, separator
  - `--c-surface`: list
  - `--c-text`: list
  - `--c-surface-hover`: item (hover, focus)
  - `--c-danger-text`: danger
- Typography
  - `--font-ui`: list
  - `--fw-ui`: list
  - `--fs-control`: item
- Borders and corners
  - `--border-thin`: list, separator
  - `--radius-control`: list
  - `--radius-control-small`: item
- Shadows
  - `--shadow-md`: list
- States and motion
  - `--opacity-disabled`: item (disabled)

**2. Dimensions — change with care** (sizes and spacing: the component keeps working, its size changes)

- Spacing
  - `--gap-tight`: list, separator
  - `--gap-inline-items`: item
- Sizes
  - `--size-md-1`: list
  - `--size-md-3`: list
  - `--control-height`: item
  - `--icon-size-medium`: icon

**3. Structure — don't change** (layout, behaviour, states, accessibility)

- Borders and corners
  - `--border-thin`: item (focus)
- States and motion
  - `--focus-outline`: item (focus)

**Set by the component — don't change**

- Variables
  - `--ui-action-menu-left`, `--ui-action-menu-top`: position of the open list (measured)

## For AI-assisted development

### Instructions

- Read this README before writing code. Import only from `actionMenuIndex.js`.
- Use ActionMenu when more than two or three actions would not fit as icon Buttons; keep the most frequent actions as visible Buttons and put the rest in the menu.
- Give the trigger a specific name (`label`), e.g. "More actions for order 1042", especially in tables with one menu per row.
- Handle the chosen `key` in `onAction(key)`; ask for confirmation before dangerous actions.
- Give each menu a unique, DOM-safe `id` and call `destroy()` before rendering into the same container again (Table does this for cells rendered with `render()`).

### Safety

- Labels are displayed as text; do not pass HTML. Link `href`s come from the application: never build them from untrusted input without validation.
- Never remove the menu roles, `aria-haspopup` or `aria-expanded`.

### Example prompts

```text
Add an ActionMenu to each order row with Duplicate, Download invoice, Track shipment (link), a separator and Delete (danger); disable Archive for open orders.
```

## For developers

### Business analysis

> **Component**: the ActionMenu itself. **Consumer**: the developer who configures the ActionMenu in the application's code. **App**: the running application that uses the ActionMenu; it provides the data, performs the actions and stores the changes.

**Menu**

- User clicks the "more" button. <!-- BA-01 -->
  - Component opens the list of actions below the button, or above it when there is no room below. <!-- BA-02 -->
  - Component displays the list aligned with the end edge of the button, or with its start edge when there is no room. <!-- BA-03 -->
- User clicks an action. <!-- BA-04 -->
  - Component closes the list. <!-- BA-05 -->
  - Component reports the chosen action to the App. <!-- BA-06 -->
  - App performs the action. <!-- BA-07 -->
- User presses Escape, presses Tab, or clicks outside the list. <!-- BA-08 -->
  - Component closes the list without reporting an action. <!-- BA-09 -->

**Actions**

- Consumer provides the actions, each with a label and an optional icon. <!-- BA-10 -->
- Consumer adds separators between groups of actions (optional). <!-- BA-11 -->
- Component displays a dangerous action, e.g. "Delete", in the danger colour. <!-- BA-12 -->
- Component displays an unavailable action and prevents choosing it. <!-- BA-13 -->
- Component opens a link entry as a page link. <!-- BA-14 -->

**Keyboard additions**

- User presses the arrow keys, Home or End to move between actions. <!-- BA-15 -->
- User types the first letter of an action to move to it. <!-- BA-16 -->

**Button**

- Consumer provides the name of the button, e.g. "More actions for order 1042". <!-- BA-17 -->
- Consumer chooses the icon, the size and whether the button has a border. <!-- BA-18 -->
- Consumer disables the whole menu (optional). <!-- BA-19 -->

**Tooltips**

- Consumer chooses how the menu button shows its name on hover and keyboard focus: the browser's tooltip, a Tooltip or none (optional). <!-- BA-20 -->

### Contracts

**Contracts:** Styling: three parts (Styling contract) · Form field: no · Actions: no · Shared behaviour: yes, additions under Accessibility

### Public API

```js
import { renderActionMenu, DEFAULT_ACTION_MENU_CONFIG, ACTION_MENU_TOOLTIP_MODES, ACTION_MENU_SIZES } from './actionMenuIndex.js';

const menu = renderActionMenu(container, config, onAction); // null after a developer error
```

| Member | Returns | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | The configured id (the trigger Button's id). |
| `open()` | — | Opens the menu and focuses the first available item. |
| `close()` | — | Closes the menu. |
| `focus()` | boolean | Moves focus to the trigger. |
| `destroy()` | — | Closes the menu, removes listeners and the trigger Button, clears the container. |

### Configuration

| Parameter | Type | Default | Allowed values / format | Applies when | Usage / description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | — | Starts with a letter; letters, digits, `_ : . -`; unique in the document | Always | Required. Id of the trigger. |
| `label` | string | `'More actions'` | Text | Always | Accessible name of the trigger. |
| `icon` | string | `'fa-solid fa-ellipsis-vertical'` | Font Awesome classes | Always | Trigger icon. |
| `size` | string | `'SMALL'` | `SMALL`, `MEDIUM`, `LARGE` | Always | Trigger size. |
| `bordered` | boolean | `false` | — | Always | `true`: the trigger is a secondary icon Button (with a border); `false`: a tertiary one (no border). |
| `disabled` | boolean | `false` | — | Always | Disables the trigger. |
| `items` | array | `[]` | `{ key, label, icon?, disabled?, danger?, href?, target? }` or `{ type:'SEPARATOR' }` | Always | Required, at least one item. Keys unique; items with `href` are links. Leading, trailing and double separators are removed. |
| `tooltipMode` | string | `'NONE'` | `NONE`, `TITLE`, `TOOLTIP` | Always | How the menu button shows its name on hover and keyboard focus: not at all, the browser's tooltip (`title`, mouse only) or a Tooltip (also on keyboard focus; needs `tooltip.css`, the Tooltip module is loaded only then). |
| `onAction` | function | `null` | `(key, instance) => {}` | Always | Takes precedence over the third `renderActionMenu()` argument. |

### Callbacks

| Callback | Arguments | Fires when | Does not fire when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `onAction` | `(key, instance)` | An available item is chosen by click, Enter or Space (links also navigate). | Unavailable items; closing with Escape, Tab or an outside click. |

### Errors

ActionMenu has no user-facing errors. Developer errors prevent rendering; warnings are logged and rendering continues. Console format: `ActionMenu "id" [LABEL]: message`.

| Label | Severity | Cause |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CONTAINER_REQUIRED` | error | No container passed. |
| `ID_REQUIRED` | error | `id` is empty. |
| `UNSAFE_ID` | error | `id` is not DOM-safe. |
| `DUPLICATE_ID` | error | An element with the same id already exists in the document. |
| `ITEMS_REQUIRED` | error | No usable item. |
| `INVALID_ITEM` | warning | An item without key or label; dropped. |
| `DUPLICATE_ITEM_KEY` | warning | Duplicate key; dropped. |
| `INVALID_OPTION` | warning | Invalid `size`; the default is used. |

### Accessibility

- ARIA menu button pattern: the trigger has `aria-haspopup="menu"`, `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`; the list has `role="menu"` labelled by the trigger; entries are `role="menuitem"` (buttons or links), unavailable ones `aria-disabled="true"`.
- Opening focuses the first available item (ArrowUp on the trigger: the last); arrows wrap, Home/End jump, typing a letter jumps to the next matching item, Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger, Tab closes and moves on.
- Danger items are distinguished by colour and by their label (e.g. "Delete"), never by colour alone.

### Examples

```js
renderActionMenu(host,
{
    id:`more-${order.id}`, label:`More actions for order ${order.id}`,
    items:[
        { key:'duplicate', label:'Duplicate', icon:'fa-regular fa-copy' },
        { key:'invoice', label:'Download invoice', icon:'fa-solid fa-file-arrow-down' },
        { key:'track', label:'Track shipment', icon:'fa-solid fa-truck', href:`/orders/${order.id}/tracking` },
        { type:'SEPARATOR' },
        { key:'delete', label:'Delete', icon:'fa-solid fa-trash', danger:true }
    ]
},( key ) => handleOrderAction(key,order));
```

### Files

| File | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `actionMenuIndex.js` | Public entry point; the only import surface. |
| `actionMenuConfig.js` | Defaults, item normalization, developer validation. |
| `actionMenuComponent.js` | Trigger Button, open/close, positioning, keyboard, type-ahead. |
| `actionMenuHTML.js` | Menu markup. |
| `actionMenuEvents.js` | Menu and open-menu listeners. |
| `actionMenuErrors.js` | Developer error and warning catalog. |
| `actionMenu.css` | Presentation. |
| `actionMenuTESTS.md` | Test plan: the cases that prove this README (automatic ones in `tests/components/actionMenu.test.mjs`). |


<!-- ===== source/components-js/appHeader/appHeaderREADME.md ===== -->

# AppHeader

## For business

### Overview

AppHeader is the top area of every application page. It can show an announcement banner, the application's identity, search, the signed-in user and quick links on the first level, the main navigation on a second level, and breadcrumbs on a third level. Every element and every level is optional, and each level can stay visible while the page scrolls.

### When to use

- Use it once per application, as the top area of every page: identity, search, user, main navigation and breadcrumbs.
- Use TopNavigation, SearchBox, Breadcrumbs or Badge alone when the page has its own header layout.

### Key features

- Up to three optional levels: identity and tools; main navigation; breadcrumbs.
- Logo and name, environment label ("TEST"), search, notifications bell with a panel, help, settings, the user and sign in / sign out.
- An optional announcement banner above everything, closable by the user.
- Levels that stay visible while the page scrolls, without the page jumping.
- A "Skip to main content" link and a compact layout on phones.

### Dependencies

| Dependency | Needed when | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Design system (`design-system.css`) | Always | Colours, spacing and typography. |
| AppHeader styles (`appHeader.css`) | Always | Header layout and elements. |
| Button component and `button.css` | Sign in/out | Buttons. |
| Notification and `notification.css` | `notifications`, `user` | Bell with counter; the user's picture. |
| NotificationsPanel and `notificationsPanel.css` | `notifications.items` | Bell with a panel of the latest notifications. |
| Badge and `badge.css` | `user` | The user's name, role and picture. |
| Message and `message.css` | `announcement` | Announcement banner. |
| SearchBox and `searchBox.css` | `search` | Search. |
| TopNavigation and `topNavigation.css` | `navigation` | Second level. |
| Breadcrumbs, ActionMenu and their CSS | `breadcrumbs` | Third level. |
| Font Awesome icon library | Icons used | Icons. Loaded by the application page. |
| Tooltip component and `tooltip.css` | `tooltipMode` `TOOLTIP` | Tooltips (the Tooltip module is loaded only then). |

### Not included

The application decides what the header shows (user, permissions, environment), performs search, sign-in/sign-out and notification handling, and places the SideNavigation (passing the menu host). An organisation switcher is not part of this version.

## For designers

### Structure

```text
div#{id}.ui-app-header.ui-app-header-bg-{surface|brand}[.ui-app-header-pinned]      (keeps the space while pinned)
└── header.ui-app-header-inner  aria-label="Application header"
    ├── a.ui-app-header-skip                                                  (skip link)
    ├── div.ui-app-header-level.ui-app-header-announcement[.ui-app-header-sticky] → Message (BANNER)
    ├── div.ui-app-header-level.ui-app-header-top[.ui-app-header-sticky]
    │   ├── div.ui-app-header-start: span.ui-app-header-menu-host, a.ui-app-header-brand (img.ui-app-header-logo, span.ui-app-header-name), span.ui-app-header-environment
    │   ├── div.ui-app-header-middle: div.ui-app-header-search-host → SearchBox
    │   └── div.ui-app-header-end: span.ui-app-header-notifications-host → Notification (bell + count), a.ui-app-header-icon-link (help, settings),
    │                              span.ui-app-header-user-host → Badge (picture, name, role, link), span.ui-app-header-auth-host → Button
    ├── div.ui-app-header-level.ui-app-header-navigation[.ui-app-header-sticky] → TopNavigation
    └── div.ui-app-header-level.ui-app-header-breadcrumbs[.ui-app-header-sticky] → Breadcrumbs
```

The first level is a row with start, middle and end zones; levels are separated by thin lines. The environment label is a small pill in the tone colours (info, success, warning, danger); the notifications bell is a Notification with a danger-coloured count; the user is a Badge (picture or initials, bold name, muted role). With the brand background both switch to light colours (`--c-on-accent`). When levels are pinned, the header gets a small shadow. With the brand background, the first level uses the accent colour with light text and secondary Buttons.

### Visual options

| Option | Values | CSS class or attribute |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Background (first level) | Surface, brand | `ui-app-header-bg-surface`, `ui-app-header-bg-brand` |
| Environment tone | Info, success, warning, danger | `ui-app-header-tone-info`, `-success`, `-warning`, `-danger` |
| Sticky level | Per level | `ui-app-header-sticky` |

### States

| State | Values | CSS class or attribute |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pinned | While the page scrolls under the sticky levels | `ui-app-header-pinned` |

### Styling contract

`appHeader.css` has three parts, marked in the stylesheet. Restyle by writing the same selector with a new value in your own stylesheet, inside `@layer overrides` (preferred: library updates keep your changes), or by changing a value in your copy of the stylesheet. After each token come the parts it styles, named by their class without `ui-app-header-` (as in Structure), with the option or state in brackets (joined by “+” when they apply together). Text uses the typography roles of `design-system.css`; border sides are physical (top, right, bottom, left).

**1. Appearance — change freely** (colours, type, borders, corners, motion: only the look changes)

- Colours
  - `--c-surface`: inner, skip
  - `--c-text`: inner
  - `--c-border`: inner, level
  - `--c-accent`: skip, top (bg brand)
  - `--c-info-soft`: tone info
  - `--c-info-text`: tone info
  - `--c-success-soft`: tone success
  - `--c-success-text`: tone success
  - `--c-warning-soft`: tone warning
  - `--c-warning-text`: tone warning
  - `--c-danger-soft`: tone danger
  - `--c-danger-text`: tone danger
  - `--c-surface-hover`: icon link (hover)
  - `--c-on-accent`: top (bg brand), icon link (bg brand + top + hover)
- Typography
  - `--font-ui`: app header
  - `--fw-ui`: app header
  - `--fw-ui-strong`: skip, name, environment
  - `--fs-block-title`: name
  - `--fs-caption`: environment
- Borders and corners
  - `--border-thin`: inner, level
  - `--radius-control`: skip, brand
  - `--radius-pill`: environment, icon link
- Shadows
  - `--shadow-sm`: inner (pinned)
- Sizes
  - `--icon-size-medium`: icon link

**2. Dimensions — change with care** (sizes and spacing: the component keeps working, its size changes)

- Spacing
  - `--gap-tight`: skip, top, environment
  - `--gap-inline-items`: skip, top, start, end, environment
  - `--workspace-gutter`: level (also narrow)
  - `--gap-block`: top, middle
  - `--space-sm-2`: navigation, breadcrumbs, logo
  - `--space-xl-1`: brand
  - `--space-sm-1`: environment
- Sizes
  - `--control-height`: top, logo, icon link
  - `--space-lg-1`: top, icon link
  - `--size-md-2`: middle, search host
  - `--size-md-1`: logo
  - `--size-md-4`: search host

**3. Structure — don't change** (layout, behaviour, states, accessibility)

- States and motion
  - `--focus-outline`: skip (focus), brand (focus), icon link (focus)
  - `--focus-offset`: skip (focus), brand (focus), icon link (focus)

**Set by the component — don't change**

- Variables
  - `--ui-app-header-space`: height kept in the page while the header is pinned (measured)
  - `--ui-app-header-left`, `--ui-app-header-width`: position and width of the pinned header (measured)
  - `--page-sticky-offset`: on the page: height of the sticky levels; Message toasts and Table read it

**Used by the code** (the component's code names these tokens; change the token to change the result)

- Tokens
  - `--c-accent`, `--c-on-accent`: user Badge and its marker on the brand background

## For AI-assisted development

### Instructions

- Read this README before writing code. Import only from `appHeaderIndex.js`.
- Configure only the elements the application needs; everything is optional. Pass SearchBox, TopNavigation and Breadcrumbs options in `search`, `navigation` and `breadcrumbs` (their `id` is set by AppHeader).
- Render AppHeader once, above the page content, in a container that spans the page width; set `skipLinkTarget` to the id of the main content (`'#main'`).
- With SideNavigation, set `menuHost:true` and pass `header.getMenuHost()` as SideNavigation's `drawerToggleHost`.
- Update the header at runtime (`getAnnouncement().update(…)`, `setUser`, `setSignedIn`, `setNotificationCount`, `getTopNavigation().setCurrent(…)`, `getBreadcrumbs().update(…)`) instead of rendering it again.
- Keep sticky levels few (usually the first level, sometimes navigation) to leave room for content on small screens.
- Give the header a unique, DOM-safe `id` and call `destroy()` before rendering into the same container again.

### Safety

- All texts are displayed as text; do not pass HTML. Build links from trusted routes only.
- Hiding elements does not secure anything: check permissions on the server.
- Keep the skip link and the header's landmark name.

### Example prompts

```text
Add an AppHeader with the logo and name "Orders", a TEST badge in the test environment, search for orders, the signed-in user's name and role linking to their profile, a settings shortcut and sign out; second level TopNavigation with Dashboard, Orders and Reports; third level breadcrumbs; keep the first two levels sticky.
```

## For developers

### Business analysis

> **Component**: the AppHeader itself. **Consumer**: the developer who configures the AppHeader in the application's code. **App**: the running application that uses the AppHeader; it provides the data, performs the actions and stores the changes.

**First level** (every element optional)

- Component displays the logo and the application name, linked to the home page. <!-- BA-01 -->
- Component displays an environment label, e.g. "TEST". <!-- BA-02 -->
- Component displays the search field. <!-- BA-03 -->
  - User types a search and presses Enter or the search button. <!-- BA-04 -->
  - Component reports the search to the App. <!-- BA-05 -->
  - App performs the search. <!-- BA-06 -->
- Component displays the notifications bell with a counter. <!-- BA-07 -->
  - User clicks the bell. <!-- BA-08 -->
  - Component opens the panel with the latest notifications, or reports the click to the App. <!-- BA-09 -->
- Component displays the help and settings shortcuts. <!-- BA-10 -->
- Component displays the signed-in user with a photo or initials, the name, the role and a marker, e.g. "Online", linked to the user's page. <!-- BA-11 -->
- Component displays "Sign in" or "Sign out". <!-- BA-12 -->
  - User clicks it. <!-- BA-13 -->
  - Component reports the request to the App. <!-- BA-14 -->
  - App performs the sign-in or sign-out. <!-- BA-15 -->
- Component displays a place for the side navigation's menu button on phones. <!-- BA-16 -->
- Consumer chooses a light or a brand-coloured first level. <!-- BA-17 -->

**Other levels** (optional)

- Component displays the main navigation on the second level. <!-- BA-18 -->
- Component displays the breadcrumbs on the third level. <!-- BA-19 -->

**Announcement** (optional)

- App provides an announcement, e.g. "Planned maintenance tonight at 22:00". <!-- BA-20 -->
  - Component displays it as a full-width banner above everything. <!-- BA-21 -->
- User clicks the close button of the announcement. <!-- BA-22 -->
  - Component reports the close to the App. <!-- BA-23 -->

**Scrolling**

- Consumer chooses which levels stay visible while the page scrolls. <!-- BA-24 -->
  - Component keeps those levels at the top and lets the others scroll away. <!-- BA-25 -->
  - Component keeps the page from jumping, and places other sticky elements, e.g. table headers, below the header. <!-- BA-26 -->

**Keyboard additions**

- Component displays a "Skip to main content" link as the first stop on the page. <!-- BA-27 -->

**Phones and narrow screens**

- Component hides the application name next to a logo, and the name and role of the user. <!-- BA-28 -->
- Component moves the search field to its own line. <!-- BA-29 -->

**Tooltips**

- Consumer chooses how the names of the help and settings links and the environment's description shows on hover and keyboard focus: the browser's tooltip, a Tooltip or none (optional, on by default with the browser). <!-- BA-30 -->

### Contracts

**Contracts:** Styling: three parts (Styling contract) · Form field: no · Actions: no · Shared behaviour: yes, additions under Accessibility

### Public API

```js
import { renderAppHeader, DEFAULT_APP_HEADER_CONFIG, APP_HEADER_TOOLTIP_MODES, APP_HEADER_TONES, APP_HEADER_BACKGROUNDS } from './appHeaderIndex.js';

const header = renderAppHeader(container, config); // null after a developer error
```

| Member | Returns | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | The configured id. |
| `getAnnouncement()` | instance \| null | The announcement Message (`show()`, `hide()`, `update()`), e.g. to change its text or show it again. |
| `showAnnouncement(message)` | — | Shows any Message configuration (`{ type, text, title?, link?, … }`) in the announcement banner, replacing the current one; announced. The collector for other components' `externalMessage.onMessage` (e.g. a Form's success message). |
| `setUser(user)` | — | Shows, changes or removes (`null`) the user Badge. |
| `setSignedIn(signedIn)` | — | Switches the Button between "Sign in" and "Sign out". |
| `setNotificationCount(count)` | — | Updates the counter (0 hides it; above 99 shows "99+"). |
| `getMenuHost()` | Element \| null | Host for SideNavigation's menu Button. |
| `getUserBadge()` / `getNotifications()` | instance \| null | The user Badge (`setIndicator`, `setDescription`, …) and the bell Notification — or the NotificationsPanel (`setNotifications`, `addNotification`, …) when `notifications.items` is configured. |
| `getSearchBox()` / `getTopNavigation()` / `getBreadcrumbs()` | instance \| null | The composed components, for runtime updates. |
| `destroy()` | — | Removes listeners and child components, restores `--page-sticky-offset`, clears the container. |

### Configuration

Every option is optional; an element is shown only when configured.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Allowed values / format | Applies when | Usage / description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | — | Starts with a letter; letters, digits, `_ : . -`; unique in the document | Always | Required. |
| `skipLinkTarget` | string | `''` | `'#main'` | Always | "Skip to main content" link to this target. |
| `menuHost` | boolean | `false` | — | Always | Adds the host for SideNavigation's menu Button (start of the first level). |
| `logo` | object | `null` | `{ src, alt }` | Always | Logo image; `alt` is used when there is no `appName` (`LOGO_ALT_MISSING`). |
| `appName` | string | `''` | Text | Always | Application name. |
| `homeHref` | string | `''` | URL | `logo` or `appName` | Makes logo and name a link to the home page. |
| `environment` | object | `null` | `{ label, description?, tone? }` | Always | Environment label, e.g. `{ label:'TEST', description:'Test environment' }`; tone default `WARNING`. |
| `announcement` | object | `null` | Message configuration (without `id` and `layout`) | Always | Banner above the header (Message `BANNER`), closable by default; when closed its level is removed and sticky heights are recalculated. |
| `search` | object | `null` | SearchBox configuration (without `id`) | Always | Search; `label` defaults to "Search", shown to screen readers only. |
| `notifications` | object | `null` | `{ count }` or NotificationsPanel configuration `{ items, maxItems?, … }` (without `id`) | Always | `{ count }`: a bell (Notification) with a count; clicks call `onNotifications`. With `items`: a NotificationsPanel — bell with the unread count and a panel of the latest notifications (see NotificationsPanel). |
| `help` / `settings` | object | `null` | `{ href, label? }` | Always | Icon links to help and to the application settings. |
| `user` | object | `null` | `{ name, role?, href?, avatar?, indicator? }` | Always | The user as a Badge: photo (`avatar` URL) or initials, name, role; `indicator` is a Notification indicator (e.g. `{ kind:'DOT', type:'SUCCESS', description:'Online' }`); a link to the user's page when `href` is set. |
| `auth` | object | `null` | `{ signedIn }` | Always | Sign in / Sign out Button (`onSignIn`, `onSignOut`). |
| `navigation` | object | `null` | TopNavigation configuration (without `id`) | Always | Second level. |
| `breadcrumbs` | object | `null` | Breadcrumbs configuration (without `id`) | Always | Third level. |
| `sticky` | object | all `false` | `{ announcement, top, navigation, breadcrumbs }` | Always | Levels that stay pinned at the top while scrolling; a level that is not configured is ignored. |
| `autoMeasure` | boolean | `true` | — | Always | Re-measures the header when a level changes height (see Sticky levels); `false` turns this off. Has an effect only when a level is sticky. |
| `background` | string | `'SURFACE'` | `SURFACE`, `BRAND` | Always | First-level background. |
| `tooltipMode` | string | `'TITLE'` | `NONE`, `TITLE`, `TOOLTIP` | Always | How the names of the help and settings links and the environment's description shows on hover and keyboard focus: not at all, the browser's tooltip (`title`, mouse only) or a Tooltip (also on keyboard focus; needs `tooltip.css`, the Tooltip module is loaded only then). It is passed to the user Badge (the "Your profile and settings" hint is on AppHeader's own host around it), the notifications and the Breadcrumbs, and (as `TOOLTIP` only) to the icon buttons of the search, the navigation and the announcement, unless their own configuration sets `tooltipMode`. |
| `texts.*` | string | English defaults | Text | Always | Each is used when its element is shown: `header`, `skipLink`, `settings`, `help`, `notifications`, `notificationsCount` ("{count} new"), `signIn`, `signOut`, `userPage`. |
| `onSignIn` / `onSignOut` | function | `null` | `(instance) => {}` | `auth` | Sign in / Sign out Button callbacks. |
| `onNotifications` | function | `null` | `(instance) => {}` | `notifications` | Notifications Button callback; only for `notifications` `{ count }` (with `items` the NotificationsPanel handles clicks). |

### Sticky levels

Each level with `sticky:true` is pinned at the top once the first sticky level scrolls past the top of the viewport (at scroll position 0 nothing is pinned, so all levels are visible); the other levels then scroll away (levels below the pinned ones are hidden while pinned). The root keeps the header's full height, so content does not jump, and `--page-sticky-offset` is set to the pinned height.

With `autoMeasure` (default), AppHeader re-measures itself when a level changes height — e.g. `getBreadcrumbs().update()` switching to the narrow back link, `getSearchBox().setMessage()`, a wrapping navigation or late-loading fonts — at most once per animation frame. While pinned, only the visible sticky levels are re-measured (the offset and the reserved space follow them); a hidden level that changed is measured again when it reappears on unpinning. With `autoMeasure:false` the header is measured only on render, window resize, `setUser()` and announcement changes (the behaviour before this option). AppHeader does this itself because CSS `position:sticky` only works inside the element's parent, and the container is owned by the application.

### Callbacks

| Callback | Arguments | Fires when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `onSignIn` / `onSignOut` | `(instance)` | The Sign in / Sign out Button is pressed (the application signs in or out and calls `setSignedIn`). |
| `onNotifications` | `(instance)` | The notifications Button is pressed. |
| `search.onSearch`, `navigation.onNavigate`, `breadcrumbs.onNavigate` | See SearchBox, TopNavigation, Breadcrumbs | Passed through to the composed components. |

### Errors

AppHeader has no user-facing errors. Developer errors prevent rendering; warnings are logged and rendering continues. Console format: `AppHeader "id" [LABEL]: message`.

| Label | Severity | Cause |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CONTAINER_REQUIRED` | error | No container passed. |
| `ID_REQUIRED` | error | `id` is empty. |
| `UNSAFE_ID` | error | `id` is not DOM-safe. |
| `DUPLICATE_ID` | error | An element with the same id already exists in the document. |
| `CONTENT_REQUIRED` | error | No element and no level configured. |
| `LOGO_ALT_MISSING` | warning | A logo without `alt` and without `appName`. |
| `BRAND_MENU_HOST` | warning | `BRAND` background with `menuHost`: SideNavigation's tertiary menu Button may be hard to see. |
| `INVALID_OPTION` | warning | Invalid tone or background; the default is used. |
| `OPTION_IGNORED` | warning | Sticky option for a level that is not configured; the removed `status` option (use `announcement`). |

### Accessibility

- A `<header>` landmark named "Application header"; the skip link is the first focusable element and becomes visible on focus.
- The announcement is a Message banner: read in place when present at load; announced when shown or updated later.
- The environment label has a spoken description; the notifications bell (Notification) includes the count in its name ("Notifications, 3 new"); the user Badge reads as one sentence ("Ana Pop, Administrator, Online"); icon links have names and tooltips; the user link has a tooltip ("Your profile and settings").
- Pinned levels keep their order and focus; hidden (non-sticky) levels are not reachable while pinned.

### Examples

```js
const header = renderAppHeader(headerHost,
{
    id:'app-header', skipLinkTarget:'#main', menuHost:true,
    logo:{ src:'/logo.svg', alt:'Orders' }, appName:'Orders', homeHref:'/',
    environment:isTest ? { label:'TEST', description:'Test environment' } : null,
    search:{ label:'Search orders', placeholder:'Search orders', searchMode:'ON_DEMAND', onSearch:( { query } ) => router.go(`/search?q=${encodeURIComponent(query)}`) },
    settings:{ href:'/settings' }, user:{ name:user.name, role:user.role, href:'/me', avatar:user.photo, indicator:{ kind:'DOT', type:'SUCCESS', description:'Online' } }, auth:{ signedIn:true },
    navigation:{ items:topItems, currentId, onNavigate:routeTo },
    breadcrumbs:{ items:path, onNavigate:routeTo },
    sticky:{ top:true, navigation:true },
    announcement:{ type:'INFO', text:'New: export to Excel is available.', onClose:() => rememberClosed('export-news') },
    onSignOut:() => auth.signOut()
});

renderSideNavigation(sideHost,{ id:'side-nav', items:sideItems, drawerToggleHost:header.getMenuHost() });
header.getAnnouncement()?.update({ type:'WARNING', text:'Maintenance tonight at 22:00' });
```

### Files

| File | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `appHeaderIndex.js` | Public entry point; the only import surface. |
| `appHeaderConfig.js` | Defaults, normalization of the optional elements, developer validation. |
| `appHeaderComponent.js` | Composition of SearchBox, TopNavigation, Breadcrumbs and Buttons; runtime updates; pinning of sticky levels. |
| `appHeaderHTML.js` | Header, levels and element markup. |
| `appHeaderEvents.js` | Scroll and resize listeners for pinning. |
| `appHeaderErrors.js` | Developer error and warning catalog. |
| `appHeader.css` | Presentation. |
| `appHeaderTESTS.md` | Test plan: the cases that prove this README (automatic ones in `tests/components/appHeader.test.mjs`). |


<!-- ===== source/components-js/badge/badgeREADME.md ===== -->

# Badge

## For business

### Overview

Badge shows who someone is (or what something is) at a glance: a picture, initials or icon — with an optional marker such as an "online" dot or a count — next to a name and an optional role or description. Typical uses: the signed-in user in the header, the owner of a record, members of a team, a support channel with unread messages.

### When to use

- Use it to show who someone is, or what something is, next to its name: the signed-in user, the owner of a record, team members, a support channel.
- Use Notification for an icon or picture with a marker and no name.
- Use Chip for short labels such as a status or a category.

### Key features

- A picture, initials or an icon next to a name and an optional role or description.
- An optional marker on the picture: a count, a dot in four shapes, or a short text.
- Text beside the picture or centred below it, in three sizes.
- A link to a page, a button, or display only.
- Long texts shortened with "…" and shown in full as a tooltip.

### Dependencies

| Dependency | Needed when | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Design system (`design-system.css`) | Always | Colours, sizes and typography. |
| Badge styles (`badge.css`) | Always | Layout and text. |
| Notification component and `notification.css` | With a picture | Picture, initials or icon and the marker. |
| Font Awesome icon library | Icon pictures | Icons. Loaded by the application page. |
| Tooltip component and `tooltip.css` | `tooltipMode` `TOOLTIP` | Tooltips (the Tooltip module is loaded only then). |

### Not included

The application provides the person's data (name, role, photo, presence) and the page the link leads to. Groups of overlapping avatars ("+4") are not part of this version.

## For designers

### Structure

```text
a#{id}.ui-badge.ui-badge-{horizontal|vertical}.ui-badge-size-{small|medium|large}.ui-badge-interactive   (link; button with onClick; span[role="group"] display only)
├── span.ui-badge-notification-host → Notification (display only, aria-hidden)          (optional)
└── span.ui-badge-text
    ├── span.ui-badge-name
    ├── span.ui-badge-description                                                       (optional)
    └── span.ui-badge-visually-hidden  ", Online"                                        (marker meaning)
```

The name is bold, the description smaller and muted. Interactive badges (link or button) have more space around the content, a rounded hover background and the focus outline around the whole badge.

### Visual options

| Option | Values | CSS class or attribute |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Layout | Horizontal, vertical | `ui-badge-horizontal`, `ui-badge-vertical` |
| Size | Small, medium, large | `ui-badge-size-small`, `-medium`, `-large` (also the Notification size) |
| Interaction | Link, button, display only | `a` / `button` with `ui-badge-interactive`, `span[role="group"]` |

### States

No states of its own.

### Styling contract

`badge.css` has three parts, marked in the stylesheet. Restyle by writing the same selector with a new value in your own stylesheet, inside `@layer overrides` (preferred: library updates keep your changes), or by changing a value in your copy of the stylesheet. After each token come the parts it styles, named by their class without `ui-badge-` (as in Structure), with the option or state in brackets (joined by “+” when they apply together). Text uses the typography roles of `design-system.css`; border sides are physical (top, right, bottom, left).

**1. Appearance — change freely** (colours, type, borders, corners, motion: only the look changes)

- Colours
  - `--c-text`: badge
  - `--c-muted`: description
  - `--c-surface-hover`: badge (interactive + hover)
- Typography
  - `--font-ui`: badge
  - `--fw-ui`: badge
  - `--lh-compact`: text
  - `--fs-label`: name, description (size large)
  - `--fw-ui-strong`: name
  - `--fs-caption`: description, name (size small)
  - `--fs-fine`: description (size small)
  - `--fs-control`: name (size large)
- Borders and corners
  - `--radius-pill`: badge
  - `--radius-control`: badge (vertical)
- States and motion
  - `--transition-1`: badge (interactive)

**2. Dimensions — change with care** (sizes and spacing: the component keeps working, its size changes)

- Spacing
  - `--gap-inline-items`: badge
  - `--space-sm-2`: badge
  - `--space-sm-3`: badge (interactive)
  - `--space-md-3`: badge (interactive)
  - `--gap-tight`: badge (vertical)
- Sizes
  - `--size-md-2`: text

**3. Structure — don't change** (layout, behaviour, states, accessibility)

- States and motion
  - `--focus-outline`: badge (interactive + focus)
  - `--focus-offset`: badge (interactive + focus)

**Set by the component — don't change**

- Variables
  - `--ui-badge-color`, `--ui-badge-description-color`: name and description colours (from `colorToken`, `descriptionColorToken`)

## For AI-assisted development

### Instructions

- Read this README before writing code. Import only from `badgeIndex.js`.
- Pass the picture in `notification` as a Notification configuration without `id`, `size`, `clickable` or `onClick` (Badge sets them): `{ image }`, `{ text:'AP' }` or `{ icon }`, plus an optional `indicator`.
- Give dot markers a `description` ("Online", "Away"), so the spoken sentence is complete.
- Use `href` when the badge leads to a page (e.g. the user's profile); `onClick` when it opens something on the page; neither for display only.
- Change the marker through `badge.setIndicator()` / `badge.setCount()` (not through the Notification directly), so the spoken text follows.
- Give each badge a unique, DOM-safe `id` and call `destroy()` before rendering into the same container again.

### Safety

- Texts are displayed as text; do not pass HTML. Use image and link addresses from trusted sources.

### Example prompts

```text
Show the signed-in user as a Badge with photo, name and role, a green "Online" dot (top-right, the default corner), linking to the profile page.
```

## For developers

### Business analysis

> **Component**: the Badge itself. **Consumer**: the developer who configures the Badge in the application's code. **App**: the running application that uses the Badge; it provides the data, performs the actions and stores the changes.

**Content**

- Consumer provides the name, and a role or description (optional), e.g. "Administrator". <!-- BA-01 -->
- Consumer provides a picture, initials or an icon (optional). <!-- BA-02 -->
  - Component displays a marker on the picture: a count, a dot or a short text (optional). <!-- BA-03 -->
  - Component displays the marker in the top-right corner, or in another corner chosen by the Consumer. <!-- BA-04 -->
- Component displays the text beside the picture, or centred below it (optional). <!-- BA-05 -->
- Consumer chooses one of three sizes. <!-- BA-06 -->
  - Component adapts the picture and the text together. <!-- BA-07 -->
- Component shortens long texts with "…". <!-- BA-08 -->
  - User hovers over a shortened text. <!-- BA-09 -->
  - Component displays the full text as a tooltip. <!-- BA-10 -->

**Interaction**

- Consumer chooses link, button or display only. <!-- BA-11 -->
- User clicks a link badge. <!-- BA-12 -->
