  - Component opens the linked page. <!-- BA-13 -->
- User clicks a button badge. <!-- BA-14 -->
  - Component reports the click to the App. <!-- BA-15 -->
  - App performs the action. <!-- BA-16 -->

**Changes**

- App changes the name, the description or the marker. <!-- BA-17 -->
  - Component displays the change in place. <!-- BA-18 -->

**Screen readers**

- Component announces the badge as one sentence, e.g. "Ana Pop, Administrator, Online". <!-- BA-19 -->

**Colours**

- Consumer chooses own text colours, e.g. light text on a brand-coloured header (optional). <!-- BA-20 -->

**Tooltips**

- Consumer chooses how the full name and description shows on hover and keyboard focus: the browser's tooltip, a Tooltip or none (optional, on by default with the browser). <!-- BA-21 -->

### Contracts

**Contracts:** Styling: three parts (Styling contract) · Form field: no · Actions: no · Shared behaviour: yes, additions under Accessibility

### Public API

```js
import { renderBadge, DEFAULT_BADGE_CONFIG, BADGE_TOOLTIP_MODES, BADGE_LAYOUTS, BADGE_SIZES } from './badgeIndex.js';

const badge = renderBadge(container, config, onClick); // null after a developer error
```

| Member | Returns | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | The configured id. |
| `getElement()` | Element | The link, button or group. |
| `getNotification()` | instance \| null | The composed Notification. |
| `setName(name)` | — | Changes the name. |
| `setDescription(description)` | — | Changes or removes (`''`) the role/description. |
| `setIndicator(changes)` | — | Changes or removes (`null`) the Notification's marker; the spoken text follows. |
| `setCount(count)` | — | Sets a count marker (0 hides it); the spoken text follows. |
| `destroy()` | — | Removes listeners and the Notification, clears the container. |

### Configuration

| Parameter | Type | Default | Allowed values / format | Applies when | Usage / description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | — | Starts with a letter; letters, digits, `_ : . -`; unique in the document | Always | Required. |
| `name` | string | — | Text | Always | Required. |
| `description` | string | `''` | Text | Always | Optional role or description. |
| `notification` | object | `null` | Notification configuration (without `id`, `size`, `clickable`, `onClick`) | Always | Picture, initials or icon, with an optional `indicator`; `label` defaults to `name`. Without it, the badge shows text only. |
| `size` | string | `'MEDIUM'` | `SMALL`, `MEDIUM`, `LARGE` | Always | Size of the Notification and the text. |
| `layout` | string | `'HORIZONTAL'` | `HORIZONTAL`, `VERTICAL` | Always | Text beside or below the picture. |
| `href` | string | `''` | URL | Always | Makes the badge a link. |
| `colorToken` | string | — | Design-token name | Always | Text colour of the name (e.g. `'--c-on-accent'` on a brand background); hover tints follow it. |
| `descriptionColorToken` | string | — | Design-token name | Always | Colour of the description (default muted). |
| `tooltipMode` | string | `'TITLE'` | `NONE`, `TITLE`, `TOOLTIP` | Always | How the full name and description (`TOOLTIP`: only when they are cut off) shows on hover and keyboard focus: not at all, the browser's tooltip (`title`, mouse only) or a Tooltip (also on keyboard focus; needs `tooltip.css`, the Tooltip module is loaded only then). |
| `onClick` | function | `null` | `(event, instance) => {}` | Always | Makes the badge a button (with `href`: reported before navigation). Takes precedence over the third argument. |

### Callbacks

| Callback | Arguments | Fires when | Does not fire when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `onClick` | `(event, instance)` | The badge (button or link) is activated. | Display-only badges. |

### Errors

Badge has no user errors of its own. Developer errors prevent rendering; warnings are logged and rendering continues. Console format: `Badge "id" [LABEL]: message`.

| Label | Severity | Cause |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CONTAINER_REQUIRED` | error | No container passed. |
| `ID_REQUIRED` | error | `id` is empty. |
| `UNSAFE_ID` | error | `id` is not DOM-safe. |
| `DUPLICATE_ID` | error | An element with the same id already exists in the document. |
| `NAME_REQUIRED` | error | `name` is empty (also in `setName()`, which then keeps the previous name). |
| `NOTIFICATION_FAILED` | warning | The Notification could not be rendered; the badge shows text only. |
| `INVALID_OPTION` | warning | Invalid size, layout or colour token; the default is used. |
| `OPTION_IGNORED` | warning | `notification.clickable`, `notification.onClick` or `notification.size` (set by Badge); `onClick` together with `href`. |

### Accessibility

- One interactive element: the whole badge is the link or button; the Notification inside is display-only and hidden from assistive technology, so there are no nested controls or double names.
- The accessible name is the visible text plus the marker's meaning: "Ana Pop, Administrator, Online" (separators are visually hidden). Display-only badges are a named group.
- Tooltips give the full name and description when they are cut.

### Examples

```js
const me = renderBadge(userHost,{ id:'me', name:user.name, description:user.role, href:'/profile',
    notification:{ image:user.photo, indicator:{ kind:'DOT', type:'SUCCESS', description:'Online' } } });
me.setIndicator({ shape:'SQUARE', type:'WARNING', description:'Away' });
```

### Files

| File | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `badgeIndex.js` | Public entry point; the only import surface. |
| `badgeConfig.js` | Defaults, normalization, developer validation. |
| `badgeComponent.js` | Composition with Notification, spoken text, updates, click. |
| `badgeHTML.js` | Badge and text markup. |
| `badgeEvents.js` | Click listener. |
| `badgeErrors.js` | Developer error and warning catalog. |
| `badge.css` | Presentation. |
| `badgeTESTS.md` | Test plan: the cases that prove this README (automatic ones in `tests/components/badge.test.mjs`). |


<!-- ===== source/components-js/breadcrumbs/breadcrumbsREADME.md ===== -->

# Breadcrumbs

## For business

### Overview

Breadcrumbs show where the user is in the application, as a path from the top level to the current page (e.g. Home › Customers › Northwind › Contracts). Each level above the current page is a link, so users can go back several steps at once.

### When to use

- Use it to show where the user is in a hierarchy of pages and to go back several levels at once, e.g. Home › Customers › Northwind › Contracts.
- Use TopNavigation or SideNavigation for the main menu, and Pagination for pages of one list.

### Key features

- The path from the top level to the current page, each level above it a link.
- Long paths shortened to the first level, "…" and the last levels.
- Optional sibling lists: jump sideways to other pages at the same level.
- A single "Back to {parent}" link on narrow screens.
- Optional data for search engines on public pages.

### Dependencies

| Dependency | Needed when | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Design system (`design-system.css`) | Always | Colours, spacing and typography. |
| Breadcrumbs styles (`breadcrumbs.css`) | Always | Path, separators, back link. |
| ActionMenu component, `actionMenu.css`, Button and `button.css` | Long paths (collapsed levels) | The "…" menu. |
| Button and `button.css` | Levels with siblings | The arrow button (tertiary icon) of sibling dropdowns. |
| Font Awesome icon library | Home icon, collapsed levels, item icons | Icons. Loaded by the application page. |
| Tooltip component and `tooltip.css` | `tooltipMode` `TOOLTIP` | Tooltips (the Tooltip module is loaded only then). |

### Not included

The application builds the path and the sibling lists (from its routes or data), updates them after navigation, and decides whether to add structured data for search engines (public pages only). Sibling lists are passed in full (no loading on demand in this version).

## For designers

### Structure

```text
nav#{id}.ui-breadcrumbs.ui-breadcrumbs-separator-{chevron|slash|arrow|dot}[.ui-breadcrumbs-back-on-narrow]  aria-label="Breadcrumb"   (size container)
├── ol.ui-breadcrumbs-list
│   ├── li.ui-breadcrumbs-item > a.ui-breadcrumbs-link  (icon + span.ui-breadcrumbs-label)
│   ├── li.ui-breadcrumbs-item.ui-breadcrumbs-more > span.ui-breadcrumbs-more-host → ActionMenu "…"   (collapsed levels)
│   ├── li.ui-breadcrumbs-item > … + span.ui-breadcrumbs-siblings-host → Button (tertiary icon, chevron)
│   │                           + ul.ui-breadcrumbs-siblings > li > a.ui-breadcrumbs-sibling[aria-current]   (siblings; hidden until opened)
│   ├── li.ui-breadcrumbs-item > span.ui-breadcrumbs-text                  (level without link)
│   └── li.ui-breadcrumbs-item > span.ui-breadcrumbs-current  aria-current="page"
└── a.ui-breadcrumbs-back  (span.ui-breadcrumbs-back-icon + "Back to …")   (shown below 30rem)
```

Separators are CSS decorations between items (not read by screen readers): a drawn chevron, or the characters "/", "›" or "·" in the muted colour; chevron and arrow mirror in right-to-left languages. Links use the accent colour and are underlined; the current page is bold in the text colour; labels are cut at a maximum width with "…".

### Visual options

| Option | Values | CSS class or attribute |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Level | Link, text | `.ui-breadcrumbs-link`, `.ui-breadcrumbs-text` |
| Separator | Chevron, slash, arrow, dot | `.ui-breadcrumbs-separator-chevron`, `-slash`, `-arrow`, `-dot` |
| Collapsed levels | Off, on | —, `.ui-breadcrumbs-more` |
| Narrow container | Path, back link | `.ui-breadcrumbs-back-on-narrow` + container query |

### States

| State | Values | CSS class or attribute |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Current level | The last level (the current page) | `.ui-breadcrumbs-current` |

### Styling contract

`breadcrumbs.css` has three parts, marked in the stylesheet. Restyle by writing the same selector with a new value in your own stylesheet, inside `@layer overrides` (preferred: library updates keep your changes), or by changing a value in your copy of the stylesheet. After each token come the parts it styles, named by their class without `ui-breadcrumbs-` (as in Structure), with the option or state in brackets (joined by “+” when they apply together). Text uses the typography roles of `design-system.css`.

**1. Appearance — change freely** (colours, type, borders, corners, motion: only the look changes)

- Colours
  - `--c-muted`: item (also separator chevron), text
  - `--c-accent`: link, back
  - `--c-text`: current, sibling
  - `--c-border`: siblings
  - `--c-surface`: siblings
  - `--c-surface-hover`: sibling (hover)
  - `--c-selected`: sibling (current)
- Typography
  - `--font-ui`: breadcrumbs
  - `--fw-ui`: breadcrumbs
  - `--fs-label`: breadcrumbs
  - `--fw-ui-strong`: item (separator dot), current, sibling (current)
- Borders and corners
  - `--border-thin`: item (separator chevron), siblings, back icon
  - `--radius-control-small`: link, sibling
  - `--border-thick`: link (hover)
  - `--radius-control`: siblings
- Shadows
  - `--shadow-md`: siblings
- Sizes
  - `--space-sm-1`: link, back

**2. Dimensions — change with care** (sizes and spacing: the component keeps working, its size changes)

- Spacing
  - `--gap-tight`: list, item, link, text, current, siblings, sibling, back
  - `--space-sm-2`: siblings
  - `--gap-inline-items`: sibling
- Sizes
  - `--space-sm-3`: item (separator chevron), back icon
  - `--size-md-2`: link, text, current
  - `--size-md-1`: siblings
  - `--size-md-3`: siblings

**3. Structure — don't change** (layout, behaviour, states, accessibility)

- Borders and corners
  - `--border-thin`: sibling (focus)
- States and motion
  - `--focus-outline`: link (focus), back (focus), sibling (focus)
  - `--focus-offset`: link (focus), back (focus)

## For AI-assisted development

### Instructions

- Read this README before writing code. Import only from `breadcrumbsIndex.js`.
- Use Breadcrumbs on pages below the top level of a hierarchy; do not use them as the main navigation or to show the browsing history.
- Pass the path from the top level to the current page; every level except the current one needs an `href`.
- Add `siblings` only to levels where users often move sideways (customers, projects, contracts), with a specific `siblingsLabel`; keep lists short (they are not searchable).
- In single-page applications, call `event.preventDefault()` in `onNavigate` and route yourself; call `update(items)` after each navigation.
- Give each breadcrumb trail a unique, DOM-safe `id` and call `destroy()` before rendering into the same container again.

### Safety

- Labels are displayed as text; do not pass HTML. Build `href`s from trusted routes only.
- Never remove `aria-current="page"` or the navigation label.

### Example prompts

```text
Add breadcrumbs above the contract page (Home › Customers › {customer} › Contracts › {contract}) with a house icon for Home, collapsing long paths, and a back link on phones.
```

## For developers

### Business analysis

> **Component**: the Breadcrumbs itself. **Consumer**: the developer who configures the Breadcrumbs in the application's code. **App**: the running application that uses the Breadcrumbs; it provides the data, performs the actions and stores the changes.

**Path**

- App provides the path from the top level to the current page. <!-- BA-01 -->
- Component displays each level above the current page as a link, and the current page in bold, not as a link. <!-- BA-02 -->
- Component displays a house icon for the first level (optional). <!-- BA-03 -->
- Consumer chooses the separator: a small chevron (default), "/", "›" or "·". <!-- BA-04 -->
- User clicks a level. <!-- BA-05 -->
  - Component opens the page, or reports it to the App when the App takes over navigation. <!-- BA-06 -->

**Long paths**

- Component shortens a long path to the first level, a "…" button and the last levels. <!-- BA-07 -->
  - User clicks "…". <!-- BA-08 -->
  - Component opens a menu with the hidden levels. <!-- BA-09 -->
- Component shortens long level names with "…". <!-- BA-10 -->
  - User hovers over a shortened name. <!-- BA-11 -->
  - Component displays the full name as a tooltip. <!-- BA-12 -->

**Siblings** (optional)

- App provides, per level, the other pages at the same place in the hierarchy. <!-- BA-13 -->
  - Component displays a small arrow button next to the level. <!-- BA-14 -->
  - User clicks the arrow. <!-- BA-15 -->
  - Component opens the list below the level, or above it near the edge of the window, with the level's own page highlighted. <!-- BA-16 -->

**Narrow screens**

- Component displays a single "Back to {parent}" link instead of the path when less than 30rem is available. <!-- BA-17 -->

**Search engines** (optional)

- Component adds the path as structured data, so search results show it instead of a plain address. <!-- BA-18 -->

**Tooltips**

- Consumer chooses how the full label of each level shows on hover and keyboard focus: the browser's tooltip, a Tooltip or none (optional, on by default with the browser). <!-- BA-19 -->

### Contracts

**Contracts:** Styling: three parts (Styling contract) · Form field: no · Actions: no · Shared behaviour: yes, additions under Accessibility

### Public API

```js
import { renderBreadcrumbs, DEFAULT_BREADCRUMBS_CONFIG, BREADCRUMBS_TOOLTIP_MODES, BREADCRUMBS_SEPARATORS } from './breadcrumbsIndex.js';

const breadcrumbs = renderBreadcrumbs(container, config, onNavigate); // null after a developer error
```

| Member | Returns | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | The configured id. |
| `getItems()` | array | Copy of the current path. |
| `update(items)` | — | Replaces the path (e.g. after navigation in a single-page application). |
| `destroy()` | — | Removes listeners and the ActionMenu, clears the container. |

### Configuration

| Parameter | Type | Default | Allowed values / format | Applies when | Usage / description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | — | Starts with a letter; letters, digits, `_ : . -`; unique in the document | Always | Required. Id of the `<nav>`. |
| `items` | array | `[]` | `{ label, href?, icon?, siblings?, siblingsLabel? }` | Always | Required. Top level first, current page last; levels without `href` are text (`LINK_MISSING`). `siblings` = `[{ label, href }]` (pages at the same level, the level itself included and highlighted); `siblingsLabel` names the arrow button (e.g. "Other customers"). |
| `maxItems` | number | `5` | `0` (never collapse) or integer ≥ 3 | Always | Beyond this number, the middle levels go into the "…" menu (first level and last `maxItems - 2` levels stay). |
| `separator` | string | `'CHEVRON'` | `CHEVRON`, `SLASH` ("/"), `ARROW` ("›"), `DOT` ("·") | Always | Separator between levels; accepted case-insensitively. |
| `homeIcon` | boolean | `false` | — | Always | Shows the first level as a house icon (its label stays available to screen readers). |
| `showCurrent` | boolean | `true` | — | Always | Shows the current page as the last level. |
| `backLinkOnNarrow` | boolean | `true` | — | Always | Below 30rem, shows "Back to {parent}" instead of the path. |
| `structuredData` | boolean | `false` | — | Always | Adds the path for search engines (schema.org `BreadcrumbList` as JSON-LD, invisible to users); see Structured data. |
| `tooltipMode` | string | `'TITLE'` | `NONE`, `TITLE`, `TOOLTIP` | Always | How the full label of each level (`TOOLTIP`: only when it is cut off) shows on hover and keyboard focus: not at all, the browser's tooltip (`title`, mouse only) or a Tooltip (also on keyboard focus; needs `tooltip.css`, the Tooltip module is loaded only then). With `TOOLTIP` it also applies to the buttons that open the sibling lists and the "…" menu button; with `TITLE` or `NONE` they show nothing (as before). |
| `texts.navigation` / `more` / `back` / `siblings` | string | `'Breadcrumb'` / `'Show hidden levels'` / `'Back to {label}'` / `'Pages next to {label}'` | Text (`{label}` in `back` and `siblings`) | Always | Landmark name, "…" button name, back link, default name of sibling arrow buttons. |
| `onNavigate` | function | `null` | `(item, event, instance) => {}` | Always | Takes precedence over the third `renderBreadcrumbs()` argument. |

### Callbacks

| Callback | Arguments | Fires when | Does not fire when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `onNavigate` | `({ label, href, index, sibling? }, event, instance)` | A level link, the back link, a level in the "…" menu (`event` is `null` there, it navigates as a link), or a sibling (`sibling:true`, `index:null`); the sibling list then closes. | The current page or a level without link is clicked; opening or closing a sibling list. |

### Errors

Breadcrumbs has no user-facing errors. Developer errors prevent rendering; warnings are logged and rendering continues. Console format: `Breadcrumbs "id" [LABEL]: message`.

| Label | Severity | Cause |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CONTAINER_REQUIRED` | error | No container passed. |
| `ID_REQUIRED` | error | `id` is empty. |
| `UNSAFE_ID` | error | `id` is not DOM-safe. |
| `DUPLICATE_ID` | error | An element with the same id already exists in the document. |
| `ITEMS_REQUIRED` | error | No item with a label (also in `update()`, which then keeps the previous path). |
| `INVALID_ITEM` | warning | An item without label; dropped. |
| `LINK_MISSING` | warning | A level above the current page without `href`; shown as text. |
| `INVALID_SIBLING` | warning | A sibling without label or href; dropped. |
| `INVALID_OPTION` | warning | Invalid `maxItems` or `separator`; the default is used. |

### Accessibility

- A `<nav>` landmark named "Breadcrumb" containing an ordered list; the current page has `aria-current="page"`.
- Separators are CSS decorations and are not read (text separators have an empty alternative text); the home icon keeps its label as hidden text.
- The "…" button is an ActionMenu (menu button pattern) listing the hidden levels as links.
- Sibling arrows are Buttons with names ("Other customers") and `aria-expanded`/`aria-controls` (disclosure pattern, as navigation links rather than a command menu); opening focuses the level's own entry (`aria-current="true"`), Escape closes and returns focus, a click outside or leaving with Tab closes the list.
- Links and the back link have visible focus; truncated labels keep the full text as a tooltip.

### Structured data

With `structuredData:true` Breadcrumbs also writes the path in a format search engines read (schema.org `BreadcrumbList`, JSON-LD) into a hidden `<script type="application/ld+json">` next to the trail. Users never see it; search engines may show the path in their results instead of the page address.

How it is built:

- every level, including levels collapsed into "…";
- full addresses: relative links are completed from the current page address (`"orders"` on `https://shop.example.com/catalog/` → `https://shop.example.com/catalog/orders`);
- the current page (no link in the trail) uses the current page address;
- it is rewritten by `update()`.

Example — the configuration:

```js
renderBreadcrumbs(pathHost,{ id:'path', structuredData:true,
    items:[ { label:'Home', href:'/' }, { label:'Laptops', href:'/laptops' }, { label:'ThinkBook 14' } ] });
```

on `https://shop.example.com/laptops/thinkbook-14` produces:

```json
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "BreadcrumbList",
  "itemListElement": [
    { "@type": "ListItem", "position": 1, "name": "Home", "item": "https://shop.example.com/" },
    { "@type": "ListItem", "position": 2, "name": "Laptops", "item": "https://shop.example.com/laptops" },
    { "@type": "ListItem", "position": 3, "name": "ThinkBook 14", "item": "https://shop.example.com/laptops/thinkbook-14" }
  ]
}
```

Use it on public pages that search engines index (shops, documentation, public portals); it brings nothing on pages behind a login. Search engines also need the page itself to be crawlable; check the result with the search engine's rich-results test.

### Examples

```js
const breadcrumbs = renderBreadcrumbs(pathHost,
{
    id:'page-path', homeIcon:true,
    items:[ { label:'Home', href:'/' }, { label:'Customers', href:'/customers' }, { label:customer.name, href:`/customers/${customer.id}` }, { label:'Contracts' } ]
},( item, event ) => { event?.preventDefault(); router.go(item.href); });

// After the router moved on:
breadcrumbs.update(newPath);
```

### Files

| File | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `breadcrumbsIndex.js` | Public entry point; the only import surface. |
| `breadcrumbsConfig.js` | Defaults, item normalization, developer validation. |
| `breadcrumbsComponent.js` | Drawing, collapse with ActionMenu, navigation reports, update. |
| `breadcrumbsHTML.js` | Navigation, list, collapse calculation and back link markup. |
| `breadcrumbsErrors.js` | Developer error and warning catalog. |
| `breadcrumbs.css` | Presentation. |
| `breadcrumbsTESTS.md` | Test plan: the cases that prove this README (automatic ones in `tests/components/breadcrumbs.test.mjs`). |


<!-- ===== source/components-js/button/buttonREADME.md ===== -->

# Button

## For business

### Overview

Button lets a user start an action, such as saving, submitting a form or opening a dialog. It is shown either with a text label (optionally with icons) or as a compact icon-only button. With an address (`href`) it becomes a link that can look like a button or like a text link, and keeps every browser link feature, such as "Open in a new tab".

### When to use

- Use it for actions the user starts: save, submit, open a dialog.
- Use ActionMenu when there are more actions than room on the screen.
- Give it an address (`href`) for moving to another page, e.g. a "README.md" link that looks like a button; a plain link inside text needs no component.
- Use CheckboxRadio (segmented look) or Toggle for choosing a state.

### Key features

- Three levels of emphasis show which action matters most: primary, secondary, tertiary; a fourth look, link, shows it as a text link.
- A link (`href`) that opens the page in the same tab or in a new tab, with "Open in a new tab" and "Copy link" always available.
- A text button with optional icons, or a compact icon-only button.
- Three sizes, three width behaviours and four corner styles.
- Unavailable state that the application switches on and off, e.g. while saving.
- A description for screen readers when the text alone is ambiguous, e.g. "Edit, Order 1042".

### Dependencies

| Dependency | Needed when | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Design system (`design-system.css`) | Always | Colors, sizes, spacing and focus style. |
| Button styles (`button.css`) | Always | Button appearance. |
| Font Awesome icon library | Icons are used | Icon glyphs. Loaded by the application page. |
| Tooltip component and `tooltip.css` | `tooltipMode` `TOOLTIP` | The tooltip with the icon button's name (the Tooltip module is loaded only then). |

### Not included

The application decides what the action does, which emphasis level fits the screen, the wording of labels, and when a button is enabled or disabled.

## For designers

### Structure

```text
button#{id}.ui-button.ui-button-{variant}.ui-button-{hierarchy}.ui-button-size-{size}.{radius class}[.ui-button-width-{width}]
├── span.ui-button-icon.ui-button-icon-before.ui-button-icon-size-{iconSize}   (optional, text button)
│   └── i.{icon classes}
├── span.ui-button-label                                                      (text button)
├── span.ui-button-icon.ui-button-icon-after.ui-button-icon-size-{iconSize}    (optional, text button)
│   └── i.{icon classes}
├── span.ui-button-visually-hidden  " (opens in a new tab)"                    (link that opens in a new tab, text button)
└── span.ui-button-icon.ui-button-icon-only.ui-button-icon-size-{size}         (icon button only)
    └── i.{icon classes}
a#{id}.ui-button.….ui-button-as-link[href][target][rel][download]             (instead of button when href is set; same content)
span#{id}-description  hidden                                               (optional description, referenced by aria-describedby)
span.ui-tooltip-host → Tooltip                                              (tooltipMode TOOLTIP, icon button; [title] on the button with TITLE)
```

Icons are decorative (`aria-hidden="true"`). The minimum width is passed inline as the local property `--ui-button-min-width`. Disabled buttons use the native `disabled` attribute; a disabled link has no `href`, `role="link"` and `aria-disabled="true"`. A link that opens in a new tab gets the icon `ui-button-icon-new-tab` after its label, unless `iconAfter` is set.

### Visual options

| Option | Values | CSS class or attribute |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Variant | Text button, icon button | `ui-button-button`, `ui-button-icon-button` |
| Hierarchy | Primary, secondary, tertiary, link | `ui-button-primary`, `ui-button-secondary`, `ui-button-tertiary`, `ui-button-link` |
| Element | Button, link (`href`) | `button`, `a.ui-button-as-link` |
| Size | Small, medium, large | `ui-button-size-small`, `ui-button-size-medium`, `ui-button-size-large` |
| Icon size (text button) | Small, medium, large | `ui-button-icon-size-small`, `ui-button-icon-size-medium`, `ui-button-icon-size-large` |
| Width (text button) | Fit content, minimum width, full | `ui-button-width-fit-content`, `ui-button-width-min-width`, `ui-button-width-full` |
| Corner radius (text button) | None, small, medium, large | `ui-button-radius-none`, `ui-button-radius-small`, `ui-button-radius-medium`, `ui-button-radius-large` |
| Corner radius (icon button) | Circle, none, small, medium, large | `ui-button-icon-radius-circle`, `ui-button-icon-radius-none`, `ui-button-icon-radius-small`, `ui-button-icon-radius-medium`, `ui-button-icon-radius-large` |

An icon button's icon size always follows the button size. The link look takes the type and size of the text around it, so size and icon size have no effect on it.

### States

No states of its own.

### Styling contract

`button.css` has three parts, marked in the stylesheet. Restyle by writing the same selector with a new value in your own stylesheet, inside `@layer overrides` (preferred: library updates keep your changes), or by changing a value in your copy of the stylesheet. After each token come the parts it styles, named by their class without `ui-button-` (as in Structure), with the option or state in brackets (joined by “+” when they apply together). Text uses the typography roles of `design-system.css`; border sides are physical (top, right, bottom, left).

**1. Appearance — change freely** (colours, type, borders, corners, motion: only the look changes)

- Colours
  - `--c-accent`: button (primary, secondary, secondary + hover, secondary + pressed)
  - `--c-grey-95`: button (primary)
  - `--c-on-accent`: button (primary, primary + hover, primary + pressed)
  - `--c-accent-hover`: button (primary + hover, primary + pressed)
  - `--c-surface`: button (secondary)
  - `--c-surface-hover`: button (secondary + hover, secondary + pressed, tertiary + hover, tertiary + pressed)
  - `--c-text`: button (secondary + hover, secondary + pressed, tertiary, tertiary + hover, tertiary + pressed)
  - `--c-link`: button (link)
  - `--c-link-visited`: button (link + as link)
  - `--c-link-hover`: button (link + hover)
  - `--c-link-active`: button (link + pressed)
  - `--c-link-disabled`: button (link + disabled)
- Typography
  - `--font-ui`: button
  - `--lh-compact`: button, icon
  - `--fs-caption`: button (size small)
  - `--fs-label`: button (size medium)
  - `--fs-control`: button (size large)
  - `--fw-ui-strong`: button (primary, secondary, tertiary)
- Borders and corners
  - `--border-thin`: button (primary, secondary, tertiary)
  - `--radius-control-small`: button (radius small, icon radius small)
  - `--radius-control`: button (radius medium, icon radius medium)
  - `--radius-control-large`: button (radius large, icon radius large)
- States and motion
  - `--transition-1`: button
  - `--opacity-disabled`: button (primary + disabled, secondary + disabled, tertiary + disabled)
- Sizes
  - `--link-decoration`: label (link)
  - `--link-underline-thickness`: label (link)
  - `--link-underline-offset`: label (link)
  - `--link-decoration-hover`: label (link + hover, link + pressed)
  - `--link-underline-thickness-hover`: label (link + hover, link + pressed)

**2. Dimensions — change with care** (sizes and spacing: the component keeps working, its size changes)

- Spacing
  - `--gap-inline-items`: button (also size small, size large), icon (button + size small, button + size large)
  - `--gap-toolbar`: button (size small)
  - `--padding-card`: button (size medium)
  - `--padding-panel`: button (size large)
- Sizes
  - `--control-height`: button (size small, size medium, size large), icon (button + size small, button + size medium, button + size large)
  - `--icon-size-small`: icon (size small, icon button + size small)
  - `--icon-size-medium`: icon (size medium, icon button + size medium)
  - `--icon-size-large`: icon (size large, icon button + size large)
  - `--percentage-full`: button (width fit content, width min width, width full)

**3. Structure — don't change** (layout, behaviour, states, accessibility)

- States and motion
  - `--focus-outline`: button (focus)
  - `--focus-offset`: button (focus)
- Sizes
  - `--link-focus-outline`: button (link + focus)
  - `--link-focus-offset`: button (link + focus)

**Set by the component — don't change**

- Variables
  - `--ui-button-min-width`: minimum width (from `minWidth`, width `MIN_WIDTH`)

## For AI-assisted development

### Instructions

- Read this README before writing code. Import only from `buttonIndex.js`.
- Check whether the configuration already provides the requested behavior before adding code.
- Render every button through `renderButton()`; never write button markup, classes or styles by hand.
- When several buttons share the same text (e.g. "Edit" in every table row), give each a `description` naming its item; never change the visible text only for screen readers.
- Keep application logic in the click callback or the consuming code, never in Button files.
- Do not modify Button source for application-specific needs; propose a framework change only for a reusable missing capability.
- Use `buttonVariant:'ICON_BUTTON'` with a meaningful `ariaLabel` for icon-only actions.
- Use `buttonType:'SUBMIT'` or `'RESET'` only for real form actions; the default `BUTTON` never submits.
- For moving to another page use `href` (a real link), never `onClick` with `window.location`: only a link offers "Open in a new tab". Choose `target:'NEW_TAB'` only when the user must keep the current page.
- For many repeated buttons (table rows), prefer one centralized `onClick` passed to `renderButton()` over per-button callbacks.
- Give each button a unique `id` and call `destroy()` before rendering into the same container again.

### Safety

- Never remove or replace `ariaLabel` on icon buttons.
- Never simulate disabled state with CSS or by ignoring clicks; use `disabled` or `setDisabled()`.
- Never pass HTML in `label`; it is displayed as text.
- Never pass `javascript:`, `data:` or `vbscript:` addresses in `href`; they are refused (`UNSAFE_HREF`).

### Example prompts

```text
Add a primary "Save" Button and a tertiary "Cancel" Button to the form footer. Disable Save while the save request is running and re-enable it when the request finishes.
```

```text
Turn the "Guide" Button into a link to /guide that opens in a new tab, with the look of a text link.
```

```text
Add a small tertiary icon Button with a trash icon to every table row. Handle all delete clicks in one callback that reads the row from the button id.
```

## For developers

### Business analysis

> **Component**: the Button itself. **Consumer**: the developer who configures the Button in the application's code. **App**: the running application that uses the Button; it provides the data, performs the actions and stores the changes.

**Action**

- User clicks the button. <!-- BA-01 -->
  - Component reports the click to the App. <!-- BA-02 -->
  - App performs the action. <!-- BA-03 -->
- Component submits or resets the form it belongs to, when the Consumer chooses that type. <!-- BA-04 -->

- User clicks a link. <!-- BA-05 -->
  - Component reports the click to the App. <!-- BA-06 -->
  - Component opens the page at the address in the same tab or in a new tab, as the Consumer chooses. <!-- BA-07 -->
  - App decides to stay on the page and performs the action itself, e.g. its own page change (optional). <!-- BA-08 -->
- User presses Ctrl or Cmd while clicking a link, or selects "Open in a new tab" in the browser's menu. <!-- BA-09 -->
  - Component keeps the browser's behaviour and sends nothing to the App. <!-- BA-10 -->

**Look**

- Consumer chooses the emphasis: primary, secondary, tertiary or link. <!-- BA-11 -->
  - Component adapts the link look to the size of the text around it. <!-- BA-12 -->
- Consumer chooses a text button or an icon-only button. <!-- BA-13 -->
  - Component displays an icon before or after the text (optional). <!-- BA-14 -->
  - Component displays an icon-only button as a circle by default. <!-- BA-15 -->
- Consumer chooses one of three sizes, one of three width behaviours and one of four corner styles. <!-- BA-16 -->
- Consumer provides an address, so the button is a link (optional). <!-- BA-17 -->
  - Component displays an icon after the text of a link that opens in a new tab (optional). <!-- BA-18 -->
  - Component announces that the link opens in a new tab. <!-- BA-19 -->

**Availability**

- App disables and enables the button, e.g. while a save is in progress. <!-- BA-20 -->
  - Component keeps a disabled button visible and prevents clicking it. <!-- BA-21 -->
  - Component removes the address of a disabled link and keeps it visible. <!-- BA-22 -->

**Screen readers**

- Consumer provides a description that follows the name, e.g. "Edit, Order 1042" (optional). <!-- BA-23 -->
- App changes the description at any time. <!-- BA-24 -->

**Tooltips**

- Consumer chooses how an icon button shows its name on hover and keyboard focus: the browser's tooltip, a Tooltip or none (optional). <!-- BA-25 -->

### Contracts

**Contracts:** Styling: three parts (Styling contract) · Form field: no · Actions: no · Shared behaviour: yes, additions under Accessibility

### Public API

```js
import { renderButton, DEFAULT_BUTTON_CONFIG, BUTTON_VARIANTS, BUTTON_TYPES, BUTTON_HIERARCHIES, BUTTON_SIZES, BUTTON_WIDTHS, BUTTON_RADII, BUTTON_ICON_RADII, BUTTON_TOOLTIP_MODES, BUTTON_TARGETS } from './buttonIndex.js';

const instance = renderButton(container, config, onClick); // null after a developer error
```

`container` is a dedicated, consumer-owned element. Rendering replaces its content; `destroy()` clears it.

| Member | Returns | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | The configured id. |
| `getElement()` | HTMLButtonElement \| HTMLAnchorElement | The native button, or the `<a>` of a link, for integrations that need it (e.g. form APIs). |
| `isDisabled()` | boolean | Current disabled state. |
| `setDisabled(disabled)` | — | Enables or disables the button; a link loses or gets back its address. |
| `setDescription(description)` | — | Sets, changes or removes (`''`) the description read by screen readers after the name. |
| `destroy()` | — | Removes the listener and clears the container. |

### Configuration

Enumerated values are canonical UPPER_CASE and accepted case-insensitively (`'icon-button'` = `'ICON_BUTTON'`). An invalid value produces an `INVALID_OPTION` warning and the default is used.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Allowed values / format | Applies when | Usage / description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | — | Starts with a letter; letters, digits, `_ : . -`; unique in the document | Always | Required. Native `id` of the button. |
| `buttonVariant` | string | `'BUTTON'` | `BUTTON`, `ICON_BUTTON` | Always | Text button or icon-only button. |
| `buttonType` | string | `'BUTTON'` | `BUTTON`, `SUBMIT`, `RESET` | not `href` | Native `type`. A link ignores it (`OPTION_IGNORED`). |
| `hierarchy` | string | `'PRIMARY'` | `PRIMARY`, `SECONDARY`, `TERTIARY`, `LINK` | Always | Emphasis level. `LINK`: the look of a text link (link tokens), in the type and size of the text around it; works with and without `href`. |
| `size` | string | `'MEDIUM'` | `SMALL`, `MEDIUM`, `LARGE` | Always | Control height, padding and font size. No effect with `LINK` (`OPTION_IGNORED` when supplied). |
| `href` | string | `''` | URL or path | Always | Optional. Makes the button a link (`<a>`): the browser's "Open in a new tab", "Copy link" and Ctrl / Cmd + click work. `javascript:`, `data:` and `vbscript:` addresses are refused (`UNSAFE_HREF`; the link has no address). |
| `target` | string | `'SAME'` | `SAME`, `NEW_TAB` | `href` | Where the page opens on a plain click: the same tab, or a new tab (`target="_blank"`, `rel="noopener"`, hidden text `newTabText`). |
| `newTabIcon` | boolean | `true` | — | `href` + `NEW_TAB` | Shows the new-tab icon after the label of a text link. An `iconAfter` replaces it. |
| `newTabText` | string | `'(opens in a new tab)'` | Text | `href` + `NEW_TAB` | Hidden text read by screen readers after the name (added to `ariaLabel` for an icon link). |
| `download` | string \| boolean | `''` | File name, or `true` | `href` | Optional. The browser saves the file instead of opening it (`true`: with its own name). |
| `rel` | string | `''` | Link types, e.g. `'nofollow'` | `href` | Optional. Extra `rel` values; `NEW_TAB` always adds `noopener`. |
| `disabled` | boolean | `false` | — | Always | Initial native disabled state. |
| `onClick` | function | `null` | `(event, instance) => {}` | Always | Button-owned click callback; see Callbacks. |
| `label` | string | `''` | Text | `BUTTON` | Required for text buttons. |
| `iconBefore` | string | `''` | CSS class names | `BUTTON` | Icon before the label. |
| `iconAfter` | string | `''` | CSS class names | `BUTTON` | Icon after the label. |
| `iconSize` | string | value of `size` | `SMALL`, `MEDIUM`, `LARGE` | `BUTTON` | Size of the label icons. With `LINK` the icons take the text size. |
| `width` | string | `'FIT_CONTENT'` | `FIT_CONTENT`, `MIN_WIDTH`, `FULL` | `BUTTON` | Width behavior. |
| `minWidth` | number | `160` | Positive number (px) | `BUTTON` + `MIN_WIDTH` | Minimum width. |
| `radius` | string | `'NONE'` | `NONE`, `SMALL`, `MEDIUM`, `LARGE` | `BUTTON` | Corner radius. Square by default, so buttons read as actions next to rounded chips and tags. |
| `icon` | string | `''` | CSS class names | `ICON_BUTTON` | Required. The only visible content. |
| `ariaLabel` | string | `''` | Text | `ICON_BUTTON` | Required. Accessible name of the icon button. |
| `description` | string | `''` | Text | Always | Optional, per instance. Extra information read by screen readers after the button's name (e.g. "Order 1042" for one of several "Edit" buttons); not visible. |
| `iconButtonRadius` | string | `'CIRCLE'` | `CIRCLE`, `NONE`, `SMALL`, `MEDIUM`, `LARGE` (`'50%'` accepted as `CIRCLE`) | `ICON_BUTTON` | Corner radius of the icon button. |
| `tooltipMode` | string | `'NONE'` | `NONE`, `TITLE`, `TOOLTIP` | `ICON_BUTTON` | How the icon button shows its name (`ariaLabel`) on hover and keyboard focus: not at all, the browser's tooltip (`title`, mouse only) or a Tooltip (purpose `LABEL`; also on keyboard focus; needs `tooltip.css`, the Tooltip module is loaded only then). A text button ignores it (`OPTION_IGNORED` for `TITLE` or `TOOLTIP`). |

Options supplied for the other variant are ignored with an `OPTION_IGNORED` warning. Icon class names are limited to letters, digits, `_` and `-`; other tokens are removed with an `INVALID_ICON_CLASS` warning.

### Callbacks

| Callback | Arguments | Fires when | Does not fire when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `config.onClick` | `(event, instance)` | The enabled button is activated (click, tap, Enter, Space); a link on a plain click, tap or Enter, before the page opens. | The button is disabled. A link: Ctrl / Cmd / Shift / Alt + click, middle-click, the browser's menu, Space. |
| `renderButton(..., onClick)` | `(event, instance)` | Same as above, only when `config.onClick` is absent. | `config.onClick` is present, or the button is disabled. |

Exactly one callback runs per activation. Neither callback changes native `SUBMIT` or `RESET` behavior. For a link, the callback may call `event.preventDefault()` to stay on the page (e.g. an app router); otherwise the page opens as `target` says.

### Errors

Button has no user-facing errors. Developer errors prevent rendering (`renderButton()` returns `null`); warnings are logged and rendering continues. Console format: `Button "id" [LABEL]: message`.

| Label | Severity | Cause |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CONTAINER_REQUIRED` | error | No container passed to `renderButton()`. |
| `ID_REQUIRED` | error | `id` is empty. |
| `UNSAFE_ID` | error | `id` is not DOM-safe. |
| `DUPLICATE_ID` | error | An element with the same id already exists in the document. |
| `LABEL_REQUIRED` | error | Text button without `label`. |
| `ICON_REQUIRED` | error | Icon button without `icon`. |
| `ARIA_LABEL_REQUIRED` | error | Icon button without `ariaLabel`. |
| `INVALID_OPTION` | warning | Invalid enumerated value or `minWidth`; the default is used. |
| `INVALID_ICON_CLASS` | warning | Invalid class names removed from an icon option. |
| `OPTION_IGNORED` | warning | Option supplied for the other variant, a link option without `href`, `buttonType` with `href`, or `size` / `iconSize` with `LINK`. |
| `UNSAFE_HREF` | warning | `href` with a `javascript:`, `data:` or `vbscript:` address; the link has no address. |

### Accessibility

- Native `<button>`: keyboard activation, focus and form semantics come from the browser.
- Icon buttons require `ariaLabel`; icons are always `aria-hidden`.
- The visible text (or `ariaLabel`) stays the accessible name; `description` adds extra context through `aria-describedby`, read after the name, so the spoken name always matches what is seen (WCAG "label in name").
- Disabled uses native `disabled`, so the button is removed from the tab order and announced as unavailable.
- A link is a native `<a href>`: Enter opens it (Space does not, as for every link) and the browser's link commands stay available. A disabled link has no `href`, so it leaves the tab order; `role="link"` and `aria-disabled="true"` announce it as an unavailable link.
- A link that opens in a new tab says so: hidden text after the name (`newTabText`) and, for a text link, the new-tab icon.
- Focus is shown with `--focus-outline`.

### Examples

Disable a button while an asynchronous action runs:

```js
renderButton(footer,
{
    id:'save-profile',
    label:'Save',
    iconBefore:'fa-solid fa-floppy-disk',
    onClick:async ( event, instance ) =>
    {
        instance.setDisabled(true);
        try { await saveProfile(); }
        finally { instance.setDisabled(false); }
    }
});
```

A link that looks like a button, and one in the look of a text link that opens in a new tab:

```js
renderButton(readmeHost, { id:'readme-open', label:'buttonREADME.md', hierarchy:'SECONDARY', size:'SMALL', href:'#/component/button/readme' });
renderButton(guideHost, { id:'guide-open', label:'Style guide', hierarchy:'LINK', href:'https://example.com/guide', target:'NEW_TAB' });
```

One centralized handler for buttons repeated in table rows:

```js
const buttons = rows.map(row => renderButton(rowActionsHost(row),
    { id:`delete-${row.id}`, buttonVariant:'ICON_BUTTON', hierarchy:'TERTIARY', size:'SMALL', icon:'fa-solid fa-trash', ariaLabel:`Delete ${row.name}` },
    ( event, instance ) => deleteRow(instance.id.replace('delete-',''))));

// When the table is rebuilt:
buttons.forEach(button => button?.destroy());
```

### Files

| File | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `buttonIndex.js` | Public entry point; the only import surface. |
| `buttonConfig.js` | Defaults, allowed values, normalization, developer validation. |
| `buttonComponent.js` | Lifecycle and runtime API. |
| `buttonHTML.js` | Markup generation. |
| `buttonEvents.js` | Click listener registration (links: plain clicks only). |
| `buttonErrors.js` | Developer error and warning catalog. |
| `button.css` | Presentation. |
| `buttonTESTS.md` | Test plan: the cases that prove this README (automatic ones in `tests/components/button.test.mjs`). |


<!-- ===== source/components-js/calendar/calendarREADME.md ===== -->

# Calendar

## For business

### Overview

Calendar is the field for dates and times: a date, a time, a date with time, a month, a week, or a period from one date (or date and time) to another. By default it is a custom field where the user types the value part by part (like in Chrome) or picks it in a calendar that looks the same in every browser; the browser's own date fields remain available as an alternative.

### When to use

- Use it for dates, times, months, weeks and periods from one date to another.
- Use TextInput for free text and numbers.
- Use Select for a choice from a short list of named periods, e.g. "This quarter".

### Key features

- Dates, times, date with time, months, weeks, and from–to periods.
- Typing part by part, as in Chrome, or picking the value in a calendar that looks the same in every browser.
- European, US or ISO date formats, with 24-hour or AM/PM time.
- Highlighted and unavailable days (weekends, holidays), earliest and latest values, period lengths and time steps.
- Quick choices for periods, such as "Last 7 days", and "Today" and "Clear" buttons.
- Read-only display as exact or relative text ("3 hours ago"), with the same formatting available anywhere in the application.
- The browser's own date fields as an alternative.

### Dependencies

| Dependency | Needed when | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Design system (`design-system.css`) | Always | Colours (including the calendar tokens), spacing and typography. |
| Calendar styles (`calendar.css`) | Always | Fields and calendar. |
| Button component and `button.css` | Always | Calendar, navigation, Today/Now, Clear, Done and quick-range buttons. |
| Font Awesome icon library | Always | Calendar and arrow icons. Loaded by the application page. |
| Tooltip component and `tooltip.css` | `tooltipMode` `TOOLTIP` | Tooltips (the Tooltip module is loaded only then). |

### Not included

The application converts between time zones (Calendar works with local date and time as entered), provides the list of holidays, checks business rules such as bookings or availability, explains the asterisk and shows the form's error summary. Relative limits ("only future dates", "at least 18 years ago") are not part of this version.

## For designers

### Structure

```text
CUSTOM (default), single value
div.ui-calendar-wrapper.ui-calendar-width-{width}.ui-calendar-custom[.ui-calendar-invalid]
├── span.ui-calendar-label (+ span.ui-calendar-optional | span.ui-calendar-mandatory)
├── div.ui-calendar-row
│   └── div.ui-calendar-box  role="group"
│       ├── span.ui-calendar-segments
│       │   └── span.ui-calendar-segment[.ui-calendar-segment-empty] role="spinbutton"  + span.ui-calendar-separator
│       └── span.ui-calendar-button-host → Button (tertiary icon, calendar)
├── div.ui-calendar-popup  popover, role="dialog"
│   └── div.ui-calendar-body
│       ├── div.ui-calendar-header → Buttons: previous, zoom title, next
│       ├── table.ui-calendar-grid (days: th.ui-calendar-week-head "Week", th.ui-calendar-week-number, td.ui-calendar-day)
│       │   or table.ui-calendar-zoom-grid (months, years, decades: td.ui-calendar-zoom)
│       ├── div.ui-calendar-time > select.ui-calendar-time-select: hour + minute (+ AM/PM for US)   (TIME, DATETIME)
│       └── div.ui-calendar-footer → Buttons: Today/Now, Clear, Done
├── div.ui-calendar-help
└── div.ui-calendar-error                                                (hidden when there is no error)

Range: fieldset.ui-calendar-wrapper.ui-calendar-range > legend + div.ui-calendar-row
       (span.ui-calendar-part: span.ui-calendar-sublabel "From"/"To" + div.ui-calendar-box) ×2
       + div.ui-calendar-quick-ranges → Buttons

NATIVE: input.ui-calendar-field (browser picker and icon) + span.ui-calendar-actions → Buttons Today/Clear
VIEW:   p.ui-calendar-label + p.ui-calendar-view-value > time (+ span.ui-calendar-relative in BOTH)
```

The segmented field looks like the other inputs (accent border while a part is focused, error border when invalid, muted background when inactive); the focused part is shown with the selected colours. Day cells: `ui-calendar-selected` (accent background, bold), `ui-calendar-in-range` (soft background between From and To), `ui-calendar-today` (inset outline), `ui-calendar-outside` (other months, muted), `ui-calendar-highlight` (background from the group's token via `--ui-calendar-highlight-bg`) and `aria-disabled="true"` (reduced opacity, struck through). Selection and range styles take precedence over highlights. The dialog position is set by the component (`--ui-calendar-popup-top`, `--ui-calendar-popup-left`).

### Visual options

| Option | Values | CSS class or attribute |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Label position | Top, left | `ui-calendar-label-top`, `ui-calendar-label-start`, or `INHERIT` inside an element with `ui-labels-start` |
| Presentation | Custom, browser | `ui-calendar-custom`, `ui-calendar-native` |
| Range | Off, on | —, `ui-calendar-range` with two `.ui-calendar-box` |
| Width | Small, medium, large, full | `ui-calendar-width-small`, `-medium`, `-large`, `-full` |
| Date format (custom) | EU, US, ISO | order of `.ui-calendar-segment` parts and separators (`.`, `/`, `-`), AM/PM part for US times |
| Week numbers (custom) | Off, on (always for WEEK) | `th.ui-calendar-week-head`, `th.ui-calendar-week-number` |
| Highlighted days (custom) | Default weekend, custom groups | `.ui-calendar-highlight` + inline `--ui-calendar-highlight-bg` |
| Read-only display | Exact, relative, both | `time`, `time` with hidden exact text, `time` + `.ui-calendar-relative` |

### States

| State | Values | CSS class or attribute |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Zoom level (custom) | Days, months, years, decades | `table.ui-calendar-grid` or `table.ui-calendar-zoom-grid` |
| Day (custom) | Selected, in range, today, other month, unavailable | `.ui-calendar-selected`, `.ui-calendar-in-range`, `.ui-calendar-today`, `.ui-calendar-outside`, `[aria-disabled="true"]` |
| Error | Shown | `.ui-calendar-invalid`, `[aria-invalid="true"]`, visible `.ui-calendar-error` |

### Styling contract

`calendar.css` has three parts, marked in the stylesheet. Restyle by writing the same selector with a new value in your own stylesheet, inside `@layer overrides` (preferred: library updates keep your changes), or by changing a value in your copy of the stylesheet. After each token come the parts it styles, named by their class without `ui-calendar-` (as in Structure), with the option or state in brackets (joined by “+” when they apply together). Text uses the typography roles of `design-system.css`; border sides are physical (top, right, bottom, left).

The disabled rules use `:disabled`, so they also apply inside a disabled `fieldset`; the label and `*` of a disabled field use `--c-muted`.

**1. Appearance — change freely** (colours, type, borders, corners, motion: only the look changes)

- Colours
  - `--c-text`: label, view value, field, box, popup, time select
  - `--c-danger-text`: label (invalid), mandatory, error
  - `--c-muted`: optional, help, relative, sublabel, field (disabled), box (disabled), label (disabled), mandatory (disabled), segment (empty), separator, header cell, outside, week head, week number
  - `--c-border`: field, box, popup, time select
  - `--c-surface`: field, box, popup, time select
  - `--c-accent`: field (focus), box (focus), today
  - `--c-danger`: field (invalid), box (invalid)
  - `--c-surface-muted`: field (disabled), box (disabled)
  - `--calendar-selected-bg`: segment (focus), selected (also hover)
  - `--calendar-selected-color`: segment (focus, empty + focus), selected
  - `--calendar-day-hover-bg`: day (hover), zoom (hover)
  - `--calendar-range-bg`: in range
  - `--calendar-range-color`: in range
- Typography
  - `--font-ui`: calendar, popup, day, zoom, time select
  - `--fw-ui`: calendar, popup, day, zoom, time select, optional, week head, week number
  - `--fs-label`: label, help, error, sublabel, day, zoom
  - `--fw-ui-strong`: label, error, header cell, today, selected
  - `--lh-compact`: label
  - `--lh-body`: help, error
  - `--fs-control`: view value, field, box
  - `--fs-caption`: header cell, week head, week number
- Borders and corners
  - `--border-thin`: field, box, popup, today, time select
  - `--radius-control-small`: segment, day, zoom
  - `--radius-control`: popup
- Shadows
  - `--shadow-md`: popup
- States and motion
  - `--transition-1`: field, box
  - `--opacity-disabled`: day (disabled), zoom (disabled)

**2. Dimensions — change with care** (sizes and spacing: the component keeps working, its size changes)

- Spacing
  - `--gap-tight`: calendar, part, box, time, time select
  - `--gap-section`: calendar
  - `--gap-inline-items`: row, actions, quick ranges, footer, popup, body, header
  - `--padding-control`: field, box
  - `--space-sm-2`: box
  - `--space-sm-1`: segment, grid
  - `--gap-toolbar`: week head, week number, calendar (label on the left, label on the left + width small, label on the left + width medium, label on the left + width large)
- Sizes
  - `--control-height`: field, box, day, zoom, time select, label (label on the left)
  - `--percentage-s`: calendar (width small, label on the left + width small)
  - `--percentage-m`: calendar (width medium, label on the left + width medium)
  - `--percentage-l`: calendar (width large, label on the left + width large)
  - `--percentage-full`: calendar (width full, label on the left + width small, label on the left + width medium, label on the left + width large)
  - `--form-label-width`: calendar (label on the left, label on the left + width small, label on the left + width medium, label on the left + width large)

**3. Structure — don't change** (layout, behaviour, states, accessibility)

- Borders and corners
  - `--border-thin`: day (focus), zoom (focus)
- States and motion
  - `--focus-outline`: field (focus), day (focus), zoom (focus), time select (focus)
  - `--focus-offset`: field (focus), time select (focus)

**Set by the component — don't change**

- Variables
  - `--ui-calendar-highlight-bg`: background of a highlighted day (from `highlights`)
  - `--ui-calendar-popup-left`, `--ui-calendar-popup-top`: position of the calendar dialog (measured)

**Used by the code** (the component's code names these tokens; change the token to change the result)

- Tokens
  - `--calendar-weekend-bg`: default weekend highlight (`highlights`)
  - `--calendar-highlight-bg`: highlight group without its own `backgroundToken`

## For AI-assisted development

### Instructions

- Inside a Form, give the field a `name` (the key of its value) and leave `labelPosition` on `INHERIT`, so the Form (or a ContentGroup with the class `ui-labels-start`) decides label placement for all fields. Show server or cross-field messages with `setError(message)`; they clear when the user changes the value.
- Read this README before writing code. Import only from `calendarIndex.js`.
- Use Calendar for every date, time, month or week input and for from–to periods; never write date inputs, pickers, date parsing or date validation by hand.
- Values are ISO strings (`'2026-09-26'`, `'14:30'`, `'2026-09-26T14:30'`, `'2026-09'`, `'2026-W39'`, `''` when empty or incomplete); ranges are `{ from, to }`. Convert to other formats or time zones in the application.
- Keep the default `presentation:'CUSTOM'`; use `'NATIVE'` only when the browser's own fields are explicitly wanted. With `NATIVE`, `MONTH`/`WEEK` fail with `NATIVE_TYPE_UNSUPPORTED` in Firefox and Safari, and custom-only options are ignored with `NOT_SUPPORTED_NATIVE` — do not ignore these messages.
- Choose `dateFormat` (`EU`, `US`, `ISO`) for the audience and `locale` for month and weekday names.
- Pass public holidays as a highlight group (`{ dates:[ { date, label } ], backgroundToken }`) and, if they must not be chosen, also in `disabledDates`.
- Calendars are mandatory by default; set `mandatory:false` explicitly. On submit, call `validate()` and use `getError()`/`focus()` in the error summary.
- To show Calendar values as text elsewhere (table cells, detail pages, e-mails), use `formatCalendarValue(value, options)` instead of formatting dates by hand; pass the same `dateFormat`/`displayFormat` the application uses.
- Give each calendar a unique, DOM-safe `id` and call `destroy()` before rendering into the same container again.

### Safety

- Never pass literal colours; only design-token names (`backgroundToken`).
- Never remove the spin-button roles and labels of the segments, the grid roles, `aria-selected`, `aria-disabled`, `aria-current` or the dialog labelling.
- Never convert times between time zones inside the component; do it explicitly in the application.
- Holiday labels are displayed as text; do not pass HTML.

### Example prompts

```text
Add a mandatory Calendar "Delivery date" in European format where weekends and the public holidays of the year are unavailable and shaded, with a Today button and an asterisk, and validate it on submit.
```

```text
Add a "Period" date range in US format to the report filters with quick choices for the last 7 days, last month and last 3 months, at most one year long, and reload the report when both dates are set.
```

## For developers

### Business analysis

> **Component**: the Calendar itself. **Consumer**: the developer who configures the Calendar in the application's code. **App**: the running application that uses the Calendar; it provides the data, performs the actions and stores the changes.

**Values**

- Consumer chooses the kind of value: date, time, date and time, month, week, or a period of dates or of dates with times. <!-- BA-01 -->
  - Component displays a period as two fields, "From" and "To". <!-- BA-02 -->
- Consumer chooses the format: European "dd.mm.yyyy" with 24-hour time, US "mm/dd/yyyy" with AM/PM, or ISO "yyyy-mm-dd". <!-- BA-03 -->

**Typing**

- User types digits in a part of the field, e.g. the day. <!-- BA-04 -->
  - Component moves to the next part when the part is full. <!-- BA-05 -->
- User presses the up or down arrow in a part. <!-- BA-06 -->
  - Component changes the part by one step. <!-- BA-07 -->
- User presses Backspace in a part. <!-- BA-08 -->
  - Component clears the part. <!-- BA-09 -->
- User pastes a whole date. <!-- BA-10 -->
  - Component displays the date in all parts. <!-- BA-11 -->
- User leaves the field after typing, using the arrows or Backspace, or pasting. <!-- BA-42 -->
  - Component reports the new value to the App once, not after every key. <!-- BA-43 -->

**Calendar**

- User clicks the calendar button. <!-- BA-12 -->
  - Component opens the calendar at the current value, or at today. <!-- BA-13 -->
- User clicks the calendar's title. <!-- BA-14 -->
  - Component displays months, then years, then decades, for distant dates. <!-- BA-15 -->
- User selects a day. <!-- BA-16 -->
  - Component closes the calendar and displays the value in the field. <!-- BA-17 -->
- Component displays the first day of the week as Monday, or Sunday when the Consumer chooses it. <!-- BA-18 -->
- Component displays week numbers (optional). <!-- BA-19 -->
- Component displays the hour as a list of 00–23 for European and ISO formats, and as a list of 1–12 with AM/PM for the US format. <!-- BA-20 -->

**Days and limits**

- Component displays Saturday and Sunday shaded (optional, on by default). <!-- BA-21 -->
- Consumer provides highlighted days with a colour and a name, e.g. public holidays (optional). <!-- BA-22 -->
  - User hovers over a highlighted day. <!-- BA-23 -->
  - Component displays its name as a tooltip. <!-- BA-24 -->
- Consumer provides unavailable days (optional). <!-- BA-25 -->
  - Component prevents selecting them. <!-- BA-26 -->
- Consumer provides the earliest and the latest value, the minimum and maximum length of a period, and the time step, e.g. 15 minutes (optional). <!-- BA-27 -->

**Buttons**

- Consumer enables the "Today" (or "Now") and "Clear" buttons (optional). <!-- BA-28 -->
- Consumer enables quick choices for periods, counted from today: last or next 7 days, month, 3 months, 6 months, year (optional). <!-- BA-29 -->
  - User clicks a quick choice. <!-- BA-30 -->
  - Component displays the period in both fields. <!-- BA-31 -->

**Errors**

- Component checks the value: missing, invalid, too early or too late, unavailable day, period incomplete, in the wrong order, too short or too long. <!-- BA-32 -->
  - Component displays the matching error message. <!-- BA-33 -->

**Read-only display**

- Component displays the value short ("12 Aug 26") or long ("12 August 2026"). <!-- BA-34 -->
- Component displays the value as exact text, relative text ("3 hours ago", "in 2 weeks"), or both. <!-- BA-35 -->
- Consumer provides the moment that relative text starts from (default: now). <!-- BA-36 -->
- Consumer chooses the same formatting for other places, e.g. table cells, each place with its own format. <!-- BA-37 -->

**Browser alternative**

- Consumer chooses the browser's own date fields instead of the custom field (optional). <!-- BA-38 -->
  - Component displays the field without the custom features. <!-- BA-39 -->
  - Component displays month and week fields only in browsers that offer them (Chrome and Edge). <!-- BA-40 -->

**Tooltips**

- Consumer chooses how the exact date of a relative date and the names of highlighted days shows on hover and keyboard focus: the browser's tooltip, a Tooltip or none (optional, on by default with the browser). <!-- BA-41 -->

### Contracts

**Contracts:** Styling: three parts (Styling contract) · Form field: yes · Actions: no · Shared behaviour: yes, additions under Accessibility

### Public API

```js
import { renderCalendar, formatCalendarValue, DEFAULT_CALENDAR_CONFIG, CALENDAR_TOOLTIP_MODES, CALENDAR_TYPES, CALENDAR_PRESENTATIONS, CALENDAR_STATES, CALENDAR_WIDTHS, CALENDAR_DISPLAY_FORMATS, CALENDAR_DATE_FORMATS, CALENDAR_DISPLAY_MODES, CALENDAR_MANDATORY_INDICATORS, CALENDAR_QUICK_RANGES } from './calendarIndex.js';

const due = renderCalendar(container, config, onValueChange, onValidation); // null after a developer error
```

`container` is a dedicated, consumer-owned element. Rendering replaces its content; `destroy()` clears it. The configuration is immutable; `config.value` remains the initial value.

| Member | Returns | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | The configured id. |
| `name` | string | The configured `name` (the key of the value in a Form). |
| `getLabelPosition()` | `'TOP'` \| `'START'` | Effective label position (`INHERIT` resolved from the surroundings). |
| `getLabel()` | string | The visible label; Form prefixes error-summary entries with it. |
| `getMandatoryState()` | object | `{ mandatory, indicator }`; Form shows "* Required field" when an asterisk is shown. |
| `setError(message)` | `{ valid, errorLabel }` | Shows an external error (server or cross-field rule, label `EXTERNAL`) until the user changes the value or `clearError()` is called; own validation errors take precedence. |
| `clearError()` | — | Removes an external error; own validation errors stay. |
| `getValue()` | string \| `{ from, to }` | ISO value (`''` when empty or incomplete); ranges return a copy of `{ from, to }`. |
| `getError()` | object \| null | Copy of the current error `{ errorLabel, message, source, severity, visibility }`. |
| `setValue(value)` | `{ valid, errorLabel }` | Sets the value programmatically (invalid ISO values ignored with `INVALID_OPTION`); no dirty flag, no `onValueChange`. |
| `setValue(value, { quiet:true })` | object | Quiet variant used by Form's quiet reset: sets the value without validating, removes any shown error and the changed state. |
| `validate()` | `{ valid, errorLabel }` | Runs final validation, shows or clears the error. |
| `isDirty()` | boolean | Whether the user has changed the value. |
| `focus()` | boolean | Moves focus to the first segment (custom) or the first input (native). |
| `destroy()` | — | Closes the dialog, destroys the Buttons, removes listeners, clears the container. |

### formatCalendarValue()

A function (not an instance member) that formats a Calendar value as plain text anywhere, with the same rules as Calendar's read-only view. Options are given **per call**, so every place can use its own format (e.g. a table column's long view and its compact view).

```js
formatCalendarValue(value, options) // → string ('' for empty or invalid values)
```

| Option | Default | Allowed values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | `'DATE'` | `DATE`, `TIME`, `DATETIME`, `MONTH`, `WEEK` | Kind of value. |
| `displayFormat` | `'SHORT'` | `SHORT`, `LONG` | "12 Aug 26" or "12 August 2026". |
| `dateFormat` | `'EU'` | `EU`, `US`, `ISO` | Order of day and month, 24-hour or AM/PM time. |
| `displayMode` | `'EXACT'` | `EXACT`, `RELATIVE`, `BOTH` | Exact text, relative text ("3 days ago") or both ("12 Aug 26 (3 days ago)"). |
| `referenceTime` | now | ISO date-time or Date | Reference for relative text. |
| `locale` | page language | BCP 47 tag | Month names and relative wording, e.g. “3 mar. 26” in Romanian (`ro`). |
| `texts` | English | `{ weekShort, weekLong }` | Week templates ("W{week} {year}", "Week {week}, {year}"). |

`value` is an ISO string of the type, or `{ from, to }` for ranges ("1 Mar 26 – 15 Mar 26").

### Configuration

Enumerated values are canonical UPPER_CASE and accepted case-insensitively. An invalid value produces an `INVALID_OPTION` warning and the default is used.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Allowed values / format | Applies when | Usage / description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | — | Starts with a letter; letters, digits, `_ : . -`; unique in the document | Always | Required. Id of the field group (custom), the input (native) or the range fieldset. |
| `name` | string | value of `id` | Text | `NATIVE` | Native `name` (ranges: `{name}-from`, `{name}-to`). |
| `label` | string | — | Text | Always | Required. Label or range legend. |
| `help` | string | `''` | Text | `EDIT`, `INACTIVE` | Help text, linked through `aria-describedby`. |
| `type` | string | `'DATE'` | `DATE`, `TIME`, `DATETIME`, `MONTH`, `WEEK` | Always | Kind of value. |
| `presentation` | string | `'CUSTOM'` | `CUSTOM`, `NATIVE` | Always | Segmented field with own calendar, or browser fields. |
| `range` | boolean | `false` | — | `DATE`, `DATETIME` | "From" and "To" fields; value `{ from, to }`. |
| `dateFormat` | string | `'EU'` | `EU` (`dd.mm.yyyy`, 24 h), `US` (`mm/dd/yyyy`, AM/PM), `ISO` (`yyyy-mm-dd`) | Always | Order and separators of the parts, time style and displayed text (the editing order needs `CUSTOM`; the browser's own fields follow the browser). |
| `state` | string | `'EDIT'` | `EDIT`, `VIEW`, `INACTIVE`, `INVISIBLE` | Always | Display mode. |
| `width` | string | `'MEDIUM'` | `SMALL`, `MEDIUM`, `LARGE`, `FULL` | Always | Field width. |
| `value` | string \| object | `''` | ISO value of the type; `{ from, to }` for ranges | Always | Initial value; invalid values are ignored with a warning. |
| `minValue` / `maxValue` | string | `''` | ISO value of the type | Always | Earliest / latest allowed value (`MIN_VALUE`, `MAX_VALUE`); also disables days in the calendar. |
| `minRangeDays` / `maxRangeDays` | number \| null | `null` | Integer ≥ 1 | `range` | Minimum / maximum period length in days, both ends included. |
| `timeStep` | number | `1` | Integer 1–60 (minutes) | `TIME`, `DATETIME` | Minute steps of the calendar's time lists and native pickers. |
| `showToday` | boolean | `false` | — | Always | "Today" button ("Now" for `TIME`/`DATETIME`). |
| `showClear` | boolean | `false` | — | Always | "Clear" button. |
| `quickRanges` | array | `[]` | `LAST_7_DAYS`, `NEXT_7_DAYS`, `LAST_1_MONTH`, `NEXT_1_MONTH`, `LAST_3_MONTHS`, `NEXT_3_MONTHS`, `LAST_6_MONTHS`, `NEXT_6_MONTHS`, `LAST_1_YEAR`, `NEXT_1_YEAR` | `range` | Rolling quick choices from `referenceTime` (today included); `DATETIME` uses 00:00–23:59. |
| `firstDayOfWeek` | number | `1` | `0` (Sunday), `1` (Monday) | `CUSTOM`, not `WEEK` | First column of the calendar (a week always starts on Monday). |
| `showWeekNumbers` | boolean | `false` (always on for `WEEK`) | — | `CUSTOM` | "Week" column with ISO week numbers. |
| `highlights` | array | `[ { daysOfWeek:[6, 0], backgroundToken:'--calendar-weekend-bg' } ]` | `{ daysOfWeek?:[0–6], dates?:['YYYY-MM-DD' \| { date, label }], label?, backgroundToken? }` | `CUSTOM` | Emphasized days; the first matching group wins; labels become tooltips and part of the day's accessible name; `[]` removes all highlights. |
| `disabledDaysOfWeek` | array | `[]` | `0`–`6` (Sunday–Saturday) | `CUSTOM` | Unavailable weekdays (`DISABLED_DATE`). |
| `disabledDates` | array | `[]` | `'YYYY-MM-DD'` | `CUSTOM` | Unavailable days. |
| `displayFormat` | string | `'SHORT'` | `SHORT` ("12 Aug 26"), `LONG` ("12 August 2026") | Always | Text in the view state and error messages (order follows `dateFormat`). |
| `displayMode` | string | `'EXACT'` | `EXACT`, `RELATIVE`, `BOTH` | `VIEW` | Exact text, relative text ("3 hours ago") or both ("12 Aug 26 (3 hours ago)"). |
| `referenceTime` | string \| Date \| null | `null` (now) | ISO date-time or Date | Always | Reference for relative texts, quick ranges, "today" in the calendar, the "Today"/"Now" button and arrow-key defaults. |
| `locale` | string | page language | BCP 47 tag, e.g. `'en-GB'`, `'ro'` | Always | Optional. The language of the month and weekday names and of the relative texts. When empty, the page language (`<html lang>`), then the browser language. For example: the 3rd of March is shown as “3 Mar 26” in English (`en-GB`) and “3 mar. 26” in Romanian (`ro`). The order of day, month and year comes from `dateFormat` and the first day of the week from `firstDayOfWeek`. |
| `mandatory` | boolean | `true` | — | Always | `true`: empty is `REQUIRED`; a half-filled range is `RANGE_INCOMPLETE` in any case. |
| `mandatoryIndicator` | string | `'NONE'` | `NONE`, `OPTIONAL_TEXT`, `MANDATORY_ASTERISK` | `label` | Marker next to the label. |
| `labelPosition` | string | `'INHERIT'` | `TOP`, `START`, `INHERIT` | Always | Label above the field (`TOP`), on its left (`START`), or as set by the surrounding Form/ContentGroup (`INHERIT`: left inside an element with the class `ui-labels-start`, otherwise on top). `START` needs a surrounding container at least 36rem wide (Form, ContentGroup, CollapsiblePanel, or any element with `container-type:inline-size`); narrower, the label moves on top. |
| `autoFocus` | boolean | `false` | — | `EDIT` | Focuses the first segment or input once, after the first render. |
| `tooltipMode` | string | `'TITLE'` | `NONE`, `TITLE`, `TOOLTIP` | Always | How the exact date of a relative date and the names of highlighted days shows on hover and keyboard focus: not at all, the browser's tooltip (`title`, mouse only) or a Tooltip (also on keyboard focus; needs `tooltip.css`, the Tooltip module is loaded only then). With `TOOLTIP` it also applies to the previous, next and calendar buttons; with `TITLE` or `NONE` they show nothing (as before). |
| `texts.*` | string | English defaults | Text | Always | Labels (`from`, `to`, `today`, `now`, `clear`, `done`, `openCalendar`, navigation names), segment names and placeholders (`day`, `month`, `year`, `hour`, `minute`, `period`, `week`, `placeholderDay` …), `weekShort`/`weekLong`, one text per quick range, and `errors.{LABEL}`. |

Custom-only options with `NATIVE` (`firstDayOfWeek`, `showWeekNumbers`, `highlights`, `disabledDaysOfWeek`, `disabledDates`, and `dateFormat` for editing) produce `NOT_SUPPORTED_NATIVE`; they are not applied (the view state still uses `dateFormat`). `range` for other types, range options without `range`, `timeStep` for types without time and a Sunday start for `WEEK` are ignored with `OPTION_IGNORED`.

### Keyboard (custom)

| Where | Keys |
| --- | --- |
| Segment | Digits (auto-advance), ↑/↓ change the part (starting from today when empty), Home/End minimum/maximum, Backspace/Delete empty the part, ←/→ and separator keys (`.` `/` `-` `:` `,` space) move between parts, Tab moves on, `a`/`p` set AM/PM, Ctrl/Cmd+V pastes a whole value, Alt+↓ opens the calendar. |
| Day grid | Arrows by day and week, Home/End start/end of week, Page Up/Down by month, Shift+Page Up/Down by year, Enter/Space choose, Escape closes. |
| Month / year / decade grid | Arrows by item (±4 vertically), Page Up/Down by year / decade / century, Enter/Space zoom in (or choose a month for `MONTH`), Escape closes. |

### Presentation support

| Feature | `CUSTOM` (default) | `NATIVE` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| DATE, TIME, DATETIME | Yes | All current browsers |
| MONTH, WEEK | Yes | Chrome and Edge only (`NATIVE_TYPE_UNSUPPORTED` elsewhere, not rendered) |
| Typing | Segmented, in `dateFormat` | Browser field, in the browser's language |
| Ranges | "From"/"To" fields, each with its calendar | "From"/"To" browser fields |
| Quick ranges, Today/Clear, limits, time steps | Yes | Yes |
| Zoom levels, week start, week numbers, highlights, unavailable days, own look | Yes | No (`NOT_SUPPORTED_NATIVE`) |

### Callbacks

| Callback | Arguments | Fires when | Does not fire when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `onValueChange` | `(value, instance)` | The effective value changes through the user. Typing, the arrows, Backspace and paste in the field (and the browser's own fields): once, when focus leaves the field, if the value differs from the last one reported. Picking in the calendar, time lists, Today/Clear, quick ranges: at once. | Each key while focus stays in the field (`getValue()` already returns the typed value), a value that ends as it was, `setValue()`, navigation and zooming in the calendar. |
| `onValidation` | `(result, instance)` with `result = { valid, errorLabel }` | The effective result changes; for typing in the field, when focus leaves it. | The result is unchanged; each key while focus stays in the field. |

### Errors

| Label | Default message | Trigger | Visibility |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `EXTERNAL` | Message passed to `setError()`. | `setError(message)`, e.g. from a Form (server errors, cross-field rules). | Corrective |
| `REQUIRED` | Enter a date. | Empty with `mandatory:true`. | Corrective |
| `INVALID_DATE` | Enter a valid date. | Incomplete or impossible value (partly filled parts, 31.02., unparseable native input). | Corrective |
| `MIN_VALUE` | Enter {minValue} or later. | Before `minValue`. | Corrective |
| `MAX_VALUE` | Enter {maxValue} or earlier. | After `maxValue`. | Corrective |
| `DISABLED_DATE` | This date is not available. | An unavailable day typed or set programmatically. | Corrective |
| `RANGE_INCOMPLETE` | Enter both dates. | Only one end of a range. | Corrective |
| `RANGE_ORDER` | The end must not be before the start. | `to` before `from`. | Corrective |
| `RANGE_TOO_SHORT` | Choose at least {minRangeDays} days. | Shorter than `minRangeDays`. | Corrective |
| `RANGE_TOO_LONG` | Choose at most {maxRangeDays} days. | Longer than `maxRangeDays`. | Corrective |
| `UNIDENTIFIED` | An unidentified error occurred. | Unknown error label. | Dismissible |

Errors are shown on `validate()`, `setValue()` and when the user leaves the component after changing it (or with incomplete input); they are updated while the user corrects them and are not announced by the field. Developer errors prevent rendering (`renderCalendar()` returns `null`); warnings are logged and rendering continues. Console format: `Calendar "id" [LABEL]: message`.

| Label | Severity | Cause |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CONTAINER_REQUIRED` | error | No container passed. |
| `ID_REQUIRED` | error | `id` is empty. |
| `UNSAFE_ID` | error | `id` is not DOM-safe. |
| `DUPLICATE_ID` | error | An element with the same id already exists in the document. |
| `LABEL_REQUIRED` | error | `label` is empty. |
| `NATIVE_TYPE_UNSUPPORTED` | error | `NATIVE` `MONTH`/`WEEK` in a browser without that picker; use `CUSTOM` or another type. |
| `INVALID_OPTION` | warning | Invalid enumerated value, number, ISO value, highlight group, token name, `referenceTime`, `locale` tag (the page language is used) or `setValue()` argument. |
| `OPTION_IGNORED` | warning | Option that does not apply to the type or range setting. |
| `NOT_SUPPORTED_NATIVE` | warning | Custom-only feature configured with `NATIVE`; not applied. |
| `UNKNOWN_QUICK_RANGE` | warning | Unknown quick-range key; dropped. |

### Accessibility

- Custom field: a `role="group"` named by the label (and "From"/"To"), whose parts are labelled spin buttons (`aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuetext`, min/max, `aria-required`, `aria-invalid`), so screen readers announce e.g. "Day, 12". The calendar button is a Button with a translated name ("Choose date").
- Calendar dialog: non-modal `role="dialog"` labelled by the field label; days, months, years and decades form a `role="grid"` with `aria-selected`, `aria-disabled`, `aria-current="date"` and a full date (plus highlight label) as each cell's name; weekday headers carry full names. Navigation and zoom controls are Buttons; the zoom title shows its purpose as a tooltip.
