- Unavailable days are shown by reduced opacity and strike-through and announced as unavailable; the selected day has colour plus bold text; highlight colours are complemented by labels.
- Native: real date/time inputs with `label for` (ranges: a fieldset with "From"/"To" labels).
- `RELATIVE` view keeps the exact date for screen readers (hidden text) and as a tooltip.
- Errors are linked through `aria-describedby` and `aria-invalid`; announcing them is the consumer's error summary's job.

### Examples

Delivery date without weekends and public holidays, validated on submit:

```js
const holidays = [ { date:'2026-12-25', label:'Christmas' }, { date:'2026-12-26', label:'Boxing Day' } ];

const delivery = renderCalendar(deliveryHost,
{
    id:'delivery-date', label:'Delivery date', locale:'en-GB',
    minValue:'2026-10-01', maxValue:'2026-12-31',
    disabledDaysOfWeek:[ 0, 6 ], disabledDates:holidays.map(holiday => holiday.date),
    highlights:[ { dates:holidays, backgroundToken:'--c-danger-soft' }, { daysOfWeek:[ 6, 0 ], backgroundToken:'--calendar-weekend-bg' } ],
    showToday:true, mandatoryIndicator:'MANDATORY_ASTERISK', texts:{ errors:{ REQUIRED:'Choose a delivery date.' } }
},( value ) => { order.deliveryDate = value; });

form.addEventListener('submit',event => { if ( !delivery.validate().valid ) { event.preventDefault(); showErrorSummary([ { message:delivery.getError().message, focus:delivery.focus } ]); } });
```

Report period in US format with quick choices, reloading the report when both dates are set:

```js
renderCalendar(periodHost,{ id:'report-period', label:'Period', range:true, dateFormat:'US', mandatory:false, maxRangeDays:366,
    quickRanges:[ 'LAST_7_DAYS', 'LAST_1_MONTH', 'LAST_3_MONTHS' ], showClear:true },
( { from, to } ) => { if ( from && to ) { loadReport(from,to); } });
```

Dates in a table column, long view and compact view (each with its own format):

```js
{ field:'date', label:'Date', type:'DATE', width:'M',
  format:value => formatCalendarValue(value,{ displayFormat:'LONG', dateFormat:'EU' }),
  compact:{ width:'S', format:value => formatCalendarValue(value,{ displayFormat:'SHORT', dateFormat:'EU' }) } }
```

Read-only "last login" as exact and relative text:

```js
renderCalendar(loginHost,{ id:'last-login', label:'Last login', type:'DATETIME', state:'VIEW', displayMode:'BOTH', value:user.lastLogin });
```

### Files

| File | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `calendarIndex.js` | Public entry point; the only import surface (`renderCalendar`, `formatCalendarValue`, constants). |
| `calendarConfig.js` | Defaults, allowed values, normalization (highlights, texts), native support detection, developer validation. |
| `calendarComponent.js` | Lifecycle, value and error lifecycle, segment editing, calendar dialog (zoom levels, keyboard, ranges, time), Button composition. |
| `calendarHTML.js` | Custom, native and view markup; dialog body builders. |
| `calendarEvents.js` | Native, custom and open-dialog listener registration. |
| `calendarState.js` | Per-instance runtime state. |
| `calendarValidation.js` | Validation rules (pure functions). |
| `calendarSegments.js` | Pure helpers: segment layouts per type and format, typing and stepping rules, conversion to and from ISO values, paste parsing. |
| `calendarDates.js` | Pure helpers: date arithmetic, ISO values and weeks, exact and relative formatting, quick ranges.; `formatCalendarValue()`. |
| `calendarErrors.js` | User error catalog and developer error and warning catalog. |
| `calendar.css` | Presentation. |
| `calendarTESTS.md` | Test plan: the cases that prove this README (automatic ones in `tests/components/calendar.test.mjs`). |


<!-- ===== source/components-js/checkboxRadio/checkboxRadioREADME.md ===== -->

# CheckboxRadio

## For business

### Overview

CheckboxRadio shows a fixed list of options from which the user picks exactly one (radio buttons) or any number (checkboxes). The same list can look like standard controls, like icons or like selectable chips.

### When to use

- Use it for a choice from a short, fixed list that stays visible: one option (radio buttons) or several (checkboxes).
- Use the segmented look for two to five short options that switch a view or a period, e.g. "List | Grid".
- Use Select when the list is long or space is short, and Toggle for a single on/off setting.

### Key features

- Single choice (radio buttons) or multiple choice (checkboxes).
- Four looks: standard controls, icons, chips or a segmented control.
- Options listed vertically or side by side.
- Options that start selected, unavailable options, and a whole list that is unavailable.

### Dependencies

| Dependency | Needed when | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Design system (`design-system.css`) | Always | Colors, spacing and typography. |
| CheckboxRadio styles (`checkboxRadio.css`) | Always | List appearance. |
| Chip component and `chip.css` | Chip look | Chip appearance. |
| Font Awesome icon library | Icon or chip look | Icon glyphs. Loaded by the application page. |

### Not included

The application provides the options, decides when the form is checked, stores the selection, applies business rules (e.g. "at least two topics"), explains the asterisk (e.g. "* Required field") and shows the form's error summary, which also announces errors to screen-reader users. Several checkboxes that must each be checked are separate lists.

## For designers

### Structure

```text
fieldset#{id}.ui-checkbox-radio.ui-checkbox-radio-{direction}.ui-checkbox-radio-presentation-{presentation}[.ui-checkbox-radio-invalid]
├── legend.ui-checkbox-radio-group-label                       (required when mandatory)
│   ├── span.ui-checkbox-radio-optional  or  span.ui-checkbox-radio-mandatory   (mandatory indicator)
│   └── span.ui-checkbox-radio-visually-hidden               (mandatory multiple choice: texts.mandatory)
├── div.ui-checkbox-radio-options
│   └── label.ui-checkbox-radio-option  data-selected         (one per option)
│       ├── input.ui-checkbox-radio-input  type=radio|checkbox (visually hidden for icon, chip and segmented looks)
│       ├── span.ui-checkbox-radio-icon.ui-checkbox-radio-icon-size-{size} > i   (icon look)
│       ├── span.ui-checkbox-radio-option-label               (native, icon and segmented looks)
│       └── span.ui-checkbox-radio-chip → Chip                (chip look)
├── div.ui-checkbox-radio-help                                (optional)
└── div.ui-checkbox-radio-error                               (hidden when there is no error; not a live region)
```

The native input stays in every look; icon, chip and segmented visuals follow its checked state. In the segmented look a thin frame joins the options, the lines between them are the frame's background showing through a 1-line gap, and the selected segment has the accent fill, the on-accent text colour and a bold label; focus is drawn inside the segment. Disabled uses native `disabled` on the input or on the `fieldset`, shown with reduced opacity; selected and disabled are independent. Focus is drawn on the option for icon and chip looks. Selected chips use the `--c-selected` background and a check icon; unselected chips use `--c-surface`.

### Visual options

| Option | Values | CSS class or attribute |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Label position | Top, left | `ui-checkbox-radio-label-top`, `ui-checkbox-radio-label-start`, or `INHERIT` inside an element with `ui-labels-start` |
| Direction | Vertical, horizontal | `ui-checkbox-radio-vertical`, `ui-checkbox-radio-horizontal` |
| Look | Native, icon, chip, segmented | `ui-checkbox-radio-presentation-native`, `-icon`, `-chip`, `-segmented` (always with `ui-checkbox-radio-horizontal`) |
| Icon size | Small, medium, large | `ui-checkbox-radio-icon-size-small`, `-medium`, `-large` |
| Icon style (unselected → selected) | Regular → regular, regular → solid | `fa-regular` / `fa-solid` on `fa-circle` → `fa-circle-check` (single) or `fa-square` → `fa-square-check` (multiple) |
| Mandatory indicator | None, optional text, mandatory asterisk | no element, `span.ui-checkbox-radio-optional` (non-mandatory lists), `span.ui-checkbox-radio-mandatory` (mandatory lists, `aria-hidden`) |

### States

| State | Values | CSS class or attribute |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Validation error | Shown | `ui-checkbox-radio-invalid` |

### Styling contract

`checkboxRadio.css` has three parts, marked in the stylesheet. Restyle by writing the same selector with a new value in your own stylesheet, inside `@layer overrides` (preferred: library updates keep your changes), or by changing a value in your copy of the stylesheet. After each token come the parts it styles, named by their class without `ui-checkbox-radio-` (as in Structure), with the option or state in brackets (joined by “+” when they apply together). Text uses the typography roles of `design-system.css`; border sides are physical (top, right, bottom, left).

**1. Appearance — change freely** (colours, type, borders, corners, motion: only the look changes)

- Colours
  - `--c-text`: checkbox radio, option (presentation segmented)
  - `--c-muted`: optional, group label (disabled), mandatory (disabled), help
  - `--c-danger-text`: mandatory, group label (invalid), error
  - `--c-accent`: icon (presentation icon + checked), option (presentation segmented + checked)
  - `--c-border`: options (presentation segmented)
  - `--c-surface`: option (presentation segmented)
  - `--c-surface-hover`: option (presentation segmented + hover)
  - `--c-on-accent`: option (presentation segmented + checked)
- Typography
  - `--font-ui`: checkbox radio
  - `--fw-ui`: checkbox radio, optional
  - `--fs-label`: group label, help, error
  - `--fw-ui-strong`: group label, option label (presentation segmented + checked), error
  - `--lh-compact`: group label
  - `--lh-body`: help, error
- Borders and corners
  - `--radius-control`: option (presentation icon + focus), options (presentation segmented)
  - `--tag-radius`: option (presentation chip + focus)
  - `--border-thin`: options (presentation segmented)
- States and motion
  - `--opacity-disabled`: option (disabled)

**2. Dimensions — change with care** (sizes and spacing: the component keeps working, its size changes)

- Borders and corners
  - `--border-thin`: options (horizontal + presentation segmented)
- Spacing
  - `--gap-tight`: group label, options (vertical), help, error
  - `--gap-toolbar`: options (horizontal), option (presentation segmented)
  - `--gap-inline-items`: options (horizontal + presentation chip), option
- Sizes
  - `--control-height`: option (presentation segmented)
  - `--icon-size-small`: icon (size small)
  - `--icon-size-medium`: icon (size medium)
  - `--icon-size-large`: icon (size large)

**3. Structure — don't change** (layout, behaviour, states, accessibility)

- Borders and corners
  - `--border-thick`: option (presentation segmented + focus)
- States and motion
  - `--focus-outline`: option (presentation icon + focus, presentation chip + focus, presentation segmented + focus)
  - `--focus-offset`: option (presentation icon + focus, presentation chip + focus)
- Spacing
  - `--gap-toolbar`: checkbox radio (label on the left)
- Sizes
  - `--form-label-width`: checkbox radio (label on the left)

**Used by the code** (the component's code names these tokens; change the token to change the result)

- Tokens
  - `--c-selected`: chip look: background of a chosen option
  - `--c-surface`: chip look: background of the other options
  - `--c-text`: chip look: text

## For AI-assisted development

### Instructions

- Inside a Form, give the field a `name` (the key of its value) and leave `labelPosition` on `INHERIT`, so the Form (or a ContentGroup with the class `ui-labels-start`) decides label placement for all fields. Show server or cross-field messages with `setError(message)`; they clear when the user changes the value.
- Read this README before writing code. Import only from `checkboxRadioIndex.js`.
- Check whether the configuration already provides the requested behavior before adding code.
- Never write radio/checkbox markup, icon toggling, chip visuals or error display by hand; use `renderCheckboxRadio()`.
- The value is always an array, also for single choice: `[]` or `['value']`. Never convert it to a scalar inside the component.
- Lists are mandatory by default (at least one option selected) and then need `groupLabel`. Set `mandatory:false` explicitly, normally together with `mandatoryIndicator:'OPTIONAL_TEXT'`. Rules such as "at least two" belong to the consuming code; checkboxes that must each be checked go in separate lists.
- Use the same `mandatoryIndicator` for every input of a form, and add the asterisk explanation when using `MANDATORY_ASTERISK`.
- On submit, call `validate()`, add failed lists to the form's error summary (message from `getError()`) and let each summary link call `focus()`.
- Use `onValueChange` to observe the selection; do not use it for validation.
- Choose the icon look with `iconVariant`; there is no separate selected/unselected style option.
- Keep business logic in the consuming code; do not modify component source for application-specific needs.
- Give each list a unique `id` and call `destroy()` before rendering into the same container again.

### Safety

- Never remove the native inputs, `legend`, `aria-invalid` or `aria-describedby`; they provide semantics and keyboard support.
- Never make the error a live region (`role="alert"`, `aria-live`); announcing errors is the error summary's job.
- Never pass HTML in `label` or `groupLabel`; they are displayed as text.
- Without `groupLabel`, provide an accessible group name through the surrounding context (e.g. a labelled FieldGroup).

### Example prompts

```text
Add a mandatory single-choice "Payment method" with Card and Bank transfer as native radios, and a mandatory one-option checkbox "I accept the terms". Validate both on submit and list failures in the form's error summary.
```

```text
Show the newsletter topics News, Sports and Technology as horizontal chips with multiple choice, preselect News, and save the selected topics whenever the selection changes.
```

## For developers

### Business analysis

> **Component**: the CheckboxRadio itself. **Consumer**: the developer who configures the CheckboxRadio in the application's code. **App**: the running application that uses the CheckboxRadio; it provides the data, performs the actions and stores the changes.

**Choice**

- Consumer chooses single choice or multiple choice. <!-- BA-01 -->
- User clicks an option in a single-choice list. <!-- BA-02 -->
  - Component selects the option and clears the previous one. <!-- BA-03 -->
- User clicks an option in a multiple-choice list. <!-- BA-04 -->
  - Component selects or clears the option. <!-- BA-05 -->
- Component reports each change of the selection to the App. <!-- BA-06 -->

**Look**

- Consumer chooses one of four looks: standard controls, icons, chips or segmented. <!-- BA-07 -->
  - Component displays icons as circles for single choice and squares for multiple choice. <!-- BA-08 -->
  - Component displays a selected chip with a tinted background and a check mark. <!-- BA-09 -->
  - Component displays the segmented look as one row of joined buttons, the selected ones filled and in bold. <!-- BA-10 -->
- Consumer chooses the icon style, outline or filled when selected, and one of three icon sizes (icon look). <!-- BA-11 -->
- Consumer chooses a vertical list or options side by side (all looks except segmented). <!-- BA-12 -->
  - Component wraps side-by-side options when space runs out. <!-- BA-13 -->

**Options**

- Consumer provides the options and the options that start selected. <!-- BA-14 -->
- Consumer disables single options or the whole list (optional). <!-- BA-15 -->
  - Component keeps the selection of an unavailable option. <!-- BA-16 -->

**Required**

- Component checks that at least one option is selected in a required list. <!-- BA-17 -->
  - Component displays the group title in the error colour and the error message. <!-- BA-18 -->
  - Component clears the error when the user selects an option. <!-- BA-19 -->

### Contracts

**Contracts:** Styling: three parts (Styling contract) · Form field: yes · Actions: no · Shared behaviour: yes, additions under Accessibility

### Public API

```js
import { renderCheckboxRadio, DEFAULT_CHECKBOX_RADIO_CONFIG, CHECKBOX_RADIO_SELECTION_MODES, CHECKBOX_RADIO_PRESENTATIONS, CHECKBOX_RADIO_DIRECTIONS, CHECKBOX_RADIO_ICON_VARIANTS, CHECKBOX_RADIO_ICON_SIZES } from './checkboxRadioIndex.js';

const list = renderCheckboxRadio(container, config, onValueChange); // null after a developer error
```

`container` is a dedicated, consumer-owned element. Rendering replaces its content; `destroy()` clears it. No setters are provided: selection changes come from the user; for another configuration, destroy and render again.

| Member | Returns | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | The configured id. |
| `name` | string | The configured `name` (the key of the value in a Form). |
| `getLabelPosition()` | `'TOP'` \| `'START'` | Effective label position (`INHERIT` resolved from the surroundings). |
| `getLabel()` | string | The visible group label (`groupLabel`); Form prefixes error-summary entries with it. |
| `getMandatoryState()` | object | `{ mandatory, indicator }`; Form shows "* Required field" when an asterisk is shown. |
| `setError(message)` | `{ valid, errorLabel }` | Shows an external error (server or cross-field rule, label `EXTERNAL`) until the user changes the value or `clearError()` is called; own validation errors take precedence. |
| `clearError()` | — | Removes an external error; own validation errors stay. |
| `getValue()` | array | New array with the selected values, in option order. |
| `setValue(values, options?)` | object | Sets the selection programmatically (no `onValueChange`, not dirty) and returns `{ valid, errorLabel }`; `{ quiet:true }` (Form's quiet reset) skips validation and removes any shown error. |
| `isDirty()` | boolean | Whether the user has changed the selection. |
| `getError()` | object \| null | Copy of the current error `{ errorLabel, message, source, severity, visibility }`. |
| `validate()` | `{ valid, errorLabel }` | Runs the required-selection check, shows or clears the error. Always valid when `mandatory:false`. |
| `focus()` | boolean | Focuses the selected enabled option, else the first enabled one; `false` when all options are disabled. |
| `destroy()` | — | Removes the listener and clears the container. |

### Configuration

Enumerated values are canonical UPPER_CASE and accepted case-insensitively. An invalid value produces an `INVALID_OPTION` warning and the default is used.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Allowed values / format | Applies when | Usage / description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | — | Starts with a letter; letters, digits, `_ : . -`; unique in the document | Always | Required. `fieldset` id and prefix of internal ids. |
| `name` | string | value of `id` | Text | Always | Native `name` shared by all inputs. |
| `groupLabel` | string | `''` | Text | Always | Group title (`legend`). Required when `mandatory:true` (`GROUP_LABEL_REQUIRED`); otherwise missing gives a `GROUP_LABEL_MISSING` warning. |
| `help` | string | `''` | Text | Always | Help text below the options, linked to the group and every input through `aria-describedby`. |
| `selectionMode` | string | `'MULTIPLE'` | `SINGLE`, `MULTIPLE` | Always | `SINGLE`: radios; `MULTIPLE`: checkboxes. |
| `presentation` | string | `'NATIVE'` | `NATIVE`, `ICON`, `CHIP`, `SEGMENTED` | Always | Look; never changes values, validation or callbacks. `SEGMENTED`: one row of joined segments, for a few short options (it does not wrap). |
| `direction` | string | `'VERTICAL'` | `VERTICAL`, `HORIZONTAL` | Not `SEGMENTED` | Option arrangement (`SEGMENTED` is always one row). |
| `iconVariant` | string | `'REGULAR_REGULAR'` | `REGULAR_REGULAR`, `REGULAR_SOLID` | `ICON` | Icon style unselected → selected. |
| `iconSize` | string | `'MEDIUM'` | `SMALL`, `MEDIUM`, `LARGE` | `ICON` | Icon size (shared `--icon-size-*` tokens). |
| `options` | array | `[]` | Option objects (below) | Always | Required, at least one. |
| `options[].value` | string | — | Non-empty, unique | Always | Programmatic value. Duplicates are dropped (first kept) with a warning. |
| `options[].label` | string | — | Non-empty text | Always | Visible text and accessible name. |
| `options[].selected` | boolean | `false` | — | Always | Initial selection; at most one with `SINGLE`. |
| `options[].disabled` | boolean | `false` | — | Always | Option cannot be changed; keeps its selection. |
| `mandatory` | boolean | `true` | — | Always | `true`: at least one option must be selected. |
| `mandatoryIndicator` | string | `'NONE'` | `NONE`, `OPTIONAL_TEXT`, `MANDATORY_ASTERISK` | `groupLabel` | `OPTIONAL_TEXT`: `texts.optional` next to non-mandatory lists (recommended with `mandatory:false`). `MANDATORY_ASTERISK`: `*` next to mandatory lists. `NONE`: no marker. |
| `labelPosition` | string | `'INHERIT'` | `TOP`, `START`, `INHERIT` | Always | Label above the field (`TOP`), on its left (`START`), or as set by the surrounding Form/ContentGroup (`INHERIT`: left inside an element with the class `ui-labels-start`, otherwise on top). `START` needs a surrounding container at least 36rem wide (Form, ContentGroup, CollapsiblePanel, or any element with `container-type:inline-size`); narrower, the label moves on top. |
| `texts.optional` | string | `'(Optional)'` | Text | `mandatory:false` + `OPTIONAL_TEXT` | Optional marker. |
| `texts.mandatory` | string | `'Mandatory'` | Text | `mandatory` + `MULTIPLE` | Visually hidden text in the legend (checkbox groups cannot use `aria-required`). |
| `texts.requiredSelection` | string | `'Select an option.'` | Text | `mandatory:true` | Message of `REQUIRED_SELECTION`. |
| `disabled` | boolean | `false` | — | Always | Disables all options (native `fieldset[disabled]`). |

`iconVariant` / `iconSize` without `ICON`, and `direction` with `SEGMENTED`, are ignored with an `OPTION_IGNORED` warning.

### Callbacks

| Callback | Arguments | Fires when | Does not fire when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `onValueChange` | `(values, instance)`, `values` a new array | A user action changes the selection. | Initial render, `validate()`, `destroy()`, clicks on disabled options. |

It fires after the visuals are updated and a corrected error is cleared.

### Errors

| Label | Trigger | Visibility | Clearing |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `EXTERNAL` | `setError(message)`, e.g. from a Form (server errors, cross-field rules). | Corrective | A user change of the value, or `clearError()`. |
| `REQUIRED_SELECTION` | `mandatory:true` with `[]`, on `validate()` or when the user leaves the list after changing it | Corrective: group label in error color, message shown, inputs get `aria-invalid` | A successful validation, or any user selection while visible. |

The error never appears on render, on focus, or when the user tabs through without changing anything, and is not announced by the component. Developer errors prevent rendering (`renderCheckboxRadio()` returns `null`); warnings are logged and rendering continues. Console format: `CheckboxRadio "id" [LABEL]: message`.

| Label | Severity | Cause |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CONTAINER_REQUIRED` | error | No container passed. |
| `ID_REQUIRED` | error | `id` is empty. |
| `UNSAFE_ID` | error | `id` is not DOM-safe. |
| `DUPLICATE_ID` | error | An element with the same id already exists in the document. |
| `OPTIONS_REQUIRED` | error | No options. |
| `OPTION_VALUE_REQUIRED` | error | An option without `value`. |
| `OPTION_LABEL_REQUIRED` | error | An option without `label`. |
| `MULTIPLE_INITIAL_SELECTION` | error | More than one `selected:true` with `SINGLE`. |
| `GROUP_LABEL_REQUIRED` | error | `mandatory:true` without `groupLabel`. |
| `INVALID_OPTION` | warning | Invalid enumerated value; the default is used. |
| `DUPLICATE_OPTION_VALUE` | warning | Duplicate option value dropped. |
| `GROUP_LABEL_MISSING` | warning | `mandatory:false` without `groupLabel`. |
| `OPTION_IGNORED` | warning | `iconVariant` or `iconSize` without the icon look. |

### Accessibility

- Native radios and checkboxes in every look: keyboard behavior (Tab, arrow keys between radios, Space) and screen-reader semantics come from the browser.
- The group is a `fieldset` named by the `legend` (`aria-labelledby`); single choice uses `role="radiogroup"`. Mandatory status is announced by `aria-required="true"` (single choice) or by the visually hidden `texts.mandatory` in the legend (multiple choice); the asterisk is `aria-hidden`. Native `required` is not used.
- Each option is a `label` wrapping its input. Icons are `aria-hidden`; selection is shown by shape (check mark), not by color alone.
- The help text is linked to the group and every input through `aria-describedby`; a visible error is added to that reference and read when the user reaches the list; it is not a live region. The consumer's error summary announces errors and uses `focus()` to move the user to the list.

### Examples

Required payment method and terms acceptance, validated on submit and reported in the form's error summary (`showErrorSummary` is application code, see the TextInput README):

```js
const payment = renderCheckboxRadio(paymentHost,
{
    id:'payment-method',
    groupLabel:'Payment method',
    selectionMode:'SINGLE',
    mandatoryIndicator:'MANDATORY_ASTERISK',
    texts:{ requiredSelection:'Select a payment method.' },
    options:[ { value:'card', label:'Card' }, { value:'transfer', label:'Bank transfer' } ]
},( values ) => { order.paymentMethod = values[0] ?? null; });

const terms = renderCheckboxRadio(termsHost,
{
    id:'terms',
    groupLabel:'Terms and conditions',
    mandatoryIndicator:'MANDATORY_ASTERISK',
    texts:{ requiredSelection:'Accept the terms and conditions to continue.' },
    options:[ { value:'accepted', label:'I accept the terms and conditions' } ]
});

checkoutForm.addEventListener('submit',event =>
{
    const invalid = [ payment, terms ].filter(list => !list.validate().valid);
    if ( invalid.length ) { event.preventDefault(); showErrorSummary(invalid.map(list => ({ message:list.getError().message, focus:list.focus }))); }
});
```

### Files

| File | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `checkboxRadioIndex.js` | Public entry point; the only import surface. |
| `checkboxRadioConfig.js` | Defaults, allowed values, normalization, developer validation. |
| `checkboxRadioComponent.js` | Lifecycle, change coordination, validation display, runtime API. |
| `checkboxRadioHTML.js` | Markup, icon classes and Chip composition. |
| `checkboxRadioEvents.js` | Delegated change and focus-leave listeners. |
| `checkboxRadioState.js` | Per-instance selection and error. |
| `checkboxRadioValidation.js` | Required-selection rule. |
| `checkboxRadioErrors.js` | User error catalog and developer error and warning catalog. |
| `checkboxRadio.css` | Presentation. |
| `checkboxRadioTESTS.md` | Test plan: the cases that prove this README (automatic ones in `tests/components/checkboxRadio.test.mjs`). |


<!-- ===== source/components-js/chip/chipREADME.md ===== -->

# Chip

## For business

### Overview

Chip is a compact label for short information such as a status, a category, a count or an applied filter. It is either read-only or removable: a removable Chip shows a small "×" the user can activate to ask for its removal.

### When to use

- Use it for short information next to other content: a status, a category, a count or an applied filter.
- Use the removable Chip for filters and selections the user removes one by one.
- Use Button for actions and Badge for people or things with a picture.

### Key features

- Short text with an optional bold prefix ("Owner: John") and optional icons.
- Four status colours (success, warning, danger, info) or custom colours from the design system.
- Removable chips with a small "×".
- Long labels shortened with "…"; several chips wrap as a row.

### Dependencies

| Dependency | Needed when | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Design system (`design-system.css`) | Always | Colors, spacing and typography. |
| Chip styles (`chip.css`) | Always | Chip appearance. |
| Font Awesome icon library | Icons are used | Icon glyphs. Loaded by the application page. |

### Not included

The application owns the list of items, decides what a removal request means, removes the data, and chooses the colors that carry the right meaning.

## For designers

### Structure

```text
div.ui-chip-list                                   (only when a Chip list is rendered)
└── span.ui-chip.ui-chip-{type}[.ui-chip-bordered]
    ├── i.ui-chip-icon-before.{icon classes}       (optional, aria-hidden)
    ├── span.ui-chip-label
    │   └── b                                      (optional prefix)
    ├── i.ui-chip-icon-after.{icon classes}        (optional, aria-hidden)
    └── button.ui-chip-remove                      (removable only)
        └── span  "×"                              (aria-hidden)
```

Custom Chips receive their colors inline through the local properties `--ui-chip-custom-bg` and `--ui-chip-custom-color`; the text color is also used for the border.

### Visual options

| Option | Values | CSS class or attribute |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Type | Custom, success, warning, danger, info | `ui-chip-custom`, `ui-chip-success`, `ui-chip-warning`, `ui-chip-danger`, `ui-chip-info` |
| Border | On | `ui-chip-bordered` |
| Removable | On | adds `button.ui-chip-remove` |

### States

No states of its own.

### Styling contract

`chip.css` has three parts, marked in the stylesheet. Restyle by writing the same selector with a new value in your own stylesheet, inside `@layer overrides` (preferred: library updates keep your changes), or by changing a value in your copy of the stylesheet. After each token come the parts it styles, named by their class without `ui-chip-` (as in Structure), with the option or state in brackets (joined by “+” when they apply together). Text uses the typography roles of `design-system.css`; border sides are physical (top, right, bottom, left).

**1. Appearance — change freely** (colours, type, borders, corners, motion: only the look changes)

- Colours
  - `--c-surface-muted`: chip
  - `--c-text`: chip (also bordered)
  - `--c-success-soft`: chip (success)
  - `--c-success-text`: chip (success)
  - `--c-warning-soft`: chip (warning)
  - `--c-warning-text`: chip (warning)
  - `--c-danger-soft`: chip (danger)
  - `--c-danger-text`: chip (danger)
  - `--c-info-soft`: chip (info)
  - `--c-info-text`: chip (info)
  - `--c-success-border`: chip (bordered + success)
  - `--c-warning-border`: chip (bordered + warning)
  - `--c-danger-border`: chip (bordered + danger)
  - `--c-info-border`: chip (bordered + info)
- Typography
  - `--font-ui`: chip
  - `--fw-ui-emphasis`: bold text
  - `--fs-label`: remove
- Borders and corners
  - `--tag-radius`: chip, remove
- States and motion
  - `--opacity-muted`: remove
- Sizes
  - `--tag-border-width`: chip
  - `--tag-font-size`: chip
  - `--tag-font-weight`: chip
  - `--tag-line-height`: chip

**2. Dimensions — change with care** (sizes and spacing: the component keeps working, its size changes)

- Spacing
  - `--tag-gap`: list, chip
  - `--tag-padding-block`: chip
  - `--tag-padding-inline`: chip
  - `--space-sm-1`: chip
- Sizes
  - `--space-lg-1`: remove

**3. Structure — don't change** (layout, behaviour, states, accessibility)

- States and motion
  - `--focus-outline`: remove (focus)
  - `--focus-offset`: remove (focus)

**Set by the component — don't change**

- Variables
  - `--ui-chip-custom-bg`, `--ui-chip-custom-color`: colours of a `CUSTOM` chip (from `backgroundToken`, `colorToken`)

**Used by the code** (the component's code names these tokens; change the token to change the result)

- Tokens
  - `--c-surface-muted`, `--c-text`: default colours of a `CUSTOM` chip (`backgroundToken`, `colorToken`)

## For AI-assisted development

### Instructions

- Read this README before writing code. Import only from `chipIndex.js`.
- Check whether the configuration already provides the requested behavior before adding code.
- Never write Chip markup, classes or styles by hand; use `buildChip()`, `buildChips()` or `renderChips()`.
- Use `buildChip()` / `buildChips()` only for read-only Chips. Removable Chips need `renderChips()`, which registers the remove action.
- Chip only reports a removal request. Update the application data yourself and call `setChips()` with the new list.
- Keep application logic in the consuming code; do not modify Chip source for application-specific needs.
- Use a semantic type (`SUCCESS`, `WARNING`, `DANGER`, `INFO`) when the color carries meaning; use `CUSTOM` with design-system token names otherwise.
- Composite components pass Chip configurations to the Chip API and never reproduce Chip behavior.

### Safety

- Never pass literal colors (`#fff`, `rgb()`) as tokens; only design-system token names such as `--c-surface-muted`.
- Never pass HTML in `label` or `prefix`; they are displayed as text.
- Never remove the remove button's accessible name; provide `removeLabel` or a `texts.remove` template in the user's language.

### Example prompts

```text
Show the active filters above the table as removable Chips with the filter name as prefix. When a Chip is removed, clear that filter, reload the table and update the Chip list.
```

```text
Show the order status in the order header as a Chip: SUCCESS for "Delivered", WARNING for "Delayed", DANGER for "Cancelled".
```

## For developers

### Business analysis

> **Component**: the Chip itself. **Consumer**: the developer who configures the Chip in the application's code. **App**: the running application that uses the Chip; it provides the data, performs the actions and stores the changes.

**Content**

- Consumer provides the text, and a bold prefix (optional), e.g. "Owner: John". <!-- BA-01 -->
- Consumer provides an icon at the start, at the end, or both (optional). <!-- BA-02 -->
- Component shortens a long label with "…". <!-- BA-03 -->
- Component displays several chips as a wrapping row. <!-- BA-04 -->

**Look**

- Consumer chooses a status colour (success, warning, danger, info) or custom colours from the design system. <!-- BA-05 -->
- Consumer enables a border (optional). <!-- BA-06 -->

**Removal**

- Consumer enables removal (optional). <!-- BA-07 -->
  - Component displays a "×" after the text. <!-- BA-08 -->
- User clicks the "×". <!-- BA-09 -->
  - Component reports the removal request to the App. <!-- BA-10 -->
  - App decides whether the item is removed. <!-- BA-11 -->

### Contracts

**Contracts:** Styling: three parts (Styling contract) · Form field: no · Actions: no · Shared behaviour: yes, additions under Accessibility

### Public API

```js
import { buildChip, buildChips, renderChips, DEFAULT_CHIP_CONFIG, CHIP_TYPES } from './chipIndex.js';

const html = buildChip(config);                          // static markup, '' after a developer error
const listHtml = buildChips(configs);                    // static markup of several Chips
const list = renderChips(container, configs, onRemove);  // managed list, null after a developer error
```

`container` is a dedicated, consumer-owned element. Rendering replaces its content; `destroy()` clears it. Invalid Chips are omitted from collections; valid ones are still rendered.

| Member of `renderChips()` result | Returns | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `setChips(configs)` | — | Replaces the rendered collection. |
| `destroy()` | — | Removes the listener and clears the container. |

### Configuration

Enumerated values are canonical UPPER_CASE and accepted case-insensitively. An invalid value produces an `INVALID_OPTION` warning and the default is used.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Allowed values / format | Applies when | Usage / description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | `''` | Non-empty, unique within the list | `removable` | Required with `removable`: identifies the Chip in `onRemove`. |
| `label` | string | `''` | Text | Always | Required. Visible text. |
| `prefix` | string | `''` | Text | Always | Bold text before the label. |
| `type` | string | `'CUSTOM'` | `CUSTOM`, `SUCCESS`, `WARNING`, `DANGER`, `INFO` | Always | Color scheme. |
| `iconBefore` | string | `''` | CSS class names | Always | Decorative icon at the start. |
| `iconAfter` | string | `''` | CSS class names | Always | Decorative icon at the end, before the remove button. |
| `bordered` | boolean | `false` | — | Always | Shows a border in the text color. |
| `backgroundToken` | string | `'--c-surface-muted'` | Design-system token name | `CUSTOM` | Background color. |
| `colorToken` | string | `'--c-text'` | Design-system token name | `CUSTOM` | Text color; also the border color. |
| `removable` | boolean | `false` | — | Always | Adds the remove action. |
| `removeLabel` | string | `''` | Text | `removable` | Accessible name of the remove action; overrides `texts.remove`. |
| `texts.remove` | string | `'Remove {label}'` | Text with `{label}` (prefix + label) | `removable` | Default accessible name template. |
| `onRemove` | function | `null` | `(id, chipElement) => {}` | `removable` | Chip-owned removal callback; see Callbacks. |

Token options for non-`CUSTOM` types and remove options for non-removable Chips are ignored with an `OPTION_IGNORED` warning.

### Callbacks

| Callback | Arguments | Fires when | Does not fire when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `config.onRemove` | `(id, chipElement)` | The user activates the remove action of a Chip rendered by `renderChips()`. | The Chip was built with `buildChip()`/`buildChips()`. |
| `renderChips(..., onRemove)` | `(id, chipElement)` | Same as above, only when the Chip has no own `onRemove`. | The Chip has its own `onRemove`. |

Exactly one callback runs per request. Chip never removes itself; the consumer updates its data and calls `setChips()`.

### Errors

Chip has no user-facing errors. Developer errors omit the invalid Chip (or the whole list for `CONTAINER_REQUIRED` / `CONFIGS_NOT_ARRAY`); warnings are logged and rendering continues. Console format: `Chip "id or label" [LABEL]: message`.

| Label | Severity | Cause |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CONTAINER_REQUIRED` | error | No container passed to `renderChips()`. |
| `CONFIGS_NOT_ARRAY` | error | The Chip collection is not an array. |
| `LABEL_REQUIRED` | error | `label` is empty. |
| `ID_REQUIRED_WHEN_REMOVABLE` | error | Removable Chip without `id`. |
| `INVALID_BACKGROUND_TOKEN` | error | `backgroundToken` is not a token name (`CUSTOM`). |
| `INVALID_COLOR_TOKEN` | error | `colorToken` is not a token name (`CUSTOM`). |
| `DUPLICATE_ID` | error | Another Chip in the collection has the same id. |
| `INVALID_OPTION` | warning | Invalid `type`; `CUSTOM` is used. |
| `INVALID_ICON_CLASS` | warning | Invalid class names removed from `iconBefore` or `iconAfter`. |
| `OPTION_IGNORED` | warning | Token or remove options that do not apply; the removed `icon` option (use `iconBefore` or `iconAfter`). |

### Accessibility

- The remove action is a native `<button>` with an accessible name (`removeLabel` or `texts.remove`); the "×" glyph and both icons are `aria-hidden` (their meaning must be in the label).
- Status colors are paired with text; do not rely on color alone to convey meaning.
- The consumer provides the surrounding context (e.g. a heading "Active filters").

### Examples

Removable filter Chips kept in sync with application data:

```js
let filters = [ { key:'status', name:'Status', value:'Open' }, { key:'owner', name:'Owner', value:'John' } ];

const toChips = () => filters.map(filter => ({ id:filter.key, prefix:`${filter.name}:`, label:filter.value, removable:true, bordered:true }));

const chips = renderChips(filterBar,toChips(),( id ) =>
{
    filters = filters.filter(filter => filter.key !== id);
    reloadTable(filters);
    chips.setChips(toChips());
});
```

### Files

| File | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `chipIndex.js` | Public entry point; the only import surface. |
| `chipConfig.js` | Defaults, allowed values, normalization, developer validation, remove label. |
| `chipComponent.js` | Static builders, managed list lifecycle and runtime API. |
| `chipHTML.js` | Markup generation. |
| `chipEvents.js` | Delegated remove-action listener. |
| `chipErrors.js` | Developer error and warning catalog. |
| `chip.css` | Presentation. |
| `chipTESTS.md` | Test plan: the cases that prove this README (automatic ones in `tests/components/chip.test.mjs`). |


<!-- ===== source/components-js/collapsiblePanel/collapsiblePanelREADME.md ===== -->

# CollapsiblePanel

## For business

### Overview

CollapsiblePanel groups related content under a titled header that the user can open and close. When closed, it can show a short summary so the user still sees the essentials. The header can also carry status Chips and action Buttons.

### When to use

- Use it to group content under a title that the user opens and closes, with a short summary while closed.
- Use Accordion for several panels that work together, and ContentGroup when the content always stays visible.

### Key features

- A header with title, description, icon, status colour, labels and action buttons.
- A short summary of the content while the panel is closed.
- Three layouts: card, inline (separated by lines) and compact.
- Panels that start open or closed, that are always open, or that are temporarily locked.
- Content prepared only when the user first opens the panel.

### Dependencies

| Dependency | Needed when | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Design system (`design-system.css`) | Always | Colors, spacing, borders and typography. |
| Panel styles (`collapsiblePanel.css`) | Always | Panel appearance. |
| Chip component and `chip.css` | Header Chips are used | Header Chips. |
| Button component and `button.css` | Header actions are used | Header action Buttons. |
| Font Awesome icon library | Header icon is used | Icon glyph. Loaded by the application page. |
| Tooltip component and `tooltip.css` | `tooltipMode` `TOOLTIP` | Tooltips (the Tooltip module is loaded only then). |

### Not included

The application provides the content and the summary, decides the status and what header actions do, and validates the content.

## For designers

### Structure

```text
section#{id}.ui-collapsible-panel[.ui-collapsible-panel-{variant}][.ui-collapsible-panel-bordered][.ui-collapsible-panel-square]  data-state data-status data-show-summary-expanded
├── div.ui-collapsible-panel-header
│   ├── h2–h6.ui-collapsible-panel-heading-level     (only with headingLevel 2–6) around:
│   ├── button.ui-collapsible-panel-toggle          (collapsible)  or  div.ui-collapsible-panel-heading  (not collapsible)
│   │   ├── span.ui-collapsible-panel-chevron       (collapsible only)
│   │   ├── i.ui-collapsible-panel-icon.{icon}      (optional)
│   │   └── span.ui-collapsible-panel-titles
│   │       ├── span.ui-collapsible-panel-title
│   │       └── span.ui-collapsible-panel-description   (optional)
│   ├── div.ui-collapsible-panel-chips              (optional) → Chip list
│   └── div.ui-collapsible-panel-actions            (optional)
│       └── span.ui-collapsible-panel-action → Button   (one per action)
├── div.ui-collapsible-panel-summary
│   └── consumer summary  or  span.ui-collapsible-panel-summary-empty
└── div.ui-collapsible-panel-content                (role="region")
    └── div.ui-collapsible-panel-item               (one per content child)
        └── child component or static HTML
```

State and status are exposed as attributes: `data-state="EXPANDED|COLLAPSED"` hides the content when collapsed; `data-status` drives the side border; `data-show-summary-expanded="false"` hides the summary while expanded. A summary with nothing to show (no `summaryRenderer` and no `summaryEmptyText`, or a renderer returning empty or blank markup) is hidden (`hidden` attribute), so a collapsed panel shows no empty strip under the title. The header wraps below a panel width of `26rem` (container query `panel`). `ui-collapsible-panel-group` is an optional consumer wrapper that stacks several panels with consistent spacing. Chip and Button appearance is owned by those components.

### Visual options

| Option | Values | CSS class or attribute |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Variant | Default, inline, compact, plain | —, `ui-collapsible-panel-inline`, `ui-collapsible-panel-compact`, `ui-collapsible-panel-plain` |
| Summary while expanded | Hidden, shown | `data-show-summary-expanded="false"`, `"true"` |
| Border (default, compact) | Status edge only (default), thin border around | `ui-collapsible-panel-bordered` |
| Corners (default, compact) | Rounded (default), square | `ui-collapsible-panel-square` |

### States

| State | Values | CSS class or attribute |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Panel | Expanded, collapsed | `data-state="EXPANDED"`, `data-state="COLLAPSED"` |
| Status | Default, success, warning, error, incomplete | `data-status="DEFAULT"`, `"SUCCESS"`, `"WARNING"`, `"ERROR"`, `"INCOMPLETE"` |

### Styling contract

`collapsiblePanel.css` has three parts, marked in the stylesheet. Restyle by writing the same selector with a new value in your own stylesheet, inside `@layer overrides` (preferred: library updates keep your changes), or by changing a value in your copy of the stylesheet. After each token come the parts it styles, named by their class without `ui-collapsible-panel-` (as in Structure), with the option or state in brackets (joined by “+” when they apply together). Text uses the typography roles of `design-system.css`; border sides are physical (top, right, bottom, left).

**1. Appearance — change freely** (colours, type, borders, corners, motion: only the look changes)

- Colours
  - `--c-border`: collapsible panel (also bordered, status incomplete, inline), content
  - `--c-surface`: collapsible panel
  - `--c-success-border`: collapsible panel (status success)
  - `--c-success`: collapsible panel (status success)
  - `--c-warning-border`: collapsible panel (status warning)
  - `--c-warning`: collapsible panel (status warning)
  - `--c-danger-border`: collapsible panel (status error)
  - `--c-danger`: collapsible panel (status error)
  - `--c-grey-40`: collapsible panel (status incomplete)
  - `--c-text`: chevron
  - `--c-muted`: description, summary empty
- Typography
  - `--font-ui`: header, summary
  - `--fw-ui`: header, summary
  - `--fw-ui-medium`: title
  - `--fs-label`: description, summary
  - `--font-italic`: summary empty
- Borders and corners
  - `--radius-panel`: collapsible panel
  - `--border-thin`: collapsible panel (bordered, inline), content
  - `--radius-sm`: toggle (focus)
- Shadows
  - `--shadow-sm`: collapsible panel
- States and motion
  - `--opacity-disabled`: toggle (disabled)
  - `--transition-1`: chevron

**2. Dimensions — change with care** (sizes and spacing: the component keeps working, its size changes)

- Spacing
  - `--gap-inline-items`: header, toggle, heading, actions
  - `--padding-card`: header (also compact), summary (also compact), content (also compact)
  - `--padding-panel`: header, summary, content
  - `--space-sm-1`: titles
  - `--gap-tight`: chips, chip list, summary
  - `--space-sm-3`: header (compact), summary (compact)
  - `--gap-toolbar`: content (compact), collapsible panel (group)

**3. Structure — don't change** (layout, behaviour, states, accessibility)

- States and motion
  - `--focus-outline`: toggle (focus)
  - `--focus-offset`: toggle (focus)
- Sizes
  - `--percentage-full`: collapsible panel, chips (narrow), actions (narrow)

## For AI-assisted development

### Instructions

- Read this README before writing code. Import only from `collapsiblePanelIndex.js`.
- Check whether the configuration already provides the requested behavior before adding code.
- Never write panel markup, classes or styles by hand; use `renderCollapsiblePanel()`.
- Pass header Chips as configuration objects (`chips`, following the Chip README) and header buttons as actions (`actions` + `onAction`, the shared contract of guidelines §10.2); never create them yourself inside the header.
- Content is the third argument of `renderCollapsiblePanel()`: an ordered `children` array of static HTML strings or functions `(host, panel) => instance` that render a component (e.g. a ContentGroup) into `host` through its own public API. Use `lazyContent:true` when content is expensive.
- The panel never passes options down to content children; configure each child directly.
- Call `refreshSummary()` after the data shown in the summary changes; call `setStatus()` to reflect validation results.
- `onToggle` reports only user toggles; programmatic `expand()`, `collapse()` and `toggle()` do not call it.
- Keep validation and business logic in the consuming code; do not modify panel source for application-specific needs.
- Give each panel a unique, DOM-safe `id` and call `destroy()` before rendering into the same container again.

### Safety

- String children and `summaryRenderer` output are inserted as HTML. Escape any user-provided or external data first.
- Never remove `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls` or the content region's label.
- Do not use `disabled` to hide content; it only blocks user toggling.

### Example prompts

```text
Create one CollapsiblePanel per checkout step (Address, Delivery, Payment). Show a one-line summary of the entered data when a panel is closed and set the status to SUCCESS or ERROR after validating that step.
```

```text
Add a compact CollapsiblePanel "Advanced options" with an Edit button in the header. Load its content only when the user opens it for the first time.
```

## For developers

### Business analysis

> **Component**: the CollapsiblePanel itself. **Consumer**: the developer who configures the CollapsiblePanel in the application's code. **App**: the running application that uses the CollapsiblePanel; it provides the data, performs the actions and stores the changes.

**Opening and closing**

- User clicks the header. <!-- BA-01 -->
  - Component opens or closes the panel. <!-- BA-02 -->
  - Component reports the new state to the App. <!-- BA-03 -->
- Consumer chooses whether the panel starts open or closed. <!-- BA-04 -->
- Consumer chooses an always-open panel (optional). <!-- BA-05 -->
- App disables the header temporarily (optional). <!-- BA-06 -->
  - Component prevents opening and closing. <!-- BA-07 -->

**Header**

- Consumer provides the title, and a description and an icon (optional). <!-- BA-08 -->
- Component displays a coloured side border for the status: success, warning, error or incomplete. <!-- BA-09 -->
  - App changes the status at any time, e.g. after checking the content. <!-- BA-10 -->
- Consumer provides labels, e.g. "Draft", and action buttons, e.g. "Edit" (optional). <!-- BA-11 -->
  - User clicks an action button. <!-- BA-12 -->
  - Component reports the action to the App, without opening or closing the panel. <!-- BA-13 -->
- Component moves the labels and buttons below the title when the panel is narrow. <!-- BA-14 -->

**Summary** (optional)

- App provides a short summary of the content. <!-- BA-15 -->
  - Component displays it while the panel is closed, and also while it is open when the Consumer chooses it. <!-- BA-16 -->
  - Component displays a placeholder text when the summary is empty. <!-- BA-17 -->

**Layout**

- Consumer chooses the layout: card, inline or compact. <!-- BA-18 -->
  - Component displays the inline layout without a card, separated from the next panel by a line. <!-- BA-19 -->
- Consumer chooses a border and rounded or square corners for the card. <!-- BA-20 -->

**Content**

- Consumer provides the content: text or other components, e.g. groups of fields. <!-- BA-21 -->
- Component displays the content only after the user first opens the panel, which makes pages with many panels faster (optional). <!-- BA-22 -->

**Tooltips**

- Consumer chooses how icon-only actions show their names on hover and keyboard focus: the browser's tooltip, a Tooltip or none (optional). <!-- BA-23 -->

### Contracts

**Contracts:** Styling: three parts (Styling contract) · Form field: no (container: `getChildren()`) · Actions: yes (`actions`, `onAction`) · Shared behaviour: yes, additions under Accessibility

### Public API

```js
import { renderCollapsiblePanel, DEFAULT_COLLAPSIBLE_PANEL_CONFIG, COLLAPSIBLE_PANEL_TOOLTIP_MODES, COLLAPSIBLE_PANEL_STATES, COLLAPSIBLE_PANEL_STATUSES, COLLAPSIBLE_PANEL_VARIANTS, COLLAPSIBLE_PANEL_HEADING_LEVELS } from './collapsiblePanelIndex.js';

const panel = renderCollapsiblePanel(container, config, children); // null after a developer error
```

`container` is a dedicated, consumer-owned element. Rendering replaces its content; `destroy()` clears it. The panel imports no content component.

`children` (the panel content) is an ordered array; a single string is accepted as one child. Children are rendered once: on render, or on the first expansion with `lazyContent:true`.

| Child | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| string | Trusted static HTML inserted into its own item host. |
| function `(host, panel) => instance \| null` | Called once with an empty item host; renders anything into it. A returned object is kept and its `destroy()` is called when the panel is destroyed. |

| Member | Returns | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | The configured id. |
| `getState()` | string | `EXPANDED` or `COLLAPSED`. |
| `getStatus()` | string | Current status. |
| `expand()` / `collapse()` / `toggle()` | boolean | Changes the state; `false` when not collapsible or already in that state. Works even when `disabled`. |
| `setActionDisabled(key, disabled)` | boolean | Enables or disables a header action Button; `false` (with `UNKNOWN_ACTION`) for an unknown key. |
| `setStatus(status)` | boolean | Sets the status (case-insensitive); `false` and `INVALID_STATUS` warning for an invalid value. |
| `focus()` | boolean | Moves keyboard focus to the header toggle; `false` when the panel is not collapsible or is disabled (e.g. Accordion moves between headers with it). |
| `refreshSummary()` | — | Re-renders the summary (hidden while it is empty). |
| `getChildren()` | array | Copy of the content child instances returned by render functions (empty until first expanded with `lazyContent`); lets a Form find fields inside the panel. |
| `destroy()` | — | Removes the listener, destroys header Chips and Buttons and content children, clears the container. |

### Configuration

Enumerated values are canonical UPPER_CASE and accepted case-insensitively. An invalid value produces an `INVALID_OPTION` warning and the default is used.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Allowed values / format | Applies when | Usage / description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | — | Starts with a letter; letters, digits, `_ : . -`; unique in the document | Always | Required. Root element id and prefix of internal ids. |
| `title` | string | — | Text | Always | Required. Header title and name of the content region. |
| `description` | string | `''` | Text | Always | Secondary header text. |
| `icon` | string | `''` | CSS class names | Always | Decorative header icon. |
| `collapsible` | boolean | `true` | — | Always | `false`: always expanded, no toggle. |
| `state` | string | `'COLLAPSED'` | `EXPANDED`, `COLLAPSED` | `collapsible` | Initial state. Forced to `EXPANDED` when not collapsible. |
| `disabled` | boolean | `false` | — | `collapsible` | Blocks user toggling only. |
| `status` | string | `'DEFAULT'` | `DEFAULT`, `SUCCESS`, `WARNING`, `ERROR`, `INCOMPLETE` | Always | Initial status. |
| `variant` | string | `'DEFAULT'` | `DEFAULT`, `INLINE`, `COMPACT`, `PLAIN` (`''` = `DEFAULT`) | Always | Layout. `DEFAULT`: a card (surface, shadow, comfortable spacing). `PLAIN`: the default spacing without any frame, line, background or shadow, for a panel that sits inside a frame drawn by its container (e.g. Accordion's joined look); the status is not shown. `INLINE`: no card — no background, shadow, side spacing or side edges, only a line below; for lists of panels or panels inside another container. `COMPACT`: the card with smaller spacing, for dense layouts. |
| `bordered` | boolean | `false` | — | `DEFAULT`, `COMPACT` | `true`: a thin border around the card as well; `false`: only the thick status edge on the start side. |
| `cornerRadius` | string | `'ROUNDED'` | `NONE`, `ROUNDED` | `DEFAULT`, `COMPACT` | `ROUNDED`: corners with the `--radius-panel` token; `NONE`: square corners. |
| `chips` | array | `[]` | Chip configurations | Always | Rendered through the Chip API; Chip rules apply. |
| `actions` | array | `[]` | `{ key, label, icon?, iconOnly?, hierarchy?, disabled? }` | Always | Header buttons (guidelines §10.2), after the Chips; TERTIARY by default; `iconOnly` shows only the icon (the label is its name). Pressing one never opens or closes the panel. Without `onAction` they are disabled (`ACTION_HANDLER_MISSING`). The former `buttons` option is ignored (`OPTION_IGNORED`). |
| `tooltipMode` | string | `'NONE'` | `NONE`, `TITLE`, `TOOLTIP` | Always | How icon-only actions show their names on hover and keyboard focus: not at all, the browser's tooltip (`title`, mouse only) or a Tooltip (also on keyboard focus; needs `tooltip.css`, the Tooltip module is loaded only then). |
| `onAction` | function | `null` | `(key, instance) => {}` | `actions` | A header action Button was pressed. |
| `summaryRenderer` | function | `null` | `(instance) => string` | Always | Summary HTML (trusted); called on render, on every state change and on `refreshSummary()`. |
| `summaryEmptyText` | string | `''` | Text | not `summaryRenderer` | Placeholder summary text. |
| `showSummaryWhenExpanded` | boolean | `false` | — | Always | Keeps the summary visible while expanded. |
| `lazyContent` | boolean | `false` | — | `collapsible` | Renders the content children on the first expansion instead of on render. |
| `headingLevel` | number | `0` | `0`, `2`–`6` | Always | `2`–`6` wraps the header toggle (or the static heading) in `<h2>`…`<h6>`, so screen-reader users can list and jump between panel headers; it adds no look. `0`: no heading element. Choose the level that fits the page outline (e.g. `3` under an `h2`). An invalid value gives `INVALID_OPTION` and `0`. |
| `onToggle` | function | `null` | `(state, instance) => {}` | `collapsible` | See Callbacks. |

When `collapsible:false`, `state:'COLLAPSED'`, `disabled`, `lazyContent` and `onToggle` are ignored with an `OPTION_IGNORED` warning; with `variant:'INLINE'` or `'PLAIN'`, so are `bordered` and `cornerRadius`.

### Callbacks

| Callback | Arguments | Fires when | Does not fire when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `onToggle` | `(state, instance)` | The user successfully toggles the panel; `state` is the new state. | Programmatic `expand()`, `collapse()`, `toggle()`; disabled or non-collapsible panel. |
| `onAction` | `(key, instance)` | A header action Button is pressed. | Disabled actions; the panel is not opened or closed. |

Header Chip callbacks are defined in their own configurations.

### Errors

CollapsiblePanel has no user-facing errors. Developer errors prevent rendering (`renderCollapsiblePanel()` returns `null`); warnings are logged and rendering continues. Chip and Button report their own configuration errors. Console format: `CollapsiblePanel "id" [LABEL]: message`.

| Label | Severity | Cause |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CONTAINER_REQUIRED` | error | No container passed. |
| `ID_REQUIRED` | error | `id` is empty. |
| `UNSAFE_ID` | error | `id` is not DOM-safe. |
| `DUPLICATE_ID` | error | An element with the same id already exists in the document. |
| `TITLE_REQUIRED` | error | `title` is empty. |
| `INVALID_OPTION` | warning | Invalid enumerated value or `headingLevel`; the default is used. |
| `INVALID_ICON_CLASS` | warning | Invalid class names removed from `icon` or an action icon. |
| `INVALID_COLLECTION` | warning | `chips` is not an array; ignored. |
| `INVALID_ACTION` | warning | An action without key or label; dropped. |
| `DUPLICATE_ACTION_KEY` | warning | A duplicate action key; the later action is dropped. |
| `UNKNOWN_ACTION` | warning | `setActionDisabled()` names no action. |
| `ACTION_HANDLER_MISSING` | warning | Actions without `onAction`; their Buttons are rendered disabled. |
| `OPTION_IGNORED` | warning | Option that does not apply: to a non-collapsible panel, or `bordered`/`cornerRadius` with INLINE or PLAIN. |
| `INVALID_CHILD` | warning | A content child is neither a string nor a function; ignored. |
| `INVALID_STATUS` | warning | `setStatus()` received an invalid value; status unchanged. |

### Accessibility

- The toggle is a native `<button>` with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` pointing to the content. With `headingLevel`, it sits inside a heading (`<h2>`…`<h6>`), as in the WAI-ARIA accordion pattern; use it whenever panels are stacked or the title names a section of the page.
- The content is a `role="region"` labelled by the title; a non-collapsible panel uses a plain heading container.
- Chevron and icon are `aria-hidden`. Status is visual only; add a Chip or text when the status must be announced.
- The consumer ensures content and summary markup are accessible.

### Examples

Step panel with a ContentGroup as lazy content, a summary and validation status:

```js
const address = { street:'', city:'' };

const panel = renderCollapsiblePanel(stepHost,
{
    id:'step-address',
    title:'Delivery address',
    status:'INCOMPLETE',
    lazyContent:true,
    summaryRenderer:() => address.city ? `${escapeHTML(address.street)}, ${escapeHTML(address.city)}` : 'No address entered yet.', // escapeHTML: application helper
    actions:[ { key:'edit', label:'Edit', icon:'fa-solid fa-pen' } ],
    onAction:( key, panel ) => { if ( key === 'edit' ) { panel.expand(); } }
},[ host => renderContentGroup(host,{ id:'address-fields', label:'Address', direction:'HORIZONTAL' },
    [
        groupHost => renderTextInput(groupHost,{ id:'address-street', label:'Street' },( value ) => { address.street = value; }),
        groupHost => renderTextInput(groupHost,{ id:'address-city', label:'City' },( value ) => { address.city = value; })
    ]) ]);

function onAddressSaved( valid )
{
    panel.setStatus(valid ? 'SUCCESS' : 'ERROR');
    panel.refreshSummary();
    if ( valid ) { panel.collapse(); }
}
```

### Files

| File | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `collapsiblePanelIndex.js` | Public entry point; the only import surface. |
| `collapsiblePanelConfig.js` | Defaults, allowed values, normalization, developer validation. |
| `collapsiblePanelComponent.js` | Lifecycle, state transitions, Chip composition, action Buttons, content children, runtime API. |
| `collapsiblePanelHTML.js` | Panel shell (empty content region) and summary markup. |
| `collapsiblePanelEvents.js` | Toggle listener on the panel's own button. |
| `collapsiblePanelState.js` | Per-instance runtime state. |
| `collapsiblePanelErrors.js` | Developer error and warning catalog. |
| `collapsiblePanel.css` | Presentation. |
| `collapsiblePanelTESTS.md` | Test plan: the cases that prove this README (automatic ones in `tests/components/collapsiblePanel.test.mjs`). |


<!-- ===== source/components-js/contentGroup/contentGroupREADME.md ===== -->

# ContentGroup

## For business

### Overview

ContentGroup is a framed block that groups related content the user perceives as one unit: "Personal data", "Address", "Usage settings" or "Important information". It can hold static text, input fields, choice lists and other components, and looks the same whatever it contains.

### When to use

- Use it to frame related content that the user perceives as one unit: "Personal data", "Address", "Usage settings".
- Use CollapsiblePanel when the user opens and closes the content, and Accordion for several such sections.
- Use Form around groups of inputs that are submitted together.

### Key features

- A frame with an optional label in its top border, an optional title and description.
- Content stacked vertically or placed side by side, wrapping when space runs out.
- A whole group of inputs made unavailable at once.
- Groups nested inside groups, wider groups in multi-column layouts.

### Dependencies

| Dependency | Needed when | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Design system (`design-system.css`) | Always | Colors, spacing, borders and typography. |
| ContentGroup styles (`contentGroup.css`) | Always | Group appearance. |
| Styles of the components placed inside | When those components are used | Their own appearance; ContentGroup does not load them. |

### Not included

The application decides what goes into a group and in which order, and provides the multi-column layout a group can span. Validation, error summaries and submitting belong to the form, not to the group.

## For designers

### Structure

```text
fieldset#{id}.ui-content-group.ui-content-group-{direction}.ui-content-group-frame[.ui-content-group-bare]   (FIELDSET: content with inputs)
├── legend#{id}-label.ui-content-group-label                                          (optional; notches the border)
├── p#{id}-description.ui-content-group-description                                   (optional)
└── div.ui-content-group-content
    └── div.ui-content-group-item                                                     (one per child)
        └── child component or static HTML

section#{id}.ui-content-group…   (SECTION: static content)
└── fieldset.ui-content-group-frame  role="none"                                      (visual frame only)
    ├── legend#{id}-label.ui-content-group-label                                      (optional; notches the border)
    ├── h2…h6#{id}-title.ui-content-group-title                                       (optional)
    ├── p#{id}-description.ui-content-group-description                               (optional)
    └── div.ui-content-group-content > div.ui-content-group-item
```

Both semantics use the same frame: a `fieldset` whose `legend` notches the border natively, on any background; for `SECTION` the frame has `role="none"` and the outer `section` carries the semantics. The content area owns the gap between items; child components keep their own margins, so the visible spacing is gap plus child margin. Side by side, items share the row equally and wrap below `--size-md-1`; below a group width of `22rem` they stack. The local property `--ui-content-group-span` sets the number of parent-grid columns (ignored outside a grid). When disabled, inputs dim themselves; the group dims only its label and description.

### Visual options

| Option | Values | CSS class or attribute |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Semantic | Field group, section | `fieldset.ui-content-group-frame`, `section` > `fieldset.ui-content-group-frame[role="none"]` |
| Label (notch) | Present, absent | `legend.ui-content-group-label`, — |
| Title (section only) | Present, absent | `h2…h6.ui-content-group-title`, — |
| Direction | Vertical, horizontal | `ui-content-group-vertical`, `ui-content-group-horizontal` |
| Border | With, without | —, `ui-content-group-bare` |
| Grid span | 1–12 columns | `style="--ui-content-group-span:N"` |

### States

| State | Values | CSS class or attribute |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Disabled | On (field group only) | `fieldset[disabled]` |

### Styling contract

`contentGroup.css` has three parts, marked in the stylesheet. Restyle by writing the same selector with a new value in your own stylesheet, inside `@layer overrides` (preferred: library updates keep your changes), or by changing a value in your copy of the stylesheet. After each token come the parts it styles, named by their class without `ui-content-group-` (as in Structure), with the option or state in brackets (joined by “+” when they apply together). Text uses the typography roles of `design-system.css`; border sides are physical (top, right, bottom, left).

**1. Appearance — change freely** (colours, type, borders, corners, motion: only the look changes)

- Colours
  - `--c-border`: frame (also bare), content group (bare)
  - `--c-text`: label, title
  - `--c-muted`: description
- Typography
  - `--font-ui`: label, title, description
  - `--fs-label`: label
  - `--fw-ui-strong`: label, title
  - `--lh-compact`: label, title
  - `--fs-block-title`: title
  - `--fs-caption`: description
- Borders and corners
  - `--border-thin`: frame
  - `--radius-control`: frame
- States and motion
  - `--opacity-disabled`: label (disabled), description (disabled)

**2. Dimensions — change with care** (sizes and spacing: the component keeps working, its size changes)

- Spacing
  - `--space-lg-1`: content group, frame
  - `--gap-tight`: frame, content
  - `--space-sm-2`: label
  - `--gap-form-field`: content (horizontal)
- Sizes
  - `--size-md-1`: item (horizontal)

**3. Structure — don't change** (layout, behaviour, states, accessibility)

- Spacing
  - `--gap-tight`: content (horizontal + narrow)

**Set by the component — don't change**

- Variables
  - `--ui-content-group-span`: columns spanned in a parent grid (from `span`)

## For AI-assisted development

### Instructions

- Read this README before writing code. Import only from `contentGroupIndex.js`.
- Use ContentGroup for any group of related content; never write grouping markup (`fieldset`, `legend`, section headings) by hand.
- Choose `semantic:'FIELDSET'` when the group contains inputs (text may be mixed in) and `semantic:'SECTION'` for static content only.
- Name every group: `label` (border notch) for field groups; `label` and/or `title` (heading) for sections. `title` does not exist for field groups.
- Pass content as an ordered `children` array: static HTML strings, or functions `(host, group) => instance` that render a framework component into `host` through that component's own public API.
- Each child component is configured through its own README. ContentGroup never passes options down to children; configure every child directly.
- Do not wrap a single CheckboxRadio in a FIELDSET group; the list is already a named group.
- To put the labels of all fields in a group on the left, add the shared class `ui-labels-start` to the group's container element (fields with `labelPosition:'INHERIT'` follow it); inside a Form, use the Form's `labelPosition`.
- Keep business logic, validation and submitting in the consuming code; do not modify ContentGroup for application needs.
- Give each group a unique, DOM-safe `id` and call `destroy()` before rendering into the same container again; it also destroys the children.

### Safety

- String children are inserted as HTML: escape any user-provided or external data first.
- Never use `SECTION` for content with inputs, or `FIELDSET` for static text only; the announcement to screen-reader users would be wrong.
- Never add special handling for particular child component types in ContentGroup.

### Example prompts

```text
Build a registration form with three ContentGroups: "Personal data" with first name, last name and optional e-mail TextInputs; "Address" with street, number, postal code and town side by side, spanning two grid columns; and "Usage settings" with an explanatory sentence and two CheckboxRadio lists.
```

```text
Put a SECTION ContentGroup labelled "Notice" with the title "Important information" and a short delivery notice inside the checkout CollapsiblePanel, above the address group.
```

## For developers

### Business analysis

> **Component**: the ContentGroup itself. **Consumer**: the developer who configures the ContentGroup in the application's code. **App**: the running application that uses the ContentGroup; it provides the data, performs the actions and stores the changes.

**Frame**

- Consumer provides a label (optional). <!-- BA-01 -->
  - Component displays the label in a gap of the frame's top border. <!-- BA-02 -->
- Consumer provides a title for a group of static content (optional). <!-- BA-03 -->
- Consumer provides a description (optional). <!-- BA-04 -->
- Component displays the frame with or without a border. <!-- BA-05 -->

**Content**

- Consumer provides the content: static text, inputs, lists and other components. <!-- BA-06 -->
- Consumer chooses vertical or side-by-side content. <!-- BA-07 -->
  - Component wraps side-by-side content when space runs out. <!-- BA-08 -->
  - Component displays the content vertically in narrow places, such as sidebars or dialogs. <!-- BA-09 -->
- Consumer adds groups inside groups (optional). <!-- BA-10 -->
- Consumer chooses a width of two columns for a group in a multi-column layout (optional). <!-- BA-11 -->

**Availability**

- App disables the group. <!-- BA-12 -->
  - Component disables every input inside at once. <!-- BA-13 -->

**Screen readers**

- Component announces a group of inputs as one named group, e.g. "Address, group". <!-- BA-14 -->
- Component exposes a group of static text as a named section, reachable by heading navigation when it has a title. <!-- BA-15 -->

### Contracts

**Contracts:** Styling: three parts (Styling contract) · Form field: no (container: `getChildren()`) · Actions: no · Shared behaviour: yes, additions under Accessibility

### Public API

```js
import { renderContentGroup, DEFAULT_CONTENT_GROUP_CONFIG, CONTENT_GROUP_SEMANTICS, CONTENT_GROUP_DIRECTIONS } from './contentGroupIndex.js';

const group = renderContentGroup(container, config, children); // null after a developer error
```

`container` is a dedicated, consumer-owned element. Rendering replaces its content; `destroy()` clears it. ContentGroup imports no other framework component.

`children` is an ordered array (a single item is accepted as a one-item array). Each item is:

| Child | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| string | Trusted static HTML inserted into its own item host. |
| function `(host, group) => instance \| null` | Called once with an empty item host; renders anything into it. A returned object is kept as a child instance and its `destroy()` is called when the group is destroyed. |

| Member | Returns | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | The configured id. |
| `getChildren()` | array | Copy of the child instances returned by render functions, in order; lets a Form find fields inside the group. |
| `destroy()` | — | Destroys child instances, then clears the container. |

### Configuration

Enumerated values are canonical UPPER_CASE and accepted case-insensitively. An invalid value produces an `INVALID_OPTION` warning and the default is used.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Allowed values / format | Applies when | Usage / description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | — | Starts with a letter; letters, digits, `_ : . -`; unique in the document | Always | Required. Root id and prefix of internal ids. |
| `label` | string | `''` | Text | Always | Text in the border notch (`legend`). Names a `FIELDSET` group; names a `SECTION` when there is no title. Missing: `NAME_MISSING` warning when the group has no other name. |
| `title` | string | `''` | Text | `SECTION` | Heading inside the frame; names the section and makes it reachable through heading navigation. |
| `description` | string | `''` | Text | Always | Explanation below the label and title, linked through `aria-describedby`. |
| `semantic` | string | `'FIELDSET'` | `FIELDSET`, `SECTION` | Always | `FIELDSET`: content with inputs. `SECTION`: static content. |
| `headingLevel` | number | `3` | Integer 2–6 | `SECTION` + `title` | Heading level; choose it to keep the page outline correct. |
| `direction` | string | `'VERTICAL'` | `VERTICAL`, `HORIZONTAL` | Always | Item arrangement. |
| `span` | number | `1` | Integer 1–12 | Always | Parent-grid columns occupied, when the group is inside a parent grid. |
| `bordered` | boolean | `true` | — | Always | `false` removes border and padding. |
| `disabled` | boolean | `false` | — | `FIELDSET` | Disables every input inside (native `fieldset[disabled]`). |

`disabled` with `SECTION`, `title` with `FIELDSET` (use `label`) and `headingLevel` without a title are ignored with an `OPTION_IGNORED` warning.

### Errors

ContentGroup has no user-facing errors. Developer errors prevent rendering (`renderContentGroup()` returns `null`); warnings are logged and rendering continues. Children report their own errors. Console format: `ContentGroup "id" [LABEL]: message`.

| Label | Severity | Cause |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CONTAINER_REQUIRED` | error | No container passed. |
| `ID_REQUIRED` | error | `id` is empty. |
| `UNSAFE_ID` | error | `id` is not DOM-safe. |
| `DUPLICATE_ID` | error | An element with the same id already exists in the document. |
| `INVALID_OPTION` | warning | Invalid enumerated value, `headingLevel` or `span`; the default is used. |
| `OPTION_IGNORED` | warning | `disabled` with `SECTION`, `title` with `FIELDSET`, or `headingLevel` without a title. |
| `NAME_MISSING` | warning | A `FIELDSET` without `label`, or a `SECTION` without `label` and `title`: the group has no accessible name. |
| `INVALID_CHILD` | warning | A child is neither a string nor a function; ignored. |
| `FIELDSET_WITHOUT_CONTROLS` | warning | A `FIELDSET` group contains no `input`, `select` or `textarea` after rendering. |
| `REDUNDANT_GROUP` | warning | All inputs of a `FIELDSET` group are inside one nested `fieldset` (e.g. a single CheckboxRadio). |

The last two checks inspect native elements only, never other components' classes.

### Accessibility

- `FIELDSET`: native `fieldset` named by its `legend` (the label); `disabled` disables all inputs natively.
- `SECTION`: `section` labelled by its title (a real heading, in heading navigation) or, without a title, by its label; the inner frame is `role="none"`, so it adds no extra group.
- The description is linked with `aria-describedby`.
- The consumer chooses the right `semantic` and `headingLevel`, and makes the content itself accessible.

### Examples

Registration form sections with child components owned by the group:

```js
import { renderContentGroup } from './contentGroup/contentGroupIndex.js';
import { renderTextInput } from './textInput/textInputIndex.js';
import { renderCheckboxRadio } from './checkboxRadio/checkboxRadioIndex.js';

const address = renderContentGroup(addressHost,{ id:'address', label:'Address', direction:'HORIZONTAL', span:2 },
[
    host => renderTextInput(host,{ id:'street', label:'Street' }),
    host => renderTextInput(host,{ id:'number', label:'Number' }),
    host => renderTextInput(host,{ id:'postal-code', label:'Postal code' }),
    host => renderTextInput(host,{ id:'town', label:'Town' })
]);

const settings = renderContentGroup(settingsHost,{ id:'settings', label:'Usage settings' },
[
    '<p>Choose how we contact you.</p>',
    host => renderCheckboxRadio(host,{ id:'channels', groupLabel:'Channels', options:[ { value:'email', label:'Email' }, { value:'sms', label:'SMS' } ] }),
    host => renderCheckboxRadio(host,{ id:'frequency', groupLabel:'Frequency', selectionMode:'SINGLE', options:[ { value:'daily', label:'Daily' }, { value:'weekly', label:'Weekly' } ] })
]);

// Validate all inputs of the groups on submit (until a Form component exists):
const inputs = [ ...address.getChildren(), ...settings.getChildren() ];
const valid = inputs.map(input => input.validate()).every(result => result.valid);
```

A ContentGroup inside a CollapsiblePanel:

```js
renderCollapsiblePanel(panelHost,{ id:'step-address', title:'Delivery address', state:'EXPANDED' },
[
```
